headline: Commissioner reviews polio campaign, dengue surveillance
description: LAHORE - Commissioner Lahore Division Nauman Yousaf visited the Tehsil Headquarters (THQ) Hospital in Ghaziabad to review cleanliness, healthcare facilities
author: STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - Commissioner Lahore Division Nauman Yousaf visited the Tehsil Headquarters (THQ) Hospital in Ghaziabad to review cleanliness, healthcare facilities and the provision of free medicines to patients. During the visit, he checked the medicine store record and inspected different medicines to verify their expiry dates. He also reviewed the record of counters established for the ongoing anti-polio campaign and inspected fire hydrants at the hospital. The commissioner sought feedback from patients in the emergency department about the medical facilities being provided to them and pointed out the need to improve cleanliness in the passage surrounding the hospital. Later, Nauman Yousaf visited the Ghaziabad area to review the performance of anti-dengue field teams and their larva surveillance activities. He said November was a crucial month for dengue prevention and stressed that no negligence would be tolerated in surveillance activities. The commissioner appealed to citizens to cooperate with anti-dengue teams, which were visiting every household, and urged them to follow government guidelines and precautionary measures to protect themselves from dengue.

headline: 1,150 rural women secure jobs under Punjab’s ‘She Thread’ programme
description: LAHORE - As many as 1,150 rural women have completed textile-sector training and secured employment under the Punjab government’s ‘She
author: Staff Reporter
article_text: LAHORE - As many as 1,150 rural women have completed textile-sector training and secured employment under the Punjab government’s ‘She Thread’ programme, which aims to equip women with market-oriented skills and expand their employment opportunities in the industry. Chief Minister Punjab Maryam Nawaz Sharif has set a target of training 2,500 rural women under the initiative by June next year. Participants are also being provided a monthly stipend of Rs15,000 during the three-month training period. The Women Development Department has opened registration for women from rural areas of Lahore under the programme. Training is being imparted at Shahkam Industries on Multan Road, where participants are being prepared for employment as industrial sewing machine operators and apparel supervisors. The three-month course combines classroom instruction with hands-on training to equip participants with practical skills in line with the requirements of the textile industry. Women aged between 18 and 45, holding Punjab domicile and at least a matriculation qualification, are eligible to apply. Applicants can register at Shahkam Industries by submitting their national identity cards and domicile certificates. Selected candidates will also be required to submit an affidavit before admission following verification of their eligibility. Information about registration and eligibility criteria is also available through assistant commissioners, union council secretaries and relevant district offices. Maryam Nawaz said the initiative was aimed at providing rural women with industry-oriented skills to help them achieve financial independence and earn a respectable livelihood. She said the programme would not only equip women with skills according to market requirements but also facilitate their employment in the textile sector after completion of training.

headline: Lahore records hazardous air quality as AQI reaches 530
description: LAHORE - Smog continued to affect Lahore, with air pollution reaching hazardous levels in several parts of the provincial capital. The city recorded an overall
author: STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - Smog continued to affect Lahore, with air pollution reaching hazardous levels in several parts of the provincial capital. The city recorded an overall Air Quality Index (AQI) of 530. Air quality levels reached critical levels in various localities. An AQI of 902 was recorded in Iqbal Town, followed by 698 in Paragon City, 619 in Chaman Park, and 569 on Barki Road. Meanwhile, AQI readings stood at 471 in Model Town, 412 in DHA Phase 5, 358 on Bedian Road, and 298 in Askari X. The deteriorating air quality poses health risks, including eye irritation and respiratory illnesses. Residents have been advised to avoid unnecessary outdoor activities and take precautionary measures when going outside. According to the Meteorological Department, dry weather conditions are expected to persist, with no possibility of rain. The current temperature is 23°C, while the maximum and minimum temperatures are forecast to reach 29°C and 17°C, respectively. Humidity stands at 65 percent, while wind speeds have been recorded at 3 km/h. With no rain expected and winds remaining light, weather conditions are unlikely to provide significant relief from air pollution in the city.

headline: Safe working environment for journalists essential:CM
description: LAHORE - Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif on Monday said that the Punjab government was committed to protecting journalists’ rights and freedom
author: STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif on Monday said that the Punjab government was committed to protecting journalists’ rights and freedom of the press, describing them as the eyes and ears of society and champions of truth. In her message on the International Day to End Impunity for Crimes against Journalists, she said that journalists who raised their voices for truth and justice must be protected and enabled to perform their professional duties without fear. She said threats, violence and harassment against journalists were unacceptable and those involved in crimes against media professionals must be brought to justice. The CM said freedom of the press and freedom of expression were essential for a democratic society while free and responsible journalism played a vital role in strengthening democratic institutions. She said journalists exposing injustice, oppression and falsehood served society by highlighting public issues and giving voice to the people. Any attempt to silence the truth was an attack on fundamental rights. CM Maryam Nawaz said that the Punjab government fully supported press freedom and the protection of journalists’ professional rights and dignity. She also expressed her resolve to help homeless journalists realize their dream of owning a home. CM maintained that journalists in Punjab were safe and said her government would continue to ensure an environment in which they could work freely and securely.

headline: Seven arrested over fatal stampede at TikToker's mehndi in Sialkot
description: Punjab Information Minister Uzma Bukhari has said that seven people have been arrested and two others are being sought in connection with the fatal stampede
author: NNI
article_text:
Punjab Information Minister Uzma Bukhari has said that seven people have been arrested and two others are being sought in connection with the fatal stampede during a TikToker's mehndi ceremony in Sialkot.

The minister said an FIR had been registered over alleged negligence and dereliction of duty, while raids were underway to arrest the remaining suspects.

She said the rule of law would be ensured and all those found responsible would be brought before the courts after a thorough investigation.

Bukhari explained that the administration had issued a no-objection certificate (NOC) for the event, with specific conditions regarding security and arrangements. Under these conditions, the administration was responsible for external security, while the organisers were required to manage arrangements inside the venue.

She described the incident as tragic and said negligence would not be tolerated, adding that those responsible would face legal action.

The minister also noted that the TikToker, known as Mr Patlu on social media, had promoted his wedding celebrations as a major event and announced prizes and a lucky draw, attracting thousands of people to the venue.

The large gathering reportedly became uncontrollable due to inadequate arrangements, triggering a stampede that left two people dead and several others injured.

headline: Punjab appoints ADCs as focal persons to facilitate businesses, attract investment
description: LAHORE - The Punjab government has designated additional deputy commissioners (Headquarters) as focal persons for Ease of Doing Business in all districts, as
author: STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - The Punjab government has designated additional deputy commissioners (Headquarters) as focal persons for Ease of Doing Business in all districts, as part of efforts to reduce bureaucratic hurdles, streamline administrative procedures and create an investment-friendly environment. A two-day training workshop for the newly appointed focal persons began at the Civil Secretariat on Monday to familiarise them with business facilitation strategies, administrative reforms and digital tools. Presiding over the inaugural session, Chief Secretary Punjab Zahid Akhtar Zaman said the government had launched the Punjab Innovation for Value, Opportunity and Transformation (PIVOT) programme to stimulate commercial activity, promote industrialisation and unlock economic potential across the province. He said a dedicated PIVOT Secretariat had been established at the Planning and Development Board to oversee business facilitation initiatives and monitor investment outcomes. The chief secretary said an integrated inspection mechanism for commercial and industrial establishments would operate under the direct supervision of the additional chief secretary as part of a new regulatory framework. To ensure transparency and prevent arbitrary inspections, all inspection-related data would be uploaded to a real-time online dashboard. Digital platforms for business facilitation and the inspection dashboard were also being integrated into the unified e-Biz portal, he added. Addressing the participants, Zahid Akhtar Zaman directed administrative officers to remove unnecessary procedural obstacles and develop a relationship of trust and cooperation between district administrations and the private sector. He said the appointment of district-level focal persons was aimed at ensuring that business-related issues were addressed promptly and that investors could access administrative support without unnecessary delays. Experts from federal and provincial departments briefed participants on digital public service delivery, commercial opportunities and administrative reforms. Meanwhile, the Punjab Small Industries Corporation (PSIC) organised an exhibition alongside the workshop, showcasing traditional crafts and artisanal products from different districts to highlight their economic potential.

headline: LHC orders meeting between Noreen Niazi, her daughters
description: LAHORE - The Lahore High Court (LHC) on Monday directed authorities to arrange a meeting between Noreen Niazi and her two daughters at the jail at 10am on
author: STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - The Lahore High Court (LHC) on Monday directed authorities to arrange a meeting between Noreen Niazi and her two daughters at the jail at 10am on Tuesday (November 3). Justice Abher Gul Khan passed the order while hearing a petition filed by Sakina and Shahraiz challenging the extension of detention orders against the sisters of PTI founder. The court directed that the two daughters be allowed to meet their mother for one hour. It asked their counsel to submit an application to the Lahore deputy commissioner, who was directed to arrange the meeting on Tuesday in response to the request. The court also summoned the Lahore deputy commissioner in person on November 4 to explain the extensions in the detention orders of Noreen Niazi and Uzma Khan. Meanwhile, the hearing on a challenge to the extension of Aleema Khan’s detention was adjourned until next week. On the court’s direction, the home secretary submitted a report. A counsel representing the Punjab government informed the court that Noreen Niazi had been taken to hospital for medical treatment and was subsequently shifted back to jail on doctors’ advice. The government counsel further submitted that Noreen Niazi had already been allowed to meet her daughter Hajra Niazi on October 29 during her hospital stay.

headline: Snow and rain forecast across Kazakhstan on November 3–5
description: BAKU - Kazhydromet has released its weather forecast for Kazakhstan for November 3–5, 2026, Qazinform News Agency reports.Most of Kazakhstan is expected
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: BAKU - Kazhydromet has released its weather forecast for Kazakhstan for November 3–5, 2026, Qazinform News Agency reports.Most of Kazakhstan is expected to remain dry under the influence of a high-pressure system. However, an approaching northwestern cyclone will bring rain to western regions on November 4–5, with heavy downpours possible in some areas. Meanwhile, eastern Kazakhstan is forecast to see precipitation on November 3, mainly in the form of snow, which could be heavy at times. Icy conditions are also expected, along with stronger winds across the country and fog during the nighttime and morning hours. Daytime temperatures are expected to fall from 13–21°C to 6–19°C in western Kazakhstan and from 13–18°C to 10–15°C in the southeast. No significant temperature changes are expected in the rest of the country.

headline: PTV Drama, Film Academy to be revived with modern training facilities: Tarar
description: ISLAMABAD - Federal Minister for Information and Broadcasting Attaullah Tarar on Monday directed the formulation of a comprehensive strategy to revive the
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: ISLAMABAD - Federal Minister for Information and Broadcasting Attaullah Tarar on Monday directed the formulation of a comprehensive strategy to revive the Pakistan Television (PTV) Drama and Film Academy as a modern training institution, equipping young people with professional skills in filmmaking, drama production and digital content creation. He was chairing a high-level meeting to review plans for the revival of the PTV Drama and Film Academy and the revamping of PTV Home through specialised training programmes, modern technical facilities and practical, industry-oriented training models. Federal Secretary for Information Ashfaq Ahmed Khalil and senior officials of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting attended the meeting. During the meeting, various training models proposed in collaboration with the private sector were reviewed, with a focus on providing hands-on professional training to young people while creating new revenue streams for Pakistan Television. The minister said the revival of the PTV Drama and Film Academy and revamping of PTV Home were part of the government’s commitment to promoting the media and creative industries in the country. He said Pakistan was launching, for the first time, an advanced training programme in colour grading, adding that previously, professionals had to travel abroad to acquire training and access modern facilities in this specialised field. The availability of advanced colour-grading facilities in Pakistan would provide the film industry and private sector with access to modern technical training and resources, while helping improve the quality of local filmmaking, he added. The minister directed that a transparent and practical pilot project be launched in partnership with the private sector to ensure that training programmes remained aligned with the evolving needs of the industry. author: Staff Reporter
article_text:
LAHORE - Medical experts have warned that vitamin D deficiency is widespread in Pakistan, affecting people across different age groups despite the country’s abundant sunshine. They stressed the need for greater public awareness, early diagnosis and proper treatment to address the growing health challenge. The concerns were raised at the D Connect Summit 2026, organised in connection with World Vitamin D Day at Avari Hotel on Mall Road, Lahore. The seminar was arranged by *Scotmann Pharmaceuticals which brought together medical professionals who discussed the impact of vitamin D deficiency on bone health, women’s health and overall well-being. Prof. Dr Faisal Masood, Professor and Head of the Department of Orthopaedics at Mayo Hospital, Lahore, spoke on the topic, “From Childhood to Aging: Vitamin D – A Lifetime Partner in Bone Health.” He explained that bones perform several important functions in the human body. These include helping people move, protecting vital organs and maintaining calcium balance. Calcium is essential for the proper functioning of the heart, muscles and nerves, while vitamin D helps the body absorb and use calcium. Dr Faisal said Pakistan was facing a serious problem of vitamin D deficiency despite receiving plenty of sunlight. He referred to estimates suggesting that approximately 73 per cent of people were either vitamin D deficient or had inadequate levels. He identified several reasons behind the problem. People often avoid direct sunlight because of concerns about skin tanning and the country’s extreme weather conditions. Clothing habits, social customs, indoor lifestyles and air pollution also reduce exposure to sunlight. He added that changing food habits had further contributed to the problem. People were increasingly choosing food for taste rather than considering its nutritional value. The orthopaedic expert warned that vitamin D deficiency could have serious consequences for bone health, particularly in older people. He explained that osteoporosis often remained undetected until a person suffered a fracture after a minor fall. Referring to a clinical example of an elderly woman who suffered a fracture after falling at home, he explained how several factors, including old age, limited physical activity, steroid use and other health conditions, could increase the risk of weak bones. He stressed that bone health should be protected from childhood rather than addressed only in old age. According to him, nearly 90 per cent of peak bone mass is achieved during younger years. Children should therefore be encouraged to participate in outdoor activities and consume nutritious food to develop strong bones. He also highlighted that vitamin D had functions beyond bone health. It plays a role in several body processes, including brain development, immunity and the proper use of calcium. Dr Faisal urged parents to pay attention to children’s nutrition and physical activities, saying that a healthy lifestyle during early life could help reduce the risk of fractures and bone-related diseases later. Prof. Dr Asma Kazi, Professor and Head of Medicine at Rashid Latif Medical College, Lahore, discussed Pakistan’s vitamin D crisis and the guidelines for its proper management. Speaking on the topic, “Mapping the Burden, Mastering the Management: Pakistan’s Vitamin D Crisis and PSIM Guidelines,” she said that vitamin D deficiency was a major public health concern. However, she also warned against the growing practice of excessive supplementation without proper medical advice. She said vitamin D was among the most frequently prescribed supplements in medical practice, but doctors needed to consider three important questions: who should be tested, who actually needed supplementation and what dose should be prescribed. Dr Asma referred to different studies highlighting the high prevalence of vitamin D deficiency in Pakistan. She cited research reporting deficiency rates of 84.3 per cent in one study and 61.1 per cent in a retrospective laboratory-based assessment. She also referred to findings suggesting that 79.7 per cent of women of reproductive age had vitamin D deficiency, with 54 per cent moderately deficient and 25.7 per cent severely deficient. According to the figures she presented, vitamin D deficiency was also reported among children and adults in both urban and rural areas. Some studies conducted in different Pakistani cities showed deficiency rates ranging from 74 to 95.1 per cent. She explained that air pollution, limited exposure to sunlight, clothing practices, skin pigmentation and a lack of vitamin D-rich food were among the major reasons behind the problem.

The physician identified children, adolescents, pregnant and breastfeeding women, elderly people and individuals suffering from obesity, kidney disease, liver disorders and conditions affecting nutrient absorption as groups requiring special attention. She emphasised that vitamin D supplementation should be based on a patient’s medical condition, age and individual needs. Doctors should review patients’ medical histories, assess possible risk factors and carry out relevant tests before prescribing high doses. She also cautioned that excessive vitamin D intake could cause harmful effects. According to her, routine high-dose supplementation was not appropriate for everyone, and treatment should follow medical guidelines.

Dr Asma further explained that vitamin D requirements varied with age.

While daily requirements could be met through diet and sunlight in some cases, supplements might be necessary when these sources were insufficient or when a person had a confirmed deficiency or belonged to a high-risk group. At the summit, Dr Andleeb Arshad, Assistant Professor at Lahore General Hospital (LGH), also spoke about women’s health and the importance of vitamin D.

They stressed the need for greater public awareness, early diagnosis and proper treatment to address the growing health challenge. The concerns were raised at the D Connect Summit 2026, organised in connection with World Vitamin D Day at Avari Hotel on Mall Road, Lahore. The seminar was arranged by *Scotmann Pharmaceuticals which brought together medical professionals who discussed the impact of vitamin D deficiency on bone health, women’s health and overall well-being. Prof. Dr Faisal Masood, Professor and Head of the Department of Orthopaedics at Mayo Hospital, Lahore, spoke on the topic, “From Childhood to Aging: Vitamin D – A Lifetime Partner in Bone Health.” He explained that bones perform several important functions in the human body. These include helping people move, protecting vital organs and maintaining calcium balance. Calcium is essential for the proper functioning of the heart, muscles and nerves, while vitamin D helps the body absorb and use calcium. Dr Faisal said Pakistan was facing a serious problem of vitamin D deficiency despite receiving plenty of sunlight. He referred to estimates suggesting that approximately 73 per cent of people were either vitamin D deficient or had inadequate levels. He identified several reasons behind the problem. People often avoid direct sunlight because of concerns about skin tanning and the country’s extreme weather conditions. Clothing habits, social customs, indoor lifestyles and air pollution also reduce exposure to sunlight. He added that changing food habits had further contributed to the problem. People were increasingly choosing food for taste rather than considering its nutritional value. The orthopaedic expert warned that vitamin D deficiency could have serious consequences for bone health, particularly in older people. He explained that osteoporosis often remained undetected until a person suffered a fracture after a minor fall. Referring to a clinical example of an elderly woman who suffered a fracture after falling at home, he explained how several factors, including old age, limited physical activity, steroid use and other health conditions, could increase the risk of weak bones. He stressed that bone health should be protected from childhood rather than addressed only in old age. According to him, nearly 90 per cent of peak bone mass is achieved during younger years. Children should therefore be encouraged to participate in outdoor activities and consume nutritious food to develop strong bones. He also highlighted that vitamin D had functions beyond bone health. It plays a role in several body processes, including brain development, immunity and the proper use of calcium. Dr Faisal urged parents to pay attention to children’s nutrition and physical activities, saying that a healthy lifestyle during early life could help reduce the risk of fractures and bone-related diseases later. Prof. Dr Asma Kazi, Professor and Head of Medicine at Rashid Latif Medical College, Lahore, discussed Pakistan’s vitamin D crisis and the guidelines for its proper management. Speaking on the topic, “Mapping the Burden, Mastering the Management: Pakistan’s Vitamin D Crisis and PSIM Guidelines,” she said that vitamin D deficiency was a major public health concern. However, she also warned against the growing practice of excessive supplementation without proper medical advice. She said vitamin D was among the most frequently prescribed supplements in medical practice, but doctors needed to consider three important questions: who should be tested, who actually needed supplementation and what dose should be prescribed. Dr Asma referred to different studies highlighting the high prevalence of vitamin D deficiency in Pakistan. She cited research reporting deficiency rates of 84.3 per cent in one study and 61.1 per cent in a retrospective laboratory-based assessment. She also referred to findings suggesting that 79.7 per cent of women of reproductive age had vitamin D deficiency, with 54 per cent moderately deficient and 25.7 per cent severely deficient. According to the figures she presented, vitamin D deficiency was also reported among children and adults in both urban and rural areas. Some studies conducted in different Pakistani cities showed deficiency rates ranging from 74 to 95.1 per cent. She explained that air pollution, limited exposure to sunlight, clothing practices, skin pigmentation and a lack of vitamin D-rich food were among the major reasons behind the problem.

The physician identified children, adolescents, pregnant and breastfeeding women, elderly people and individuals suffering from obesity, kidney disease, liver disorders and conditions affecting nutrient absorption as groups requiring special attention. She emphasised that vitamin D supplementation should be based on a patient’s medical condition, age and individual needs. Doctors should review patients’ medical histories, assess possible risk factors and carry out relevant tests before prescribing high doses. She also cautioned that excessive vitamin D intake could cause harmful effects. According to her, routine high-dose supplementation was not appropriate for everyone, and treatment should follow medical guidelines.

Dr Asma further explained that vitamin D requirements varied with age.

While daily requirements could be met through diet and sunlight in some cases, supplements might be necessary when these sources were insufficient or when a person had a confirmed deficiency or belonged to a high-risk group. At the summit, Dr Andleeb Arshad, Assistant Professor at Lahore General Hospital (LGH), also spoke about women’s health and the importance of vitamin D.

headline: CM Punjab, French envoy discuss trade, investment and climate cooperation
description: French Ambassador to Pakistan Jean-Noël Poirier met Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif on Monday to discuss expanding bilateral cooperation in trade,
author: NNI
article_text:
French Ambassador to Pakistan Jean-Noël Poirier met Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif on Monday to discuss expanding bilateral cooperation in trade, investment, culture and climate action.

During the meeting, both sides exchanged views on strengthening partnerships between France and Punjab through economic opportunities, heritage preservation and joint efforts to address climate change.

Maryam Nawaz welcomed the French ambassador and said Punjab valued its longstanding relations with France. She expressed the provincial government's interest in exploring new avenues of collaboration, particularly in trade, investment, culture, education and environmental sustainability.

Ambassador Jean-Noël Poirier appreciated the Punjab government's development initiatives and expressed France's desire to further strengthen cooperation with Punjab in areas of mutual interest.

The meeting was held in a cordial atmosphere, with both sides reaffirming their commitment to promoting people-to-people contacts and institutional partnerships.

headline: China's solar technology plan signals new phase in global renewable energy industry
description: China's proposed framework for managing exports of advanced solar manufacturing technologies signals a new phase in the global renewable energy industry,
author: Web Desk
article_text:
China's proposed framework for managing exports of advanced solar manufacturing technologies signals a new phase in the global renewable energy industry, highlighting the growing importance of technological innovation and international industrial cooperation while maintaining the country's role as a major supplier of solar products.

China's Ministry of Commerce published the proposal in October as part of a wider revision of its technology export list, which also covers artificial intelligence and biotechnology. The proposal covers 12 advanced solar manufacturing technologies, while exports of finished solar panels remain unaffected.

Under the proposed framework, exports of technologies used to manufacture perovskite and tandem solar cells, certain thin wafers and large-scale fluidised-bed polysilicon would be prohibited.

Mainstream cell technologies, including TOPCon, heterojunction (HJT) and XBC, would face restrictions rather than outright bans.

The ministry cited the growing use of advanced solar technologies in sensitive sectors, such as aerospace and defence, as the primary reason for stricter oversight. Public consultation will continue until November 15, after which the final rules are expected to take shape. Until the list is formally updated, exporters must register certain overseas technology transfers.

The proposed measures distinguish between advanced manufacturing know-how and finished solar products, allowing China to strengthen the management of specialised technologies while continuing to supply international markets.

China accounts for more than 80% of global solar manufacturing capacity at every stage of production, while its capacity can meet nearly twice global demand, according to the Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis (IEEFA).

The country's manufacturing strength has helped expand global access to solar technology. UK-based energy think tank Ember reported that China's solar exports reached a record 68 gigawatts in March, doubling from the previous month as high energy prices linked to the Iran conflict encouraged countries to accelerate solar adoption.

Export trends have since moderated. According to customs data cited by Reuters, China's solar equipment exports declined 6.4% year-on-year in September and were down 9.5% during the year to date, following the removal of an export tax rebate on April 1.

The structure of international solar trade has also evolved. Exports of solar cells and wafers overtook those of finished panels in October 2025 as more countries developed domestic module assembly operations using imported components.

Muhammad Zaid Masood Khan, a PhD researcher at the National University of Sciences and Technology (NUST) and visiting researcher at the University of Science and Technology of China (USTC), told Wealth Pakistan that China's competitive advantage extended beyond finished panels to the sophisticated manufacturing knowledge required to produce them.

He explained that solar deployment in countries such as Pakistan would remain largely unaffected because the proposed measures do not cover finished panels. Module assembly would also face limited direct impact.

However, Khan said countries seeking to establish advanced manufacturing facilities would need to consider technology licensing requirements, particularly for production processes involving solar cells, wafers and polysilicon.

He noted that manufacturers could face additional licensing procedures for advanced technologies such as TOPCon or consider established alternatives such as PERC. For Pakistan, he identified government-to-government cooperation and joint ventures under the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) as potential avenues for developing domestic solar manufacturing capabilities.

Tim Buckley, Director of Climate Energy Finance, a public-interest think tank, said the immediate commercial impact of the proposed measures was likely to be limited because some technologies covered by the proposal, including perovskite cells, were not yet ready for widespread commercial manufacturing.

He said solar module prices had remained below production costs for at least 18 months, while global manufacturing overcapacity meant additional module factories might not be commercially necessary for another two to three years.

“For countries like Australia and Pakistan, and most of Africa, it will be immaterial,” he said.

For Pakistan and other import-reliant economies, the distinction between finished solar products and manufacturing technologies remains important. Continued access to Chinese solar panels can support renewable energy expansion, while domestic manufacturing ambitions may require more structured technology partnerships.

China's extensive manufacturing capacity and technological expertise provide opportunities for cooperation in module assembly, equipment supply, technical training and industrial development, subject to applicable technology-transfer requirements.

The proposed framework highlights the increasing strategic value of advanced solar manufacturing knowledge as renewable energy industries expand worldwide.

As public consultation continues until November 15, the final rules will help determine how advanced technology licensing develops alongside international solar trade and industrial cooperation.

headline: Jam Kamal urges OIC countries to strengthen trade financing and digital cooperation
description: Federal Minister for Commerce Jam Kamal Khan has called on member states of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) to strengthen economic integration,
author: NNI
article_text:
Federal Minister for Commerce Jam Kamal Khan has called on member states of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) to strengthen economic integration, expand access to trade financing and promote digital cooperation to boost exports and private-sector partnerships.

Addressing the 42nd session of the Standing Committee for Economic and Commercial Cooperation (COMCEC) in Istanbul, the minister reaffirmed Pakistan's commitment to enhancing economic and commercial ties with OIC member states.

The high-level gathering was chaired by Turkish Vice President Cevdet Yilmaz and focused on the theme of developing effective trade financing tools to increase exports among OIC countries.

Jam Kamal highlighted Pakistan's efforts to modernize its trade ecosystem, reduce export-related risks and facilitate businesses seeking access to international markets.

He said the operationalization of the Export-Import Bank of Pakistan (EXIM Bank) had strengthened support for exporters through trade credit insurance, guarantees and refinancing facilities.

The minister also highlighted the expansion of Shariah-compliant financing instruments, including Murabaha, Salam and Ijarah, to provide businesses with alternative financial solutions.

He said Pakistan was digitalizing export credit processes through integrated online portals connecting commercial banks and development finance institutions, helping reduce processing times and improve access to financing for micro, small and medium enterprises.

The minister also emphasized Pakistan's role as the host of the headquarters of the Islamic Chamber of Commerce and Development (ICCD), which connects private-sector representatives from 57 Islamic countries.

Highlighting emerging economic challenges, he called for stronger cooperation in digital integration, artificial intelligence and sustainable development, saying technological advancements offered new opportunities to improve competitiveness and regional connectivity.

Jam Kamal appreciated COMCEC's role in promoting economic cooperation and urged OIC member states to work collectively towards stronger trade partnerships, greater economic integration and sustainable prosperity.

headline: Uzbekistan’s Namangan invites Pakistani tourists to explore pilgrimage routes
description: Uzbekistan’s rich historical and spiritual heritage, sacred pilgrimage sites, and unique culture are attracting considerable interest among international
author: PR
article_text:
Uzbekistan’s rich historical and spiritual heritage, sacred pilgrimage sites, and unique culture are attracting considerable interest among international tourists. With the aim of further increasing the number of pilgrims from Muslim countries, a tourism routes programme entitled “Heritage of Pilgrimage” has been developed in the Namangan Region.

Initiated by the Namangan Regional Administration, this programme is designed to introduce international visitors to the region’s rich religious, historical, and cultural heritage. Through this initiative, visitors will not only have the opportunity to visit sacred sites but also to gain a deeper insight into the centuries-old history, national traditions, and profound spiritual values of the Fergana Valley.

In particular, the “Heritage of Pilgrimage” tourism programme includes historical monuments and pilgrimage sites located in various districts and cities of the region. Key destinations along the route include the Aksikent Archaeological Park in Turakurgan District, the Bibiona Mazar pilgrimage site in Chust District, and the Sultan Uvays Qaraniy and Bibi Naima Ona pilgrimage sites in Chortoq District. Other notable destinations include the “Mothers’ Tears” Complex in Pop District, the “Eleven Ahmad” pilgrimage site in Davlatabad District, and the Mulla Kyrgyz Okhund Complex in Namangan city.

Importantly, the routes are not limited to these destinations alone. The programme also encompasses more than 20 other major pilgrimage sites and cultural heritage attractions located throughout the region. This will enable international tourists to explore Namangan’s historical and spiritual treasures in greater depth.

The initiative is primarily aimed at showcasing the potential of pilgrimage tourism in the Namangan Region on the international stage. At the same time, by bringing historical monuments and sacred sites together into integrated tourist routes, it will enhance the region’s appeal as a travel destination. In the future, this is expected to help increase the flow of international tourists to the region, develop local tourism infrastructure, and create new economic opportunities.

Namangan’s pilgrimage destinations are particularly likely to attract interest in Pakistan, where the majority of the population is Muslim. Indeed, Uzbekistan and Pakistan share common religious values, a rich historical heritage, deep respect for great Islamic scholars, and spiritual traditions that have evolved over centuries.

In this regard, the “Heritage of Pilgrimage” tourism routes programme represents an important opportunity to take tourism and cultural cooperation between our countries to a new level.

headline: CM Punjab, French envoy discuss cooperation in trade, climate change
description: Punjab CM Maryam Nawaz and French Ambassador Jean-Noël Poirier discuss expanding cooperation in trade, investment, education, heritage and climate change.
author: APP
article_text:
French Ambassador to Pakistan Jean-Noël Poirier called on Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif on Monday to discuss expanding cooperation in trade, investment, heritage preservation and climate change.

During the meeting, both sides exchanged views on strengthening partnerships between France and Punjab in various sectors, with a focus on economic opportunities, cultural heritage and joint efforts to address environmental challenges.

Welcoming the French ambassador, Maryam Nawaz said Punjab valued its longstanding relations with France and was keen to explore new avenues of collaboration.

She expressed the provincial government's interest in enhancing cooperation in trade, investment, culture, education and environmental sustainability.

Ambassador Poirier appreciated the Punjab government's development initiatives and expressed France's willingness to deepen cooperation with the province in areas of mutual interest.

headline: Domestic violence can constitute misconduct by civil servants, rules SC
description: Supreme Court rules domestic violence can amount to service misconduct, upholding an IB employee's compulsory retirement despite his criminal acquittal.
author: APP
article_text:
The Supreme Court has ruled that serious misconduct by a civil servant in his private life, including domestic violence, can amount to service misconduct even if the act takes place outside office hours and has no direct connection with official duties.

Dismissing a petition filed by an Intelligence Bureau (IB) employee, the apex court held that acquittal in a criminal case did not automatically invalidate departmental proceedings where misconduct had been independently established through evidence.

The court upheld the compulsory retirement of Jawad Abbasi, who served as a cook in the IB and was accused of setting his wife on fire. He had challenged a Federal Service Tribunal decision upholding the departmental penalty imposed on him.

In a judgment authored by Justice Shahid Waheed, with Justice Ayesha A. Malik also on the bench, the court observed that the dignity of women was a fundamental constitutional value and that a civil servant's conduct at home could reflect on his suitability for public office and the reputation of the institution he served.

The court held that violence did not become a private matter merely because it occurred within the confines of a home.

It observed that under the Civil Servants (Efficiency and Discipline) Rules, 2020, conduct unbecoming of an officer and prejudicial to service discipline could constitute misconduct even when committed outside the workplace.

The bench clarified that the registration of a first information report (FIR) alone was insufficient to justify departmental punishment.

However, in the present case, the inquiry officer had examined 13 witnesses in the employee's presence and afforded him an opportunity to cross-examine them.

The departmental inquiry had independently established the charges, including allegations that the employee had subjected his wife to violence and attempted to portray the incident as a suicide.

The court explained that criminal trials and departmental proceedings served different purposes and were governed by different standards of proof.

It observed that an acquittal in criminal proceedings meant the prosecution had failed to establish guilt beyond reasonable doubt, but did not necessarily establish the accused's innocence for departmental purposes or certify his fitness to remain in government service.

The bench further noted that the employee had been provided an opportunity to defend himself and that the penalty of compulsory retirement was proportionate to the gravity of the established misconduct.

Finding no legal error, violation of due process or substantial question of law of public importance, the Supreme Court refused leave to appeal and dismissed the petition.

headline: Two policemen killed in attack on polio security team in Mohmand
description: Two policemen were killed and another injured in a gun attack on personnel assigned to polio vaccination security in Mohmand district's Pindiali tehsil.
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Two policemen were killed and another injured when unidentified gunmen opened fire on police personnel assigned to security duties for an anti-polio vaccination campaign in Mohmand district on Tuesday.

According to police, the attack took place in the Dag Taman Zai area of Pindiali tehsil, where armed assailants targeted policemen heading to perform security duties for the vaccination drive.

Two policemen lost their lives on the spot, while another sustained injuries in the attack.

Sources said the incident occurred near the Hashim Kor police checkpoint.

Police identified the deceased personnel as Zahoor and Arabi, while the injured policeman was shifted to a hospital for medical treatment.

Police said further details of the incident were awaited, adding that security personnel had cordoned off the area and launched efforts to apprehend the attackers.

Federal Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi strongly condemned the attack on police personnel assigned to polio vaccination security, warning that those responsible would not be shown any leniency.

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi also condemned the incident, saying such acts of violence could not weaken the nation's resolve to combat terrorism.

headline: Several schools blocked across France as thousands expected to join protests
description: Several high schools and universities were blocked early Tuesday across France as thousands are expected to take to the streets following a call by student
author: Anadolu
article_text:
Several high schools and universities were blocked early Tuesday across France as thousands are expected to take to the streets following a call by student organizations, according to broadcaster BFMTV.

Blockades continued at several high schools and universities in Paris, as well as in Marseille and Toulouse, where 12 of the city's 13 high schools were disrupted on Monday.

Several student organizations in Lille also called for the mobilization to continue, including through a demonstration scheduled for the afternoon.

The "Black Tuesday" called by high school student organizations is also expected to unfold in Lyon, where authorities approved a student demonstration.

The Paris police prefecture estimated between 15,000 and 30,000 demonstrators to take to the streets following a call by student organizations.

On Monday, the police prefecture banned the planned march from the Pantheon to the area around the Medef headquarters, citing a route that was "incompatible with the security constraints currently in force."

An alternative route between Porte de Charenton and Porte de Montreuil was later proposed, but the order was challenged before an administrative court.

headline: Australian premier warns global leaders of political polarization, threats to democracy
description: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese warned on Tuesday that growing political polarization was undermining social cohesion and putting democratic
author: Anadolu
article_text:
Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese warned on Tuesday that growing political polarization was undermining social cohesion and putting democratic institutions under increasing pressure worldwide.

Addressing the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Saint John's, Antigua and Barbuda, Albanese urged leaders to strengthen democratic safeguards and protect elected representatives from violence.

“Across the world, political polarisation is reducing social cohesion, placing additional pressures on democratic processes,” he said, according to a transcript shared by his office.

He warned that threats against politicians, particularly women, were increasing, with some resulting in serious attacks and killings.

Albanese cited the recent attack on Australian lawmaker Helen Haines, who suffered grievous injuries and remains in serious condition.

On Oct. 19, Haines, 65, was struck by a vehicle outside her electoral office in Wangaratta, Victoria, forcing doctors to amputate both her legs.

The premier said the incident underscored the urgency of protecting elected representatives and backed Commonwealth initiatives to improve their safety.

He added that conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East were having a "devastating" impact on the global economy.

Albanese renewed Australia's calls for Russia to end its war on Ukraine, a Middle East ceasefire and for the Strait of Hormuz to “reopen and restore the freedom of navigation and trade.”

He urged Commonwealth members to confront disinformation, election interference and the misuse of artificial intelligence, warning that digital platforms were fueling division and violence.

Australia, he said, supports keeping humans in control of AI "development and deployment."

He also called for stronger international cooperation on climate change, particularly to protect vulnerable Pacific island nations.

headline: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia agree to strengthen media, cultural cooperation
description: Attaullah Tarar and Saudi Ambassador Dr Rajeh Tami Albugamy agree to expand cooperation in media, culture, tourism, fact-checking and digital communication.
author: APP
article_text:
Federal Minister for Information and Broadcasting Attaullah Tarar and Saudi Ambassador to Pakistan Dr Rajeh Tami Albugamy on Tuesday agreed to expand bilateral cooperation in information, broadcasting, media, culture and public relations.

During a meeting with the Saudi envoy, Tarar welcomed him to Pakistan and congratulated him on his diplomatic assignment, expressing confidence that his tenure would further strengthen longstanding relations between the two countries.

The minister said Pakistan-Saudi Arabia ties were reaching new heights, with considerable opportunities to enhance cooperation in media, culture, television dramas, music, tourism and people-to-people exchanges.

He said the relationship between the two countries had developed over generations and was rooted not only in diplomatic and political engagement but also in shared history, religious bonds and strong public connections.

Referring to the strategic partnership between Islamabad and Riyadh, Tarar said the defence agreement between the two countries reflected the strength of their cooperation in the defence sector.

He also highlighted Saudi Arabia's economic and cultural transformation under Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, citing the development of tourism in AlUla and efforts to showcase the historical and cultural significance of Diriyah as examples of the kingdom's changing landscape.

Emphasising the importance of cultural diplomacy, the minister called for joint initiatives to strengthen cultural cooperation, particularly through the introduction of Pakistani television dramas in Saudi Arabia.

He said Pakistani dramas reflected family values, eastern traditions and Islamic culture and could help bring the people of the two countries closer.

Tarar also proposed exchanges of delegations comprising writers, poets, artists, musicians, media professionals and digital content creators to promote cultural and professional linkages.

Highlighting Pakistan's tourism potential, he invited Saudi media representatives, tourists and digital influencers to visit the country's tourist destinations and explore its natural beauty and historical heritage.

The minister recalled the sacrifice of Pakistani national Farman Ali Khan, who lost his life while rescuing several people during the 2009 floods in Jeddah.

He said Khan's bravery symbolised the enduring bonds of solidarity, affection and brotherhood between the people of Pakistan and Saudi Arabia.

Tarar also stressed the need for cooperation in countering misinformation and negative propaganda, strengthening fact-checking mechanisms and developing content that reflected the shared cultural values of the two countries.

He proposed establishing a joint working group comprising focal persons and technical teams from both sides to facilitate practical cooperation in these areas.

Briefing the Saudi ambassador on Pakistan's engagement with social media influencers for public awareness campaigns and the promotion of government initiatives, the minister said a social media post about the Prime Minister's Fuel Relief Scheme had received more than eight million views.

The Saudi ambassador described the longstanding ties between Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, based on mutual trust, respect and political and military cooperation, as a source of pride.

He also emphasised the need to further expand bilateral collaboration in cultural events, arts, literature and media.

headline: Meghan Markle's Netflix show loses out at 2026 Daytime Emmy Awards
description: Meghan Markle's Netflix series With Love, Meghan loses the 2026 Daytime Emmy for Outstanding Lifestyle Programme to A Different Breed, drawing online
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Meghan Markle's Netflix lifestyle series, With Love, Meghan, has failed to secure a 2026 Daytime Emmy Award despite receiving a nomination in the Outstanding Lifestyle Programme category.

The Duchess of Sussex's cooking and lifestyle show lost the award to A Different Breed, a programme centred on dogs.

The result prompted criticism on social media, with some users questioning the show's nomination.

"She should never have been nominated in the first place," one user wrote on X, while another reacted to the outcome by saying, "That is hilarious."

Meghan had earlier celebrated the show's Emmy nomination in an Instagram post on July 15, expressing appreciation for the production team behind the Netflix series.

"A huge congratulations to the amazing crew, producers, and team who worked on ‘With Love, Meghan’ on @netflix," she wrote.

"We are nominated for an Emmy for Outstanding Lifestyle Series!" she added.

The award loss comes amid reports of an ongoing investigation involving allegations of child pornography against her father, Thomas Markle.

headline: PSX investor base reaches record 681,965 in October
description: Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) recorded an all-time high monthly increase of 25,747 equity investors in October 2026, marking a 66 percent year-on-year rise and
author: APP
article_text:
Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) recorded an all-time high monthly increase of 25,747 equity investors in October 2026, marking a 66 percent year-on-year rise and taking the total investor base to a record 681,965.

Adviser to the Finance Minister Khurram Schezad said that the stock exchange added 218,894 net new investors during the first 10 months of 2026, from January to October, surpassing the combined additions recorded during the previous four full calendar years (2022–2025).

In a post on X, he said the investor base had increased by 56 percent year-on-year, while the addition of 406,995 net new investors since June 2022 represented an expansion of 148 percent from the then investor base of 274,970.

He noted that around 85 percent of the new investors belonged to Generation Z and the Millennial age groups, reflecting growing participation of younger people in Pakistan's capital markets.

According to the adviser, the sustained increase in investor participation signals growing confidence in Pakistan's economic stabilisation, improving macroeconomic fundamentals, policy direction and long-term prospects of the capital market.

He added that the trend also supported the government's broader agenda of promoting investment among ordinary citizens, expanding retail investor access, strengthening financial inclusion and deepening domestic capital markets.

The growing participation of individual investors is also expected to help channel household savings into productive investments and contribute to long-term economic growth.

headline: Americans vote in crucial midterms as early turnout tops 58 million
description: Americans vote in the 2026 midterm elections to decide control of Congress, with over 58 million early ballots cast and key Senate and House seats at stake.
author: Anadolu
article_text:
Americans are heading to the polls on Tuesday for midterm elections that will determine control of Congress during the final two years of President Donald Trump's second term, with governorships, state legislative seats and other offices also at stake.

The Nov 3 elections follow record early voter participation, with more than 58 million ballots cast ahead of election day, surpassing the approximately 45.9 million recorded during the same period in the 2022 midterms, according to the University of Florida Election Lab.

The elections will decide the balance of power in the House of Representatives and Senate, while voters across several states will also elect governors, state lawmakers and decide on ballot measures.

Record early voter turnout

Early voting includes ballots cast in person at designated polling stations and those submitted by mail.

Texas has recorded more than 7.7 million early votes, a substantial increase from the 2022 midterms. In Harris County, which includes Houston, participation exceeded one million before the early-voting period concluded.

Other states have also reported significant early turnout.

According to University of Florida figures based on state reports available through Sunday, more than 5.4 million ballots have been cast in Florida, 2.8 million each in Georgia and North Carolina, and 1.8 million in Michigan.

While the figures indicate increased voter participation ahead of election day, they do not necessarily suggest an advantage for either political party.

In states reporting party registration data, Democrats account for approximately 43 per cent of early ballots, Republicans 32pc and independent or other voters around 25pc, according to the University of Florida Election Lab.

However, party registration does not reveal how individuals voted, as ballots remain secret. The figures also exclude states that do not report voters' party affiliations.

Age-based data from reporting states shows that voters aged 65 and above account for approximately 44pc of early participants, compared with 37pc among those aged 41 to 65 and 6pc among voters aged 18 to 25.

Nearly 250 million Americans eligible to vote

An estimated 249.75 million US citizens aged 18 and above are eligible to vote in the 2026 elections, according to the Pew Research Center.

The figure represents an increase of approximately 8.45 million eligible voters, or around 3pc, compared with the 2022 midterms.

The American electorate has also become increasingly diverse.

White Americans account for approximately 61pc of eligible voters, followed by Hispanic Americans at 16pc, Black Americans at 12pc and Asian Americans at 5pc.

The Hispanic electorate has expanded by approximately 5.25 million since 2022, reaching 38.95 million eligible voters.

Asian Americans represent the fastest-growing racial or ethnic group among eligible voters, with their numbers increasing by around 20pc over the same period to 13.65 million.

However, eligibility does not necessarily mean that individuals are registered to vote or will participate in the elections, a distinction that remains important when comparing the overall electorate with early voting figures.

To participate in federal elections, voters must be US citizens, be at least 18 years old by election day and meet the registration requirements established by their respective states.

Control of Congress at stake

All 435 voting seats in the US House of Representatives and 35 of the Senate's 100 seats are being contested in the midterm elections.

Members of the House serve two-year terms and represent congressional districts allocated among states according to population. All 435 seats are contested every two years.

The Senate comprises 100 members, with each of the 50 states represented by two senators.

Senators serve six-year terms, with approximately one-third of the chamber facing elections every two years.

Of the 35 Senate seats being contested this year, 33 are part of regularly scheduled elections, while two are special elections to fill vacancies.

Beyond Congress, voters will elect governors in 36 states and thousands of state lawmakers.

According to the National Conference of State Legislatures, 6,139 state legislative seats are being contested across 46 states.

Voters in 39 states and the Northern Mariana Islands will also decide on 146 statewide ballot measures addressing issues including taxation, public spending and constitutional amendments.

When will the new Congress take office?

Voting is taking place on Tuesday, Nov 3, with polling hours varying according to state and local election regulations.

Results will be announced as ballots are counted, although closely contested races and differences in counting procedures could delay final certification.

Newly elected members of Congress are scheduled to assume office on Jan 3, 2027, when the 120th Congress convenes.

The outcome of the midterms will determine the balance of power in the House and Senate during the remaining two years of Trump's second presidential term.

The next US presidential election is scheduled for November 2028.

According to University of Florida figures based on state reports available through Sunday, more than 5.4 million ballots have been cast in Florida, 2.8 million each in Georgia and North Carolina, and 1.8 million in Michigan.
While the figures indicate increased voter participation ahead of election day, they do not necessarily suggest an advantage for either political party.

In states reporting party registration data, Democrats account for approximately 43 per cent of early ballots, Republicans 32pc and independent or other voters around 25pc, according to the University of Florida Election Lab.
However, party registration does not reveal how individuals voted, as ballots remain secret. The figures also exclude states that do not report voters' party affiliations.

Age-based data from reporting states shows that voters aged 65 and above account for approximately 44pc of early participants, compared with 37pc among those aged 41 to 65 and 6pc among voters aged 18 to 25.
Nearly 250 million Americans eligible to vote
An estimated 249.75 million US citizens aged 18 and above are eligible to vote in the 2026 elections, according to the Pew Research Center.
The figure represents an increase of approximately 8.45 million eligible voters, or around 3pc, compared with the 2022 midterms.
The American electorate has also become increasingly diverse.
White Americans account for approximately 61pc of eligible voters, followed by Hispanic Americans at 16pc, Black Americans at 12pc and Asian Americans at 5pc.
The Hispanic electorate has expanded by approximately 5.25 million since 2022, reaching 38.95 million eligible voters.
Asian Americans represent the fastest-growing racial or ethnic group among eligible voters, with their numbers increasing by around 20pc over the same period to 13.65 million.

However, eligibility does not necessarily mean that individuals are registered to vote or will participate in the elections, a distinction that remains important when comparing the overall electorate with early voting figures.
To participate in federal elections, voters must be US citizens, be at least 18 years old by election day and meet the registration requirements established by their respective states.
Control of Congress at stake
All 435 voting seats in the US House of Representatives and 35 of the Senate's 100 seats are being contested in the midterm elections.
Members of the House serve two-year terms and represent congressional districts allocated among states according to population. All 435 seats are contested every two years.
The Senate comprises 100 members, with each of the 50 states represented by two senators.
Senators serve six-year terms, with approximately one-third of the chamber facing elections every two years.
Of the 35 Senate seats being contested this year, 33 are part of regularly scheduled elections, while two are special elections to fill vacancies.
Beyond Congress, voters will elect governors in 36 states and thousands of state lawmakers.
According to the National Conference of State Legislatures, 6,139 state legislative seats are being contested across 46 states.
Voters in 39 states and the Northern Mariana Islands will also decide on 146 statewide ballot measures addressing issues including taxation, public spending and constitutional amendments.
When will the new Congress take office?
Voting is taking place on Tuesday, Nov 3, with polling hours varying according to state and local election regulations.
Results will be announced as ballots are counted, although closely contested races and differences in counting procedures could delay final certification.
Newly elected members of Congress are scheduled to assume office on Jan 3, 2027, when the 120th Congress convenes.
The outcome of the midterms will determine the balance of power in the House and Senate during the remaining two years of Trump's second presidential term.
The next US presidential election is scheduled for November 2028.

headline: TikToker Mr Patlu granted protective bail until November 10
description: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Tuesday granted protective bail until November 10 to TikToker Mr Patlu in connection with the stampede during a mehndi
author: NNI
article_text:
The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Tuesday granted protective bail until November 10 to TikToker Mr Patlu in connection with the stampede during a mehndi ceremony in Sialkot.

Mr Patlu appeared before IHC Chief Justice Sarfraz Dogar in his chambers at around 1:40 pm. Following a brief hearing, the court granted him protective bail five minutes later.

He was brought to the court in a wheelchair and left the premises in the same manner after the hearing.

When a journalist asked whether he regretted his actions following the stampede, the TikToker remained silent, raised his hands and left without commenting on the incident.

Punjab Information Minister Uzma Bukhari said the TikToker had extensively promoted his wedding celebrations and announced a large-scale prize draw, attracting thousands of people and resulting in an uncontrollable gathering.

She said that although a no-objection certificate (NOC) had been issued for the event, external security was the responsibility of the security administration, while internal arrangements fell under the organisers.

The minister added that a case had been registered and an investigation into the incident was under way.

headline: Fake doctor arrested at Lahore General Hospital
description: A young man posing as a doctor was arrested at Lahore General Hospital after the hospital administration exposed his false identity and handed him over to
author: NNI
article_text:
A young man posing as a doctor was arrested at Lahore General Hospital after the hospital administration exposed his false identity and handed him over to police.

According to reports, the suspect, identified as Muhammad Anas, entered the hospital claiming to be a doctor and attempted to deceive staff on duty. However, hospital security personnel became suspicious and questioned him, exposing his impersonation.

The hospital administration subsequently called police from Kot Lakhpat Police Station and handed over the suspect.

Police registered a fraud case against Muhammad Anas on the complaint of hospital security supervisor Mirza Hafeez and initiated legal proceedings.

According to police, the suspect had previously defrauded a citizen of a substantial amount of money by providing him with a fake job appointment letter.

headline: KP governor condemns attacks on polio teams
description: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi on Tuesday strongly condemned the killing of two police personnel protecting a polio vaccination campaign in
author: NNI
article_text:
Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi on Tuesday strongly condemned the killing of two police personnel protecting a polio vaccination campaign in Mohmand district and the abduction of four polio workers in Tank, calling the incidents attacks on humanity and the country's future.

In separate statements, the governor expressed profound grief over the martyrdom of two police personnel in a firing incident in Pandiali tehsil of Mohmand during the ongoing anti-polio campaign.

He said targeting police personnel deployed to protect polio workers was a cowardly act that would not weaken the nation's resolve against terrorism.

Paying tribute to the martyred officials, Kundi said they had sacrificed their lives while performing their national duty and their services for protecting the country and securing a healthy future for children would always be remembered.

He stressed the need for effective security arrangements to protect polio teams and police personnel during vaccination campaigns, adding that attacks on them threatened the health and future of the country's children.

The governor also prayed for the early recovery of those injured in the Mohmand incident and extended condolences to the bereaved families.

Expressing concern over the abduction of four polio workers in Tank, he termed the incident unacceptable and said the workers were performing a national duty to eradicate polio and protect children's health.

He directed the relevant authorities to take immediate and effective measures for the safe recovery of the abducted workers, emphasising that ensuring the security of polio teams was the government's responsibility.

headline: UCP celebrates Türkiye’s 103rd Republic Day
description: The University of Central Punjab (UCP) celebrated Türkiye’s 103rd Republic Day with a special ceremony on Tuesday, highlighting the historic friendship between
author: NNI
article_text:
The University of Central Punjab (UCP) celebrated Türkiye’s 103rd Republic Day with a special ceremony on Tuesday, highlighting the historic friendship between Pakistan and Türkiye and exploring opportunities for enhanced academic cooperation.

Turkish Consul General in Lahore Mehmet Emin Shamshek attended the ceremony as chief guest, accompanied by his wife. UCP Dean Professor Dr Khalid Manzoor Butt, Pro-Rector Professor Dr Hammad Naveed, Group Head of Punjab Group of Colleges Khadija Amir and other distinguished guests were also present.

The university campus was decorated with the national flags of Pakistan and Türkiye, while students warmly welcomed the guests with bouquets.

In his welcome address, Professor Dr Khalid Manzoor Butt highlighted the longstanding cultural, historical and brotherly ties between the two countries, describing their friendship as rooted in mutual trust and shared values.

He also highlighted the importance of defence cooperation among Pakistan, Türkiye and Saudi Arabia.

Students presented traditional songs and regional dances showcasing Pakistani culture, which were appreciated by the chief guest.

The Turkish Consul General thanked the university administration for celebrating Türkiye’s national day with enthusiasm and warmth.

headline: Pakistan-India World Cup clash receives 8.4 million ticket applications
description: The Pakistan-India group-stage match at the 2027 ICC Men's Cricket World Cup has drawn approximately 8.4 million ticket applications, highlighting the enormous
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The Pakistan-India group-stage match at the 2027 ICC Men's Cricket World Cup has drawn approximately 8.4 million ticket applications, highlighting the enormous demand for one of cricket's most anticipated contests.

Tournament organisers have scheduled the encounter for October 10, 2027, at Johannesburg's Wanderers Stadium, which can accommodate around 34,000 spectators.

The World Cup final, also set to take place at the same venue on November 21, has attracted nearly eight million applications.

South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia will jointly host the 14-team competition, which has received more than 120 million ticket applications from around three million applicants across 193 countries. The application window is scheduled to remain open until November 21.

The tournament will run from October 2 to November 21, 2027, with Australia and India, the finalists of the 2023 edition, set to meet in the opening fixture on October 7.

In the group-stage draw, Pakistan have been placed with Australia, Afghanistan, Zimbabwe and a team yet to qualify. England, South Africa, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, New Zealand and another qualifying side make up the second group.

headline: Pakistan welcomes Sri Lankan delegation for Buddhist Heritage familiarization tour to advance academic and cultural coop
description: A 16-member Sri Lankan delegation comprising senior government officials, Buddhist community leaders, archaeologists, academics, business representatives,
author: APP
article_text: A 16-member Sri Lankan delegation comprising senior government officials, Buddhist community leaders, archaeologists, academics, business representatives, legal professionals, and media personalities has arrived in Pakistan for an eight-day Pakistan Buddhist Heritage Familiarization Tour, aimed at strengthening bilateral relations and advancing cooperation in Gandhara heritage, archaeology, education, cultural preservation, and people-to-people connections. The delegation included Dr. E. A. Senarath Dissanayake, Director General, Department of Archaeology, Sri Lanka; Professor P. D. Mandawala, former Director General of the Department of Archaeology; Mrs. Dilrukshi Dias Wickramasinghe, 46th Solicitor General of Sri Lanka; and prominent Buddhist community and business leaders, including Mr. Jagath Sumathipala. The delegation is led by Mr. Deeptha Wickramaratna, President of the Bodhi Dhamma Buddhist Association, Australia, serving as its Principal Coordinator. The initiative is being organized and coordinated by Mr. Imran Shauket, Coordinator of the Prime Minister’s Taskforce on Gandhara, under the chairmanship of the Federal Minister for National Heritage and Culture, Mr. Aurangzeb Khan Khichi. It reflects Pakistan’s commitment to strengthening international engagement around the Gandhara civilization through cultural diplomacy, academic exchange, institutional partnerships, and heritage preservation. The delegation was formally welcomed at the Pakistan National Council of the Arts (PNCA) by Federal Minister Mr. Aurangzeb Khan Khichi, Secretary, National Heritage and Culture Division, Mr. Asad Rehman Gilani, Rear Admiral Fred Senevirathne (Retd.), High Commissioner of Sri Lanka to Pakistan, and Mr. Christy Ruban, Deputy High Commissioner, Sri Lankan High Commission. A key highlight of the opening day was the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between Hazara University, Mansehra, Pakistan, and Nagananda International Buddhist University (NIIBS), Sri Lanka. The agreement provides a framework for student and faculty exchanges, archaeology, Buddhist studies, joint research, academic programmes, and heritage preservation. The MoU was signed by Dr. Shakir Ullah, Professor and Chairman, Department of Archaeology, Dean, Faculty of Arts and Humanities, Hazara University, and Professor P. D. Mandawala, Founder of Nagananda International Buddhist University (NIIBS), Sri Lanka, in the presence of the Federal Minister, the Vice Chancellor, Prof. Dr. Ikram Ullah Khan, Hazara University, and other distinguished dignitaries. Following the ceremony, the delegation visited the Islamabad Museum, exploring its archaeological collections and gaining further insight into Pakistan’s Gandhara civilization and Buddhist heritage. The visit also features a significant international media component, with renowned Sri Lankan television presenter and media personality Mr. Chathura Alwis, accompanied by a professional production team, documenting the journey for an eight-episode television series to be broadcast in Sri Lanka, showcasing Pakistan’s Gandhara civilization, Buddhist heritage, archaeological treasures, and cultural connections with Sri Lanka. The remaining programme includes engagements with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, visits to museums and significant archaeological sites in Taxila, Takht-i-Bahi, Peshawar, and Swat, and interactions with Pakistani academic and heritage institutions. A further MoU between the University of Swat and Nagananda International Buddhist University is also planned to advance academic, archaeological, and research cooperation.
