headline: Hyra Arman inside the journey of a TikTok Star
description: Behind every popular profile, there is usually a person who has spent a long time learning what an audience wants. Hyra Arman, a Pakistani social media
author: Web Desk
article_text: Behind every popular profile, there is usually a person who has spent a long time learning what an audience wants. Hyra Arman, a Pakistani social media influencer, digital creator, and entrepreneur, is a recent example. Her career offers a useful look at how personality and persistence can turn into a profession. Who She Is She describes herself as an influencer, digital creator, and entrepreneur. Her journey is marked by dedication, consistency, and independence, and she has chosen to build her own identity rather than wait for opportunities to arrive. That self-directed approach explains much of the pace at which her career has moved. Content With a Human Touch Her videos cover lifestyle, beauty, fashion, skincare, travel, and everyday experiences. None of these subjects is rare, so what makes the difference is the way she presents them. She takes small, familiar moments and builds a story around them, which gives viewers something personal to connect with. This storytelling approach has resonated with millions of people across her platforms. The Weight of 1.6 Million Followers A following of 1.6 million on TikTok is a significant milestone for a creator only three years into her journey. It shows that her audience has not just watched her videos but chosen to stay. Many of her clips have crossed into viral territory with millions of views, a result that depends on both content and timing. Viral moments bring attention, but a large follower base keeps that attention from fading. How Brands Use Creator Reach Businesses in Pakistan increasingly turn to creators because audiences often trust a familiar face more than a traditional advertisement. A creator with strong reach and a consistent voice can present a product in a way that feels natural. Her work with more than 3,500 brands reflects this demand and suggests that brands see value in her ability to deliver professional, creative content across different categories. Spread Across Three Apps TikTok is her strongest platform, but it is not the only one. Instagram works well for her fashion, lifestyle, and daily moments, while YouTube allows longer content with more room for detail. Both perform well, giving her a base that does not depend on one platform alone. The Repute Connection Hyra Arman has begun a partnership with Repute Agency and Repute Talent, as part of her effort to widen the reach of her work in the digital space. Repute Agency is led by founder and CEO Malik Tayyab, whose experience in digital marketing focuses on helping creators build reach, communication, and growth online. Lessons From a Three-Year Climb Her progress points to a few simple habits. She stays consistent, keeps her content relatable, and treats her platforms as a business. She also keeps a genuine connection with her audience while delivering professional work for brands, a balance many creators find difficult. Repeated over time, these habits have helped her build trust with both viewers and partners. Final Thoughts For Hyra Arman, success is not only about numbers or recognition. She links it to creating her own identity, inspiring others, and building a legacy through passion and hard work. How she carries her current momentum forward will decide how lasting her place in Pakistan’s digital space becomes.

headline: DPM Dar reiterates Govt’s commitment to facilitating citizens
description: Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar, on Tuesday, reiterated the Government’s commitment to prioritising public welfare and
author: APP
article_text:
Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar, on Tuesday, reiterated the Government’s commitment to prioritising public welfare and facilitating ordinary citizens amidst global economic challenges.

He emphasised that sustained cross-party dialogue remained key to addressing national economic challenges effectively.

The DPM/FM expressed these views during a meeting with a delegation of Jamaat-e-Islami (JI) led by Liaquat Baloch today to discuss petroleum prices in the country, the Foreign Office Spokesperson said in a press release.

The meeting was attended by the Minister for Planning, Development and Special Initiatives, Adviser to the PM on Inter-Provincial Coordination, SAPM Tariq Bajwa, Secretary Finance and Special Secretary Petroleum.

The two sides held candid discussions on practical measures to provide relief to the common man, with a specific focus on easing the economic burden on low-income citizens.

Both sides agreed to continue their consultations over the coming days to formulate a way forward on energy pricing and public relief.

headline: Abdul Samad to captain Pakistan squad for Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026
description: The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) has named a 15-member Shaheens squad for the ACC Men’s Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026, with Abdul Samad appointed captain for the
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) has named a 15-member Shaheens squad for the ACC Men’s Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026, with Abdul Samad appointed captain for the 50-over tournament in Qatar from November 19 to 29.

Maaz Sadaqat and Hasan Nawaz are among the prominent selections as Pakistan prepare to defend the title they won in 2023.

Eight teams will compete in the event, divided into two groups. Pakistan are placed in Group B with India A, Nepal and the United Arab Emirates, while Group A comprises Afghanistan A, Bangladesh A, Hong Kong China and Sri Lanka A.

Pakistan will open their campaign against the UAE on November 20 at the University of Doha for Science and Technology ground. They will then face India A on November 22 and Nepal on November 24, with both matches scheduled at West End Park International Cricket Stadium.

Except for Pakistan's opening fixture, all group-stage matches will be played under lights. The semi-finals are set for November 26 and 27, while the final will take place on November 29.

Samad will lead a batting unit featuring Maaz Sadaqat, Hasan Nawaz, Haider Ali, Shahzaib Khan, Farhan Yousuf and Shamyl Hussain. Rohail Nazir has been named wicketkeeper.

The bowling options include spin all-rounder Danish Aziz, leg-spinner Saad Masood and Sufyan Moqim. The pace attack consists of Mohammad Hasnain, Ahmed Daniyal, Akif Javed and Muhammad Imran Randhawa.

Ahmed Daniyal was also part of Pakistan's Shaheens squad that won the previous T20 title, defeating Bangladesh A in a final decided by a Super Over.

Pakistan won the 2023 50-over championship in Sri Lanka after beating India A by 128 runs in the final. The team had previously finished runners-up in the 2013 and 2017 editions before claiming the 2019 title.

The Shaheens will aim to retain their 50-over crown in Qatar, where their group-stage meeting with India A is among the fixtures attracting attention.

headline: Point Of Law creates Melbourne Cup history
description: Point Of Law produced a remarkable performance to win the 166th Melbourne Cup at Flemington on Tuesday, giving trainer Ciaron Maher a historic achievement as
author: Muhammad Yashal Mazhar
article_text:
MELBOURNE: Point Of Law produced a remarkable performance to win the 166th Melbourne Cup at Flemington on Tuesday, giving trainer Ciaron Maher a historic achievement as he secured the first-ever trifecta in the race’s 166-year history.

Ridden by Ethan Brown, Point Of Law came from behind to claim the prestigious 3200-metre Group 1 contest, finishing 3.75 lengths ahead of stablemate Zahrann, while Juja Kibo completed an extraordinary one-two-three finish for Maher’s stable.

The result was a significant moment for Australian racing, with Maher becoming the first trainer to prepare the first three finishers in the country’s most celebrated staying race.

However, the victory was not without its challenges. Royal Supremacy made an aggressive move during the middle stages, opening up a considerable advantage over the field and carrying a strong lead into the home straight. Brown remained patient aboard Point Of Law before producing a decisive finishing effort to run down the leader.

The winning performance was particularly impressive considering Point Of Law had only six career starts. The British-bred four-year-old also arrived at Flemington with confidence after winning the Geelong Cup just two weeks earlier, becoming the fourth horse to complete the Geelong Cup-Melbourne Cup double.

Bred by and formerly owned by King Charles III before being sold to Australian interests, Point Of Law added another fascinating story to the Melbourne Cup’s international history.

The race was run in 3:21.88 on a Soft 5 track, with the $10.2 million prize race attracting a crowd of 97,112 to Flemington, the largest Melbourne Cup Day attendance since 2016.

While Maher’s stable dominated the finish, the result also highlighted the growing influence of international-bred stayers in Australian racing. The Melbourne Cup has increasingly become a meeting point for Australian and international racing talent, with horses from Britain and Ireland again featuring prominently.

For Brown, the victory was a career-defining achievement, while Maher’s historic trifecta underlined the depth and quality of his stable.

Beyond the result, the Melbourne Cup remains an important part of Australia’s sporting and cultural identity. First run in 1861, the race continues to attract national attention, bringing together racing enthusiasts and the wider public for one of the country’s biggest sporting occasions.

This year’s edition delivered more than a winner. It produced a piece of racing history, with Point Of Law, Brown and Maher adding their names to the long list of memorable Melbourne Cup stories.

headline: Gold prices remain unchanged, silver rates decline
description: Gold prices remained stable in the local market on Tuesday, while silver rates witnessed a decline, according to the rates issued by the All Pakistan Sarafa
author: APP
article_text:
Gold prices remained stable in the local market on Tuesday, while silver rates witnessed a decline, according to the rates issued by the All Pakistan Sarafa Gems and Jewellers Association.

According to the association, the price of 24-karat gold per tola stood at Rs412,136, while 10-gram 24-karat gold was traded at Rs353,340.

Similarly, the price of 10-gram 22-karat gold remained unchanged at Rs323,906.

In the international market, gold was recorded at $3,896 per ounce, with no change in its price.

Meanwhile, silver prices registered a decline of Rs120 per tola to settle at Rs5,368, while the price of 10-gram silver decreased by Rs103 to Rs4,602.

In the international market, silver was quoted at $48.90 per ounce, down by $1.20.

The association stated that the gold rates were based on interbank exchange rates, with purity of 999.0 (24 karat).

headline: BISP highlights progress in adaptive social protection, strengthens Pakistan-Germany cooperation
description: The Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP) and German Development Cooperation have reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening Pakistan’s social protection
author: APP
article_text:
The Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP) and German Development Cooperation have reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening Pakistan’s social protection system, with a particular focus on developing adaptive mechanisms to respond to climate-related risks, disasters and emerging vulnerabilities. A high-level German delegation, comprising representatives of the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ), the German Embassy, Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ), and KfW Development Bank, visited BISP’s One Window Centre in Islamabad to learn about the programme’s progress and the impact of Pakistan-Germany cooperation in expanding access to social protection. Chairperson BISP, Senator Rubina Khalid, warmly welcomed the German delegation. Dr. Asim Ijaz, Director General (NSER), and Muhammad Idrees Mian, Director General (CT), were also present on the occasion. The visit highlighted the growing importance of adaptive social protection, not only in addressing poverty but also in enabling vulnerable communities to prepare for and recover from economic and climate-related shocks. As Pakistan faces increasing exposure to floods, extreme weather events and other climate risks, strengthening the capacity of social protection institutions to respond to crises has emerged as an important development priority. Through Pakistan-Germany cooperation, BISP’s 647 Dynamic Registry Centres and 32 Mobile Registration Vehicles have supported the registration and updating of information for 38.7 million people, significantly strengthening access to social protection across the country.

These achievements reflect the value of sustained development cooperation in strengthening Pakistan’s social protection infrastructure, expanding outreach to underserved communities and enhancing the systems through which people can access assistance.

The BISP leadership highlighted the importance of Pakistan-Germany cooperation in strengthening the country’s social protection system and expanding access for vulnerable communities.

It underscored that social protection must go beyond providing assistance to address poverty and increasingly serve as a mechanism for building resilience against climate-related and economic shocks.

The leadership emphasised the importance of continued collaboration, institutional strengthening and coordination across federal and provincial levels to advance adaptive social protection and ensure that vulnerable people are better prepared for future crises.

The German delegation acknowledged the progress made through Pakistan-Germany cooperation in expanding access to social protection and strengthening institutional capacity. It highlighted the importance of continued partnership in advancing adaptive social protection, particularly as climate change and disasters pose growing challenges for vulnerable communities. The delegation reaffirmed the value of cooperation that supports Pakistan’s efforts to develop an inclusive, responsive and sustainable social protection system, with stronger links to climate adaptation and disaster risk management.

The German delegation’s visit provided an opportunity to discuss these priorities and continued cooperation between Pakistan and Germany in supporting a social protection system that is inclusive, responsive and better prepared for future risks.

The visit underscored the shared commitment of BISP and its German partners to strengthening social protection as a foundation for resilience, ensuring that people and institutions are better prepared to respond to the challenges of a changing climate.

The German delegation comprised senior representatives from the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ), Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ), and KfW Development Bank. The BMZ delegation included Christoph Rauh, Deputy Director-General for Bilateral Cooperation (Africa, Asia and Latin America); Anna Friedemann, Senior Policy Officer; Manuel Winkenbach, Senior Policy Officer; and Dr. Mirjam Büdenbender-Buchholz, Head of Cooperation.

The GIZ delegation was represented by Tilmann Nagel, Director, Division South Asia; Maria Poddey, Country Director, GIZ Pakistan; Johanna Knoess, AV/Project Head, Adaptive Social Protection; Alicia Beck, Country Manager, GIZ Pakistan; and Dr. Inam Muhammad, Social Protection Advisor, Adaptive Social Protection.

Representing KfW Development Bank were Klaus Müller, Director; Charlotte van der Schaaf, Senior Desk Officer; Andrea Grajcar, Country Head, KfW Development Bank, Pakistan; and Masuma Zaidi, Senior Sector Specialist.

The meeting also covered the SOPRAN Project, including Disbursement and Registration Centres (DRCs), Mobile Registration Vans (MRVs), Digital Financial Literacy Training (DFLT), capacity building and forthcoming shock-responsive initiatives. BISP provided an overview of its various programmes and initiatives, followed by an interactive session with beneficiaries to gain insights into their experiences and the impact of BISP’s interventions.

headline: Export-led growth, SME financing key to economic revival, says Aurangzeb
description: Federal Minister for Finance and Revenue Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb and Lahore Chamber of Commerce and Industry (LCCI) President Ali Hussam Asghar on Tuesday
author: APP
article_text: Federal Minister for Finance and Revenue Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb and Lahore Chamber of Commerce and Industry (LCCI) President Ali Hussam Asghar on Tuesday discussed key priorities, including export-led growth, improved access to financing for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) and a predictable business policy environment. During the meeting, they focused on strengthening the role of the private sector in economic growth, addressing business community concerns and introducing measures to improve competitiveness, investment and exports, according to the LCCI spokesman here. The finance minister welcomed Ali Hussam Asghar and highlighted the government’s commitment to achieving sustainable economic growth through greater private-sector participation, enhanced competitiveness and an expanded export base. He said that exports must remain central to the country’s growth strategy and that policies should facilitate exporters in becoming more competitive in regional and international markets. The meeting was also attended by Minister of State for Finance Bilal Azhar Kiyani, Governor of the State Bank of Pakistan, Federal Secretary Finance, and senior representatives from the Tax Policy Office, Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) and Finance Division. Emphasizing the importance of an improved business environment, Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb said that ease of doing business requires a facilitative and predictable policy framework, simplified regulatory procedures and effective coordination among relevant institutions. He underscored the need to address the concerns of businesses, particularly SMEs, and ensure that government policies support investment, productivity, employment generation and business expansion. Ali Hussam Asghar presented Lahore Chamber’s perspective on promoting SMEs, improving access to finance and facilitating business expansion. He highlighted the importance of a supportive business ecosystem, greater policy predictability, modernization and export growth. He also stressed the need for continued consultation with chambers of commerce and industry to ensure that business policies address ground-level challenges and support sustainable economic activity. The LCCI President also covered the ways to strengthen the SME sector as an important driver of economic activity, exports and employment. The Finance Minister said that improving access to finance for SMEs, facilitating business expansion and encouraging investment in modernization and capacity-building. He said that there is a dire need for practical and targeted measures to encourage businesses to expand their operations, increase investment and contribute to economic growth. Discussing taxation and regulatory policies, the finance minister said that these should support productive economic activity while promoting documentation and broadening the tax base. He emphasized evidence-based policymaking and constructive engagement with the business community to assess the impact of proposed measures on businesses, investment and employment. He also underlined the importance of simplifying procedures and building greater confidence between businesses and government institutions. Highlighting the importance of policy continuity and predictability, Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb underscored the role of the Tax Policy Office in maintaining sustained engagement with the private sector and developing a medium-term tax policy framework. He said that a stable and predictable policy environment would enable businesses to make informed investment decisions and plan for long-term growth. The Finance Minister said that the government is committed to working closely with chambers of commerce, industry representatives and other stakeholders to address business-related matters, promote SMEs and facilitate exporters. He observed that sustained collaboration with the private sector is essential to building a competitive economy driven by investment, productivity and exports.

headline: EcoStar’s QD Mini LED lineup brings cinema, sports and gaming to life with “Your world, your way”
description: Every home has its own way of enjoying entertainment. For some, it is settling in for a favorite film; for others, following the excitement of a cricket match
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Every home has its own way of enjoying entertainment. For some, it is settling in for a favorite film; for others, following the excitement of a cricket match or stepping into the world of gaming. With its latest QD Mini LED television lineup, EcoStar is bringing these different experiences together under its campaign, “Your World, Your Way.”

The lineup is led by EcoStar’s 100-inch Smart 4K QD Mini LED TV, designed to bring a larger-than-life viewing experience into the home. Combining advanced display technology, high-performance features, and immersive sound, the range caters to a variety of entertainment preferences, allowing consumers to choose a screen that suits their space and how they watch.

At the heart of the lineup is QD Mini LED technology, which combines Quantum Dot technology with Mini LED backlighting to deliver vibrant colors, deeper blacks and detailed visuals. 4K Ultra HD resolution and local dimming enhance picture clarity and contrast, while Dolby Vision and HDR10 support bring greater depth and richness to on-screen content.

The campaign’s three worlds- Cinema, Sports, and Gaming reflect the different ways consumers experience entertainment.

Cinema World: Bring the Big-Screen Experience Home

For movie enthusiasts, the Cinema World is about making every viewing feel more immersive. The 100-inch display offers a cinematic scale, transforming movie nights, favourite dramas and streaming content into a larger-than-life experience.

Dolby Vision enhances visual depth and detail, while Dolby Atmos, paired with a premium 4.1-channel sound system and built-in subwoofer, delivers fuller sound and deeper bass. Together, these features create an engaging viewing environment, whether watching an action-packed blockbuster or enjoying a quieter, story-driven film.

Sports World: Feel the Excitement of Every Moment

For sports fans, the experience is all about following the action as it unfolds. From cricket and football to other live sporting events, EcoStar’s Sports World is designed to bring the excitement closer to home.

A higher refresh rate supports smoother motion, helping viewers follow fast-moving action on screen. Combined with the expansive display, vivid picture quality, and immersive audio, the television makes watching matches a shared experience for family and friends.

Gaming World: Speed, Precision and Immersive Visuals

Gaming enthusiasts can explore a different kind of experience through the Gaming World. The television features a 144Hz native refresh rate, with support for up to 288Hz through DLG technology in compatible gaming modes, delivering smoother motion for fast-paced gameplay.

HDMI 2.1 connectivity enables users to connect compatible gaming consoles, including the PlayStation 5. QD Mini LED technology adds vibrant colors, sharper details, and visual depth, bringing game environments to life on the big screen.

Smart Entertainment for Everyday Viewing

Beyond its display and audio capabilities, the television offers smart features designed to make everyday entertainment more convenient. Google TV, powered by Android 14, brings supported content and apps together in one place.

Built-in Chromecast enables users to cast supported content from compatible devices, while Google Assistant supports voice commands for searching entertainment and navigating smart features. With 3GB RAM, 64GB internal storage and Bluetooth 5.1 connectivity, the television combines smart functionality with an immersive viewing experience.

A Screen for Every Space

Recognizing that every home has different viewing needs, EcoStar’s QD Mini LED TV range is available in 55-inch, 65-inch, 75-inch, 85-inch and 100-inch screen sizes. This variety allows consumers to choose a television that suits their living space, viewing preferences and entertainment requirements.

With its latest lineup, EcoStar brings together advanced display technology, smart features and a range of viewing experiences under one campaign. Whether it is the scale of cinema, the thrill of sports or the excitement of gaming, the range reflects a simple idea: entertainment should be experienced in a way that feels right for every viewer.

Because every home has its own world of entertainment and, with EcoStar, it is “Your World, Your Way.”

headline: NA body calls for true implementation of revised minimum wages
description: NA Standing Committee on Overseas Pakistanis called for the true implementation of the revised minimum wage to be paid as soon as it is announced, across all
author: APP
article_text:
NA Standing Committee on Overseas Pakistanis called for the true implementation of the revised minimum wage to be paid as soon as it is announced, across all bodies under the Ministry.

The Committee expressed reservations over replies on the payment of the minimum wage, and recommended that all boards and organisations under the Ministry put in place rules or a mechanism so that the minimum wage is paid as soon as the Federal Government raises it, said a press release.

The Committee recommended to all provinces and Gilgit-Baltistan that grants to workers following any incident be raised to Rs3 million. The Committee deferred the Employees’ Old-Age Benefits (Amendment) Bill, 2026, the Industrial Relations (Amendment) Bill, 2026 and the Emigration (Amendment) Bill, 2026.

Standing Committee on Overseas Pakistanis and Human Resource Development met today here, presided over by Syed Rafiullah, to review the implementation of its previous recommendations and to consider three Government Bills. The Committee expressed reservations over several of the replies furnished by the Ministry and its attached bodies on its earlier recommendations on the minimum wage.

The Chairperson observed that the Ministry should put in place an automatic mechanism for raising the minimum wage. The Committee accordingly recommended that all boards and organisations under the Ministry make rules, or adopt an appropriate mechanism, so that the minimum wage is paid as soon as the Federal Government raises it.

Reviewing the coal mine incident at Sorrange in Balochistan, the Committee was informed that three inspectors had been suspended by the Mines Department and two officials by the Labour Department of the Government of Balochistan, First Information Reports had been lodged and show-cause notices issued to the companies concerned, and 34 cheques had been handed to the Deputy Commissioner for disbursement to the affected families. The Committee recommended to all provinces and Gilgit-Baltistan that grants to workers following any incident be raised to Rs. 3 million.

The Committee deferred all three Bills, i.e. the Employees’ Old-Age Benefits (Amendment) Bill, 2026, the Industrial Relations (Amendment) Bill, 2026 and the Emigration (Amendment) Bill, 2026 together with its review of the recommendations concerning the Bureau of Emigration and Overseas Employment.

The Committee further sought complete details of the investment portfolio and interest income of all departments of the Ministry, and recommended that the Workers Welfare Fund place before it the details of every proposal presented to its Board in future.

The meeting was attended by MNAs including Zulfiqar Ali Bhatti, Dr Mahreen Razzaq Bhutto, Fateh Ullah Khan, Mohammad Ilyas Choudhary, Ms Sofia Saeed Shah (virtually), Ms Saeeda Jamshid, Mian Khan Bugti, Farhan Chishti and Ms Erum Hamid, along with the Secretary, Ministry of Overseas Pakistanis and Human Resource Development, and senior officials of the Ministry, EOBI, the Overseas Pakistanis Foundation, the Ministry of Law and Justice, and the Labour and Mines Departments of the Government of Balochistan.

headline: Govt moves to end LPG monopolies, abolish discretionary quota system: Tarar
description: Federal Minister for Information and Broadcasting Attaullah Tarar on Tuesday said the government was taking measures to promote competition in the liquefied
author: APP
article_text:
Federal Minister for Information and Broadcasting Attaullah Tarar on Tuesday said the government was taking measures to promote competition in the liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) sector by ending monopolistic practices and abolishing the long-standing discretionary quota system.

Addressing a news conference alongside Federal Minister for Petroleum Ali Pervaiz Malik, he said Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had directed the introduction of a merit-based and transparent system in the LPG sector to ensure fair competition and facilitate consumers.

Tarar termed the initiative a historic step, saying no previous government had attempted to dismantle the monopoly of a few individuals and introduce a competitive mechanism based on merit.

He said the government had also taken an unprecedented initiative by transferring profits generated by oil refineries to the public for the first time in the country’s history.

Highlighting the government’s response to the global energy crisis, the minister said the prime minister had prioritised public interests and taken measures to prevent additional financial burdens on consumers.

He said the government initially provided subsidies worth Rs133 billion to prevent increases in petrol and diesel prices and ensure fuel availability. Subsequently, a targeted subsidy mechanism was introduced through the Fuel Relief Scheme to extend assistance to deserving and underprivileged segments of society.

He said the measures reflected the prime minister’s commitment to protecting vulnerable sections of society while maintaining macroeconomic stability.

The minister said the government was also pursuing structural reforms to bring transparency into the economic system and strengthen regulatory oversight.

In this regard, he said the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA) had started publishing all relevant details on its website, describing it as a first in the country’s history.

Referring to reforms in the sugar sector, Tarar said the sector had generated an additional Rs60 billion in tax revenue for the first time.

He said the government was encouraging profitable sectors and those with the capacity to pay taxes to fulfil their national responsibility and demonstrate patriotism by paying their due taxes, adding that additional measures were being taken to reduce the financial burden on the public.

The minister said these measures formed part of a broader reform agenda aimed at improving transparency, strengthening tax collection and ensuring a fairer distribution of economic responsibilities.

He added that the prime minister had directed the formulation of a comprehensive strategy for gas supply during the winter season and instructed federal ministers to expedite measures aimed at providing relief to the people.

Responding to a question about the petroleum levy, Tarar said the prime minister had made special efforts to provide relief under difficult circumstances, including a temporary reduction in the levy.

Regarding talks with Jamaat-e-Islami, he said relevant issues had been discussed and the party had been asked to submit its proposals and possible solutions, along with technical recommendations. He said the government would consider further relief measures wherever feasible.

On the situation in Gilgit-Baltistan, the minister said the region held great importance for the federal government and the prime minister had also chaired a review meeting to assess development initiatives.

He said several measures were being undertaken to improve facilities in the region, including a 100-megawatt power project and the provision of solar panels, with the federal government providing funding worth billions of rupees.

Tarar said construction work on the Jaglot-Skardu Road was continuing, while various corridors were being developed and Danish Schools were being established in different areas of Gilgit-Baltistan.

He said the federal government was giving special attention to the region and a thorough investigation into the recent incident there was underway. The government, he added, would prioritise resolving the problems faced by the people of Gilgit-Baltistan.

The minister further said the Attorney General had been issued special instructions to ensure effective pursuit of pending cases affected by the implementation of the new system so that no legal impediments obstructed the provision of relief to the public.

headline: Pakistan achieves milestone with successful test of indigenous Fa’az air-to-air missile
description: Pakistan has successfully conducted the flight test of its first indigenously developed Fa’az air-to-air missile, marking another significant milestone in the
author: APP
article_text:
Pakistan has successfully conducted the flight test of its first indigenously developed Fa’az air-to-air missile, marking another significant milestone in the advancement of the country’s aerospace and defence capabilities.

Equipped with a state-of-the-art terminal guidance system, the missile is capable of engaging enemy aerial targets at extended ranges, said a news release issued by Inter Services Public Relations (ISPR).

Fa’az will significantly enhance the operational flexibility of the Pakistan Air Force, further strengthening the country’s overall defense posture. The successful flight test underscores the technical maturity, innovation, and self-reliance achieved by Pakistan’s defense industry.

The launch was witnessed by senior officers of the Pakistan Armed Forces, along with distinguished scientists and engineers who played a pivotal role in the development of this advanced weapon system.

The President, Prime Minister of Pakistan, COAS & CDF, and Services Chiefs have congratulated the scientists and engineers on this remarkable achievement, the news release said.

headline: Pakistan secures 11 China education deals for youth skills
description: The agreements, signed or witnessed by the PMYP chairman, establish cooperation between Pakistani and Chinese institutions in mechatronics, green energy,
author: APP
article_text:
Pakistan has secured 11 cooperation agreements and 14 skills and education projects with Chinese institutions during Prime Minister’s Youth Programme (PMYP) Chairman Rana Mashhood Ahmad Khan’s October 27 to November 3 visit to China, aimed at expanding international qualifications, technical training and employment opportunities for Pakistani youth, with Pakistan recording the highest number of signings among participating countries at the 27th China Annual Conference and Expo for International Education (CACIE 2026), according to a press release received here. The agreements, signed or witnessed by the PMYP chairman, establish cooperation between Pakistani and Chinese institutions in mechatronics, green energy, mobile communications, nursing, modern agriculture, cross-border e-commerce and international skills certification.

Of the 11 agreements, PMYP is directly a party to three, signed with the China Global Professional and Technical Certification Center, Jilin Electronic Information Vocational and Technical College, and Peili Vocational College.

The remaining eight involve the University of Lahore, Ghazi University, NUTECH Karachi, Preston Institute of Management Science and Technology, and Punjab Technical Education and Vocational Training Authority (TEVTA), in partnership with Chinese vocational institutions.

The visit also saw the unveiling or witnessing of 14 flagship skills and education initiatives, including an International Nursing Talent Training Base, a Cross-Border E-Commerce Talent Training Base unveiled by Rana Mashhood, Pakistan Tiangong College, a Joint Teacher Training Centre, and new committees on Industrial Robotics and Electronic Information Engineering.

In a significant development for employment opportunities linked to the country’s railway infrastructure, China Railway Group Secretary Han Hui flew to Pakistan on the same day following strategic discussions with the PMYP chairman to initiate on-the-ground work on skills training and employment opportunities associated with the Main Line-I (ML-1) railway upgrade.

Under the academic cooperation arrangements, Jilin Electronic Information Vocational and Technical College has already trained 10 Pakistani faculty members and will enrol 15 Pakistani students in its Chinese language programme from November.

“Every student enrolled, and every teacher trained is a step towards a stronger, more skilled Pakistan,” Rana Mashhood said.

The chairman also co-launched the International Green Power Talent Development Base in collaboration with the China Electricity Council, Thailand’s Office of the Vocational Education Commission (OVEC) and TANG International Education Group, aimed at strengthening international cooperation in green energy skills development.

During the visit, he addressed the Belt and Road International Forum on Industry-Education Cooperation, emphasising the need to align vocational training with industry requirements, promote joint academic programmes, introduce internationally recognised certifications and strengthen vocational teacher training.

He also addressed the International Seminar on Green Energy Talent Exchange at the China Electricity Council and held meetings with Pakistan’s Ambassador to China Ali Asad Gillani and senior embassy officials to discuss diplomatic support for education and skills partnerships.

In a separate meeting, Rana Mashhood held discussions with Mrs Benjawan Pokpong, Director of the Bureau of Cooperation at Thailand’s OVEC, on expanding education and vocational training collaboration among Belt and Road partner countries.

As part of the visit, the chairman presented the China-Pakistan International Education Cooperation Awards (2025-2026) under the auspices of the Embassy of Pakistan in Beijing.

To ensure effective implementation of the agreements and projects, the PMYP China Secretariat has been established at the Beijing headquarters of TANG International Education Group. It will coordinate cooperation among government departments, educational institutions and industry partners.

Rana Mashhood said youth empowerment remained a key priority of the government under the leadership of Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif, with the initiatives advancing the vision of a Skilled, Empowered and Digital Pakistan.

headline: Petrol price cut by Rs5.45 per litre, diesel rate increased by Rs3.68
description: The federal government has lowered the price of petrol by Rs5.45 per litre but raised the rate of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs3.68 for the latest pricing
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The federal government has lowered the price of petrol by Rs5.45 per litre but raised the rate of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs3.68 for the latest pricing period, according to an official notification issued on Tuesday.

Under the revised rates, petrol will now cost Rs369.06 per litre, compared with the previous Rs374.51. The price of high-speed diesel has been increased from Rs391.52 to Rs395.20 per litre.

The new prices will come into force at midnight on November 4 and remain effective until the next review.

The adjustment offers some relief to users of petrol-powered vehicles, including motorcycles and cars, while increasing fuel expenses for diesel consumers. The higher diesel rate may also add to operating costs for transport and logistics businesses, as HSD is commonly used by buses, trucks, heavy vehicles and agricultural machinery. Any rise in transportation expenses could put further pressure on the prices of essential goods.

The revision comes amid government efforts to address the financial difficulties faced by consumers. Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said earlier on Tuesday that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had instructed relevant authorities to prepare a winter gas supply plan and take measures to protect vulnerable segments of society.

Speaking at a press conference, Tarar said the government was mindful of the financial challenges facing ordinary citizens. He added that Rs15 billion in refinery profits had been transferred to the public and that profiteering by certain operators in the liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) sector had been curbed.

Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik said Pakistan had been facing economic pressures linked to the conflict that began on February 28. He noted that international oil prices had declined and expressed hope that the global market trend would lead to further relief for consumers.

headline: China shows how culture, digital economy can work together: WIPO chief
description: BEIJING - China can be an example of how to combine the creative economy, cultural heritage and the digital economy, Daren Tang, head of the UN’s World
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: BEIJING - China can be an example of how to combine the creative economy, cultural heritage and the digital economy, Daren Tang, head of the UN’s World Intellectual Property Organisation (WIPO), said a group of journalists. Tang spoke on the sidelines of the 2026 International Copyright Forum, which runs from November 2 to 4 in Dunhuang, Gansu province, northwest China and is co-hosted by China’s National Copyright Administration and WIPO. According to the administration, China’s copyright industry generated 10.06 trillion yuan in value added in 2024, or 7.46 percent of GDP, and employed 15.8 million people in urban units. Tang cited a presentation by Chinese tech giant Tencent on using its digital platforms to promote Chinese culture overseas through films, music and stories. He also pointed to Black Myth: Wukong, a Chinese action game based on the classic novel Journey to the West, which he said introduces international audiences to Chinese culture, history and historical sites, a wire service reported. Worldwide, he said, the creative economy, cultural heritage and digital technologies are coming together to entertain audiences and create economic opportunities, in what he called “the next evolution of the creative economy.” Dunhuang is home to the Mogao Caves, a UNESCO World Heritage site spanning over 1,000 years of Buddhist art. headline: Lahore records 15pc improvement in air quality: EPCCD
description: LAHORE - The provincial capital recorded a 15 per cent net improvement across six major air pollutants during the first year of the Punjab government’s
author: STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - The provincial capital recorded a 15 per cent net improvement across six major air pollutants during the first year of the Punjab government’s real-time air quality monitoring program, while the city’s peak Air Quality Index (AQI) declined by 28pc in October 2026 compared to the corresponding period last year, according to a report released by the Environment Protection and Climate Change Department (EPCCD). The department said the improvement reflected a reduction across six major atmospheric pollutants rather than a change in a single parameter, particularly fine particulate matter (PM2.5). Lahore also recorded no days in the hazardous AQI category, defined as an index above 300, during October 2026,against four such days in October 2025. The findings were based on the first full year of real-time air quality monitoring and publicly available ground-based measurements. The government said the data provided an empirical basis for assessing the impact of its air pollution control measures and developing targeted interventions. According to the EPCCD, the first reading on Punjab’s real-time air quality portal was published on Oct 1, 2025, with an initial network of 30 regulatory-grade monitoring stations. The network has since expanded to 59 stations, which continuously measure six air pollutants and seven meteorological parameters. The government plans to increase the number of monitoring stations to 100 during the 2025-26 period to strengthen its capacity for monitoring ambient air quality across the province. The department maintained that the expanded network had enabled authorities to make more informed decisions through accurate, ground-based measurements, particularly in contrast to assessments relying on low-cost, non-regulatory sensors and satellite-derived models. The EPCCD also highlighted the role of meteorological conditions in interpreting the improvement. According to official Pakistan Meteorological Department statistics, Lahore received 50pc less rainfall in October 2026 than in October 2025,indicating that the improvement was recorded despite relatively drier conditions. Another important factor in assessing air pollution is the atmospheric boundary layer, also known as the mixing height, which determines the volume of air available to dilute and disperse pollutants. The department said ground-based measurements conducted by the SUPARCO using a ceilometer in Lahore showed an increase of only 10 meters in the minimum mixing layer height during the comparison period. This finding was presented in contrast to a 25-meter increase cited by the Pakistan Air Quality Initiative (PAQI). The EPCCD questioned the reliability of the latter assessment, arguing that ground-based instruments provided more appropriate measurements for evaluating local air quality interventions. The department also referred to peer-reviewed research published in January 2026, which identified systematic biases of between 200 and 500 meters in ERA5 reanalysis data over the monsoon region. It said such model-derived products were useful for regional research but had limitations when used to assess the local impact of air pollution control policies. Alongside monitoring infrastructure, the Punjab government has been implementing a multi-sectoral air pollution reduction strategy targeting transport, industrial emissions, brick kilns and agricultural burning. In the transport sector, the government has introduced 612 electric buses while also providing electric bikes and improving traffic management to reduce emissions from conventional vehicles. The department said around 500,000 vehicles had undergone emissions testing while more than 800 legal notices had been issued to heavy transport vehicles over emissions and fitness certification requirements. The government aims to expand its electric bus fleet to 3,000 vehicles as part of its clean mobility strategy. Industrial compliance has also been strengthened through the Environment Protection Force, which monitors emissions, fuel quality and fugitive dust control systems at more than 600 sites across Punjab. The department said industries emitting excessive smoke without adequate emission-control systems, as well as units using unauthorized fuels, were not allowed to operate. The government has also imposed a complete ban on the operation of tyre pyrolysis plants and the use of carbon powder as industrial fuel, citing concerns over hazardous emissions. Agricultural emissions, particularly those caused by the burning of crop residue, remain another major component of the anti-smog strategy. The EPCCD said field-level stubble-burning incidents had declined by one-third during the first year after the government provided 10,000 super seeders to farmers through targeted subsidies. The government plans to increase the number of subsidized super seeders to 25,000 and introduce additional mechanized solutions,including Kubota harvesters and stubble balers, to discourage open burning and facilitate the use of crop residue as industrial fuel.

LAHORE - The provincial capital recorded a 15 per cent net improvement across six major air pollutants during the first year of the Punjab government’s real-time air quality monitoring program, while the city’s peak Air Quality Index (AQI) declined by 28pc in October 2026 compared to the corresponding period last year, according to a report released by the Environment Protection and Climate Change Department (EPCCD).

The department said the improvement reflected a reduction across six major atmospheric pollutants rather than a change in a single parameter, particularly fine particulate matter (PM2.5). Lahore also recorded no days in the hazardous AQI category, defined as an index above 300, during October 2026,against four such days in October 2025. The findings were based on the first full year of real-time air quality monitoring and publicly available ground-based measurements. The government said the data provided an empirical basis for assessing the impact of its air pollution control measures and developing targeted interventions. According to the EPCCD, the first reading on Punjab’s real-time air quality portal was published on Oct 1, 2025, with an initial network of 30 regulatory-grade monitoring stations. The network has since expanded to 59 stations, which continuously measure six air pollutants and seven meteorological parameters. The government plans to increase the number of monitoring stations to 100 during the 2025-26 period to strengthen its capacity for monitoring ambient air quality across the province. The department maintained that the expanded network had enabled authorities to make more informed decisions through accurate, ground-based measurements, particularly in contrast to assessments relying on low-cost, non-regulatory sensors and satellite-derived models. The EPCCD also highlighted the role of meteorological conditions in interpreting the improvement. According to official Pakistan Meteorological Department statistics, Lahore received 50pc less rainfall in October 2026 than in October 2025,indicating that the improvement was recorded despite relatively drier conditions. Another important factor in assessing air pollution is the atmospheric boundary layer, also known as the mixing height, which determines the volume of air available to dilute and disperse pollutants. The department said ground-based measurements conducted by the SUPARCO using a ceilometer in Lahore showed an increase of only 10 meters in the minimum mixing layer height during the comparison period. This finding was presented in contrast to a 25-meter increase cited by the Pakistan Air Quality Initiative (PAQI). The EPCCD questioned the reliability of the latter assessment, arguing that ground-based instruments provided more appropriate measurements for evaluating local air quality interventions. The department also referred to peer-reviewed research published in January 2026, which identified systematic biases of between 200 and 500 meters in ERA5 reanalysis data over the monsoon region. It said such model-derived products were useful for regional research but had limitations when used to assess the local impact of air pollution control policies. Alongside monitoring infrastructure, the Punjab government has been implementing a multi-sectoral air pollution reduction strategy targeting transport, industrial emissions, brick kilns and agricultural burning. In the transport sector, the government has introduced 612 electric buses while also providing electric bikes and improving traffic management to reduce emissions from conventional vehicles.

The department said around 500,000 vehicles had undergone emissions testing while more than 800 legal notices had been issued to heavy transport vehicles over emissions and fitness certification requirements.

The government aims to expand its electric bus fleet to 3,000 vehicles as part of its clean mobility strategy.

Industrial compliance has also been strengthened through the Environment Protection Force, which monitors emissions, fuel quality and fugitive dust control systems at more than 600 sites across Punjab.

The department said industries emitting excessive smoke without adequate emission-control systems, as well as units using unauthorized fuels, were not allowed to operate.

The government has also imposed a complete ban on the operation of tyre pyrolysis plants and the use of carbon powder as industrial fuel, citing concerns over hazardous emissions.

Agricultural emissions, particularly those caused by the burning of crop residue, remain another major component of the anti-smog strategy.

The EPCCD said field-level stubble-burning incidents had declined by one-third during the first year after the government provided 10,000 super seeders to farmers through targeted subsidies.

The government plans to increase the number of subsidized super seeders to 25,000 and introduce additional mechanized solutions,including Kubota harvesters and stubble balers, to discourage open burning and facilitate the use of crop residue as industrial fuel.

headline: US votes in midterm elections seen as referendum on Trump
description: WASHINGTON - Americans struggling with high prices and angry over an unpopular war with Iran began voting on Tuesday in one of the most consequential
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
WASHINGTON - Americans struggling with high prices and angry over an unpopular war with Iran began voting on Tuesday in one of the most consequential elections, widely seen as a referendum on Donald Trump’s second term.

Voters in several US states, including New York, Georgia and South Carolina, have been casting their ballots this morning, joining millions who did so before Election Day.

The stakes are high for both parties as Democrats attempt to gain control of both the House and Senate. Democrats entered Election Day with a 9-point advantage in the generic congressional ballot, according to CNN’s Poll of Polls. Meanwhile, Republicans face tests of their redistricting strategy and their grip on Senate seats in solidly red states.

At stake in the elections are all 435 seats of the House and 37 seats in the 100-member Senate.

Elections are also being held for the post of Governor in 36 states. On Monday, the Republicans and the Democrats made their final pitch to the voters, with Trump choosing an unusual venue the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool to focus on the renovations undertaken in the national capital instead of talking about tax cuts, tariffs and border security, which have been the high points of his election rallies.

With more than $1.48 billion wagered on Tuesday’s US midterm elections, prediction markets such as Kalshi and Polymarket are facing their biggest test yet of how reliably they can forecast political races amid growing scrutiny of their businesses.

The platforms rose to prominence in 2024 when they bucked traditional opinion polls in signaling that Donald Trump would win the presidency, and have since amassed a global following among media outlets and investors.

According to the White House, Trump did a whirlwind tour of 20 states, mostly Republican strongholds, to address 30 rallies in the last 32 days. Analysts say his approval ratings are at an all-time low, and he has become a liability to Republican candidates.

If the pre-poll forecasts come true and Democrats take control of the US Congress, it will allow for deeper Congressional scrutiny and checks of Trump’s actions, which will severely limit his ability to push his agenda. He will, however, retain the power to govern through executive orders, which will be valid for two years.

Trump acknowledged the possibility of his wings being clipped but indicated that he will not allow Congress to slow him down.

“I guess I’ll become Mr Veto,” Trump told the New York Postin response to a question on Republicans losing control of both Houses of the US Congress.

Former President Barack Obama boosted the Democratic campaign with rallies in Ohio, Michigan and Georgia, which clearly left Trump rattled.

“This election is our last, best chance of at least reining him in, reining in some of the foolishness of this administration,” Obama said in Georgia.

The Democrats, however, suffered an unexpected setback in the eleventh hour when Congresswoman Haley Stevens of Michigan crossed over to the Republican side on Sunday, breaking ranks with Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed, who could be the first Muslim elected to the US Senate.

The Democratic Party quickly rallied behind El-Sayed by issuing statements condemning Stevens, who sprung a surprise by endorsing El-Sayed’s Republican rival, Mike Rogers, and appearing alongside him in public.

Stevens lost in the Senate primary to El-Sayed. She is a staunch supporter of Israel, while El-Sayed is a fierce critic of the US ally.

The Democrats are hoping to flip seven Senate seats: Michigan, Maine, Ohio, Kansas, Texas, Iowa and Alaska in their bid to gain a majority in the 100-member House.

Each of the 50 states in the United States is represented by two Senators who sit in the Congress for a six-year term. But the Senators are divided into three lots, and their terms are staggered so that elections are held every two years.

The mid-term elections are also crucial for Vice President J D Vance, who is burnishing his credentials to become a successor to Trump’s mantle.

Vance made campaign stops in New York and Ohio on Monday, where Republicans were fighting for House and Senate seats.

He highlighted Trump’s moves to end taxes on tips and overtime and secure the border while branding Democrats as “lunatics” who have contempt for American voters.

About 210 million Americans are registered to vote, according to USAFacts. California has the most registered voters, with 23.2 million, followed by Texas (17.4 million) and Florida (13.6 million). Together, they account for about 26 percent of all registered voters.

According to the AP, more than 57 million ballots have been cast in 47 states and D.C. as of Monday, with turnout surpassing the early vote four years ago in many closely watched states.

Meanwhile, The United States has launched “defensive strikes” on Iran’s Qeshm island in the Strait of Hormuz on the eve of crucial midterm elections, according to US officials.

Iranian state news agency IRNA confirmed several explosions on the island on Monday.

The US officials described the strikes as limited and said they were in response to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) firing upon a US aircraft.

The strikes appeared to be limited as opposed to a return to full hostilities but followed President Donald Trump previously saying the US wouldn’t launch strikes on Iran before Tuesday’s midterms. The strikes were reported by The Wall Street Journal and CBS News.

The unpopular Iran war and the resulting impact on US gasoline prices and other parts of the economy have been a vulnerability for Republicans as they try to keep control of Congress.

The administration was last known to have carried out some attacks in early September, but thousands of US troops remain in the waters off Iran to maintain a naval blockade aimed at preventing tankers carrying Iranian oil from getting to the global market. A third aircraft carrier and thousands of additional troops are on their way to the Middle East.

Iran’s top security official says the US response to the latest ceasefire offer was “not convincing.”

“America’s response to Iran’s rights and demands was not convincing,” writes Supreme National Security Secretary Mohsen Rezaei on X, “and they must fully and explicitly address Iran’s seven conditions and act upon them; only then will the Strait of Hormuz be reopened.”

Among Iran’s demands are a permanent end to the war, including Israel’s operations against Hamas and Hezbollah; the lifting of the US blockade on Iran; the withdrawal of US forces; lifting sanctions; paying reparations for the war; and recognizing new arrangements for shipping in Hormuz that Iran will set.

Earlier Monday, US Vice President JD Vance offered optimism that a deal can still be struck to prevent Trump from following through on his threat to potentially order new strikes on Iran after the midterm elections.

Vance sent a letter to Iran’s security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, last week, but the White House has offered scant details about the contents. Trump told reporters that the letter was focused on assisting Iran with “medical supplies and various things.”

But Vance on Monday suggested there’s reason to believe that the US and Iran could still come to an agreement.

“We’ve had a number of good conversations with the Iranians,” Vance told reporters on Monday when asked about the letter. “I actually just spoke with the president of the United States about an hour ago about this. Look, the president and I both feel pretty good about the prospects for potentially coming to a negotiated settlement. We’re going to keep on working at it.”

Vance’s comments came as the region remains on edge about the prospects of the US resuming full-scale operations against Iran. The backchannel efforts are playing out as Israel and some Middle East allies lobby Trump on the way ahead in the 8-month-old war that has rattled global markets and wreaked havoc on Iran.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is pushing for another wave of strikes on Iran after Tuesday’s elections in the United States, according to two regional officials and a third person familiar with the matter.

A return to full-scale war with Iran could help Netanyahu to form an emergency government after he and his far-right allies lost their parliamentary majority in last week’s elections. Trump has alternated between threatening major strikes and pushing for a deal with Iran.

The two officials said diplomatic efforts have made progress, with Qatari mediators holding two rounds of talks last week with Iranian officials. The two officials said the mediators are trying to advance a framework for Iran to cease its attacks in the Strait of Hormuz in return for the US lifting its blockade on Iran’s ports.

They said more talks are planned for this week. The two officials spoke on condition of anonymity because they were discussing classified briefings they had received from American and Israeli officials.

One official said Netanyahu was working with senior officials in the US administration to persuade Trump to launch a quick but extensive air campaign and that the president does not appear to have made a decision.

Netanyahu pressed for strikes during a call over the weekend with Trump, who would not commit to taking military action, according to a person who was briefed on it.

Other US allies in the Middle East are warning against more strikes, saying that would destabilize the region and could lead Iran-allied Houthi rebels in Yemen to step up their attacks on Saudi Arabia and Red Sea shipping, a third regional official said. Iran-backed militias in Iraq could also get involved.

Saudi Defense Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman said he spoke by phone on Monday with US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth about “the latest regional and international developments” and the Houthis’ continued attacks on Saudi Arabia.

Oil prices dropped sharply on Monday as renewed diplomatic efforts to end the war between the US and Iran appeared to show signs of headway. Rising prices at the pump, a byproduct of the war, have been a weight on Trump’s Republican Party as it tries to maintain control of both chambers of Congress.

Trump noted the drop in a speech in Washington on Monday, which was billed as his closing argument to Americans, and sought to minimize the scale of the conflict, which has cost US taxpayers at least $47 billion.

“I don’t know if you even call it a war, because we haven’t been doing any fighting for months,” Trump said.

Netanyahu has not commented on Iran since the Israeli election, and there was no word from his office on the latest call with Trump.

Iranian officials say publicly they are prepared for war or diplomacy.

Iran’s foreign minister Abbas Araghchi told the IRNA earlier that “very intensive” talks to try and end the war are under way with the US via mediators.

He also said Tehran was prepared for both diplomatic and military scenarios “more than ever before” and that it was up to the US to choose between a “wise path” of negotiation or the “mistake of military aggression”.

But Iran wants guarantees that the US will implement its side of any agreement. The US and Israel have twice attacked Iran while it was engaged in negotiations over its disputed nuclear program.

The new supreme leader, Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, met with Iran’s military chiefs and said the response to “any kind and level of threat” from the US or Israel should be immediate and without “geographic limits,” and urged an expansion of the list of potential targets.

A recent analysis by The Associated Press found that Iranian strikes on more than two dozen US bases since the start of the war have caused billions of dollars in equipment damage.

Iran’s security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, told state television that “the tone has completely changed” from the US and called it a “very good sign.” He also gave no details about the letter he received from Vance, which Iran acknowledged last week, and said he had not responded.

Meanwhile, Vance told reporters on Monday that the Republican administration’s foremost concern is Iran agreeing to take substantive action on its nuclear program.

“We do think that there is a pathway there, but it really does require a firm commitment and a verifiable commitment that they don’t rebuild that nuclear program,” Vance added.

article_html:
WASHINGTON - Americans struggling with high prices and angry over an unpopular war with Iran began voting on Tuesday in one of the most consequential elections, widely seen as a referendum on Donald Trump’s second term.

Voters in several US states, including New York, Georgia and South Carolina, have been casting their ballots this morning, joining millions who did so before Election Day.

The stakes are high for both parties as Democrats attempt to gain control of both the House and Senate. Democrats entered Election Day with a 9-point advantage in the generic congressional ballot, according to CNN’s Poll of Polls. Meanwhile, Republicans face tests of their redistricting strategy and their grip on Senate seats in solidly red states.

225,000 loans disbursed under Apni Chhat, Apna Ghar scheme

At stake in the elections are all 435 seats of the House and 37 seats in the 100-member Senate.

Elections are also being held for the post of Governor in 36 states. On Monday, the Republicans and the Democrats made their final pitch to the voters, with Trump choosing an unusual venue the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool  to focus on the renovations undertaken in the national capital instead of talking about tax cuts, tariffs and border security, which have been the high points of his election rallies.

With more than $1.48 billion wagered on Tuesday’s US midterm elections, prediction markets such as Kalshi and Polymarket are facing their biggest test yet of how reliably they can forecast political races amid growing scrutiny of their businesses.

Punjab CM Maryam inaugurates development projects in Attock

The platforms rose to prominence in 2024 when they bucked traditional opinion polls in signaling that Donald Trump would win the presidency, and have since amassed a global following among media outlets and investors.

According to the White House, Trump did a whirlwind tour of 20 states, mostly Republican strongholds, to address 30 rallies in the last 32 days. Analysts say his approval ratings are at an all-time low, and he has become a liability to Republican candidates.

If the pre-poll forecasts come true and Democrats take control of the US Congress, it will allow for deeper Congressional scrutiny and checks of Trump’s actions, which will severely limit his ability to push his agenda. He will, however, retain the power to govern through executive orders, which will be valid for two years.

Faryal Talpur to visit Lahore ahead of LG elections

Trump acknowledged the possibility of his wings being clipped but indicated that he will not allow Congress to slow him down.

“I guess I’ll become Mr Veto,” Trump told the New York Postin response to a question on Republicans losing control of both Houses of the US Congress.

Former President Barack Obama boosted the Democratic campaign with rallies in Ohio, Michigan and Georgia, which clearly left Trump rattled.

“This election is our last, best chance of at least reining him in, reining in some of the foolishness of this administration,” Obama said in Georgia.

Over 456,000 children administered polio drops on first day

The Democrats, however, suffered an unexpected setback in the eleventh hour when Congresswoman Haley Stevens of Michigan crossed over to the Republican side on Sunday, breaking ranks with Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed, who could be the first Muslim elected to the US Senate.

The Democratic Party quickly rallied behind El-Sayed by issuing statements condemning Stevens, who sprung a surprise by endorsing El-Sayed’s Republican rival, Mike Rogers, and appearing alongside him in public.

Stevens lost in the Senate primary to El-Sayed. She is a staunch supporter of Israel, while El-Sayed is a fierce critic of the US ally.

Punjab launches ‘Chamkta Lahore’ campaign to combat smog

The Democrats are hoping to flip seven Senate seats: Michigan, Maine, Ohio, Kansas, Texas, Iowa and Alaska in their bid to gain a majority in the 100-member House.

Each of the 50 states in the United States is represented by two Senators who sit in the Congress for a six-year term. But the Senators are divided into three lots, and their terms are staggered so that elections are held every two years.

The mid-term elections are also crucial for Vice President J D Vance, who is burnishing his credentials to become a successor to Trump’s mantle.

Vance made campaign stops in New York and Ohio on Monday, where Republicans were fighting for House and Senate seats.

He highlighted Trump’s moves to end taxes on tips and overtime and secure the border while branding Democrats as “lunatics” who have contempt for American voters.

About 210 million Americans are registered to vote, according to USAFacts. California has the most registered voters, with 23.2 million, followed by Texas (17.4 million) and Florida (13.6 million). Together, they account for about 26 percent of all registered voters.

According to the AP, more than 57 million ballots have been cast in 47 states and D.C. as of Monday, with turnout surpassing the early vote four years ago in many closely watched states.

Meanwhile, The United States has launched “defensive strikes” on Iran’s Qeshm island in the Strait of Hormuz on the eve of crucial midterm elections, according to US officials.

Iranian state news agency IRNA confirmed several explosions on the island on Monday.

The US officials described the strikes as limited and said they were in response to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) firing upon a US aircraft.

The strikes appeared to be limited as opposed to a return to full hostilities but followed President Donald Trump previously saying the US wouldn’t launch strikes on Iran before Tuesday’s midterms. The strikes were reported by The Wall Street Journal and CBS News.

The unpopular Iran war and the resulting impact on US gasoline prices and other parts of the economy have been a vulnerability for Republicans as they try to keep control of Congress.

The administration was last known to have carried out some attacks in early September, but thousands of US troops remain in the waters off Iran to maintain a naval blockade aimed at preventing tankers carrying Iranian oil from getting to the global market. A third aircraft carrier and thousands of additional troops are on their way to the Middle East.

Iran’s top security official says the US response to the latest ceasefire offer was “not convincing.”

“America’s response to Iran’s rights and demands was not convincing,” writes Supreme National Security Secretary Mohsen Rezaei on X, “and they must fully and explicitly address Iran’s seven conditions and act upon them; only then will the Strait of Hormuz be reopened.”

Among Iran’s demands are a permanent end to the war, including Israel’s operations against Hamas and Hezbollah; the lifting of the US blockade on Iran; the withdrawal of US forces; lifting sanctions; paying reparations for the war; and recognizing new arrangements for shipping in Hormuz that Iran will set.

Earlier Monday, US Vice President JD Vance offered optimism that a deal can still be struck to prevent Trump from following through on his threat to potentially order new strikes on Iran after the midterm elections.

Vance sent a letter to Iran’s security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, last week, but the White House has offered scant details about the contents. Trump told reporters that the letter was focused on assisting Iran with “medical supplies and various things.”

But Vance on Monday suggested there’s reason to believe that the US and Iran could still come to an agreement.

“We’ve had a number of good conversations with the Iranians,” Vance told reporters on Monday when asked about the letter. “I actually just spoke with the president of the United States about an hour ago about this. Look, the president and I both feel pretty good about the prospects for potentially coming to a negotiated settlement. We’re going to keep on working at it.”

Vance’s comments came as the region remains on edge about the prospects of the US resuming full-scale operations against Iran. The backchannel efforts are playing out as Israel and some Middle East allies lobby Trump on the way ahead in the 8-month-old war that has rattled global markets and wreaked havoc on Iran.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is pushing for another wave of strikes on Iran after Tuesday’s elections in the United States, according to two regional officials and a third person familiar with the matter.

A return to full-scale war with Iran could help Netanyahu to form an emergency government after he and his far-right allies lost their parliamentary majority in last week’s elections. Trump has alternated between threatening major strikes and pushing for a deal with Iran.

The two officials said diplomatic efforts have made progress, with Qatari mediators holding two rounds of talks last week with Iranian officials. The two officials said the mediators are trying to advance a framework for Iran to cease its attacks in the Strait of Hormuz in return for the US lifting its blockade on Iran’s ports.

They said more talks are planned for this week. The two officials spoke on condition of anonymity because they were discussing classified briefings they had received from American and Israeli officials.

One official said Netanyahu was working with senior officials in the US administration to persuade Trump to launch a quick but extensive air campaign and that the president does not appear to have made a decision.

Netanyahu pressed for strikes during a call over the weekend with Trump, who would not commit to taking military action, according to a person who was briefed on it.

Other US allies in the Middle East are warning against more strikes, saying that would destabilize the region and could lead Iran-allied Houthi rebels in Yemen to step up their attacks on Saudi Arabia and Red Sea shipping, a third regional official said. Iran-backed militias in Iraq could also get involved.

Saudi Defense Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman said he spoke by phone on Monday with US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth about “the latest regional and international developments” and the Houthis’ continued attacks on Saudi Arabia.

Oil prices dropped sharply on Monday as renewed diplomatic efforts to end the war between the US and Iran appeared to show signs of headway. Rising prices at the pump, a byproduct of the war, have been a weight on Trump’s Republican Party as it tries to maintain control of both chambers of Congress.

Trump noted the drop in a speech in Washington on Monday, which was billed as his closing argument to Americans, and sought to minimize the scale of the conflict, which has cost US taxpayers at least $47 billion.

“I don’t know if you even call it a war, because we haven’t been doing any fighting for months,” Trump said.

Netanyahu has not commented on Iran since the Israeli election, and there was no word from his office on the latest call with Trump.

Iranian officials say publicly they are prepared for war or diplomacy.

Iran’s foreign minister Abbas Araghchi told the IRNA earlier that “very intensive” talks to try and end the war are under way with the US via mediators.

He also said Tehran was prepared for both diplomatic and military scenarios “more than ever before” and that it was up to the US to choose between a “wise path” of negotiation or the “mistake of military aggression”.

But Iran wants guarantees that the US will implement its side of any agreement. The US and Israel have twice attacked Iran while it was engaged in negotiations over its disputed nuclear program.

The new supreme leader, Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, met with Iran’s military chiefs and said the response to “any kind and level of threat” from the US or Israel should be immediate and without “geographic limits,” and urged an expansion of the list of potential targets.

A recent analysis by The Associated Press found that Iranian strikes on more than two dozen US bases since the start of the war have caused billions of dollars in equipment damage.

Iran’s security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, told state television that “the tone has completely changed” from the US and called it a “very good sign.” He also gave no details about the letter he received from Vance, which Iran acknowledged last week, and said he had not responded.

Meanwhile, Vance told reporters on Monday that the Republican administration’s foremost concern is Iran agreeing to take substantive action on its nuclear program.

“We do think that there is a pathway there, but it really does require a firm commitment and a verifiable commitment that they don’t rebuild that nuclear program,” Vance added.
