The US officials described the strikes as limited and said they were in response to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) firing upon a US aircraft.

The strikes appeared to be limited as opposed to a return to full hostilities but followed President Donald Trump previously saying the US wouldn’t launch strikes on Iran before Tuesday’s midterms. The strikes were reported by The Wall Street Journal and CBS News.
The unpopular Iran war and the resulting impact on US gasoline prices and other parts of the economy have been a vulnerability for Republicans as they try to keep control of Congress.

The administration was last known to have carried out some attacks in early September, but thousands of US troops remain in the waters off Iran to maintain a naval blockade aimed at preventing tankers carrying Iranian oil from getting to the global market. A third aircraft carrier and thousands of additional troops are on their way to the Middle East.
Iran’s top security official says the US response to the latest ceasefire offer was “not convincing.”

“America’s response to Iran’s rights and demands was not convincing,” writes Supreme National Security Secretary Mohsen Rezaei on X, “and they must fully and explicitly address Iran’s seven conditions and act upon them; only then will the Strait of Hormuz be reopened.”

Among Iran’s demands are a permanent end to the war, including Israel’s operations against Hamas and Hezbollah; the lifting of the US blockade on Iran; the withdrawal of US forces; lifting sanctions; paying reparations for the war; and recognizing new arrangements for shipping in Hormuz that Iran will set.

Earlier Monday, US Vice President JD Vance offered optimism that a deal can still be struck to prevent Trump from following through on his threat to potentially order new strikes on Iran after the midterm elections.

Vance sent a letter to Iran’s security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, last week, but the White House has offered scant details about the contents. Trump told reporters that the letter was focused on assisting Iran with “medical supplies and various things.”
But Vance on Monday suggested there’s reason to believe that the US and Iran could still come to an agreement.

“We’ve had a number of good conversations with the Iranians,” Vance told reporters on Monday when asked about the letter. “I actually just spoke with the president of the United States about an hour ago about this. Look, the president and I both feel pretty good about the prospects for potentially coming to a negotiated settlement. We’re going to keep on working at it.”

Vance’s comments came as the region remains on edge about the prospects of the US resuming full-scale operations against Iran. The backchannel efforts are playing out as Israel and some Middle East allies lobby Trump on the way ahead in the 8-month-old war that has rattled global markets and wreaked havoc on Iran.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is pushing for another wave of strikes on Iran after Tuesday’s elections in the United States, according to two regional officials and a third person familiar with the matter.

A return to full-scale war with Iran could help Netanyahu to form an emergency government after he and his far-right allies lost their parliamentary majority in last week’s elections. Trump has alternated between threatening major strikes and pushing for a deal with Iran.

The two officials said diplomatic efforts have made progress, with Qatari mediators holding two rounds of talks last week with Iranian officials. The two officials said the mediators are trying to advance a framework for Iran to cease its attacks in the Strait of Hormuz in return for the US lifting its blockade on Iran’s ports.

They said more talks are planned for this week. The two officials spoke on condition of anonymity because they were discussing classified briefings they had received from American and Israeli officials.

One official said Netanyahu was working with senior officials in the US administration to persuade Trump to launch a quick but extensive air campaign and that the president does not appear to have made a decision.
Netanyahu pressed for strikes during a call over the weekend with Trump, who would not commit to taking military action, according to a person who was briefed on it.

Other US allies in the Middle East are warning against more strikes, saying that would destabilize the region and could lead Iran-allied Houthi rebels in Yemen to step up their attacks on Saudi Arabia and Red Sea shipping, a third regional official said. Iran-backed militias in Iraq could also get involved.

Saudi Defense Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman said he spoke by phone on Monday with US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth about “the latest regional and international developments” and the Houthis’ continued attacks on Saudi Arabia.

Oil prices dropped sharply on Monday as renewed diplomatic efforts to end the war between the US and Iran appeared to show signs of headway. Rising prices at the pump, a byproduct of the war, have been a weight on Trump’s Republican Party as it tries to maintain control of both chambers of Congress.

Trump noted the drop in a speech in Washington on Monday, which was billed as his closing argument to Americans, and sought to minimize the scale of the conflict, which has cost US taxpayers at least $47 billion.
“I don’t know if you even call it a war, because we haven’t been doing any fighting for months,” Trump said.
Netanyahu has not commented on Iran since the Israeli election, and there was no word from his office on the latest call with Trump.
Iranian officials say publicly they are prepared for war or diplomacy.
Iran’s foreign minister Abbas Araghchi told the IRNA earlier that “very intensive” talks to try and end the war are under way with the US via mediators.

He also said Tehran was prepared for both diplomatic and military scenarios “more than ever before” and that it was up to the US to choose between a “wise path” of negotiation or the “mistake of military aggression”.
But Iran wants guarantees that the US will implement its side of any agreement. The US and Israel have twice attacked Iran while it was engaged in negotiations over its disputed nuclear program.

The new supreme leader, Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, met with Iran’s military chiefs and said the response to “any kind and level of threat” from the US or Israel should be immediate and without “geographic limits,” and urged an expansion of the list of potential targets.
A recent analysis by The Associated Press found that Iranian strikes on more than two dozen US bases since the start of the war have caused billions of dollars in equipment damage.

Iran’s security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, told state television that “the tone has completely changed” from the US and called it a “very good sign.” He also gave no details about the letter he received from Vance, which Iran acknowledged last week, and said he had not responded.
Meanwhile, Vance told reporters on Monday that the Republican administration’s foremost concern is Iran agreeing to take substantive action on its nuclear program.
“We do think that there is a pathway there, but it really does require a firm commitment and a verifiable commitment that they don’t rebuild that nuclear program,” Vance added.

headline: Govt assures domestic consumers of meeting gas demand in winter
description: ISLAMABAD - Amid a supply disruption caused by the closure of the Iranian border, which has pushed LPG prices to Rs700/kg, the federal government has taken
author: Fawad Yousafzai
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Amid a supply disruption caused by the closure of the Iranian border, which has pushed LPG prices to Rs700/kg, the federal government has taken swift action to end the monopoly of a few private companies by directing four state-owned companies to start importing LPG and holding transparent auctions.

Addressing a press conference in alongside Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, Federal Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik said that Pakistan State Oil (PSO), Sui Southern Gas Company, Pakistan LNG Limited and PARCO had been directed to import LPG, while local supplies would be auctioned transparently in five-tonne and 10-tonne lots.

The petroleum minister said Pakistan consumed around 2.4 million tonnes of LPG annually, with more than half met through imports. The closure of Iranian border crossings had created shortages, allowing some market players to sell LPG at Rs700-800 per kilogram, well above the international-market-based price of around Rs450.

Malik said the government will make every effort to maintain gas supply through the pipeline network during breakfast, lunch and dinner hours during the winter season. He said if necessary, additional LNG will also be imported to meet domestic requirements, while rationing can be considered if ircumstances demand. He said Pakistan’s annual LPG demand stands at approximately 2.4 million tonnes, while domestic production is around 2,000 to 2,500 tonnes per day. The remaining requirement is met through imports, including supplies previously received through the western border and sea routes.

The Minister for Petroleum said disruptions in supplies through the western border have created additional challenges, highlighting the need to diversify import sources and strengthen the country’s energy infrastructure.

He said the Prime Minister has directed the formulation of a comprehensive energy security framework, including improvements in storage facilities, refineries and LPG import infrastructure.

Ali Pervaiz Malik said the government has decided to introduce competition in the LPG sector to ensure the availability of the commodity at the lowest possible cost to consumers.

He said state-owned companies, including Pakistan State Oil, Sui gas companies and Pakistan LNG Limited, have been directed to arrange bulk LPG purchases through government-to-government and business-to-business agreements. The private sector will also be encouraged to import LPG, which will increase supply and promote competition.

The minister said all importing companies will publish details of their monthly procurement costs, including Saudi Aramco’s contract price, premiums and freight charges, on their websites to ensure transparency.

He further said the existing quota-based system for locally produced LPG will also be replaced with a transparent auction mechanism. Companies will offer the commodity in lots of five to ten tonnes, and auction results will be made public under the supervision of the relevant authorities.

Ali Pervaiz Malik said the government has also taken measures to protect low-income households from the impact of international price fluctuations. Under the LPG policy, ten percent of the quota reserved for hard areas will be distributed transparently through state-owned companies in consultation with provincial authorities.

He said additional revenue generated through the new pricing and auction mechanism will be channelled into a Price Stabilisation Fund and a Vulnerable Protection Fund to provide subsidized LPG to deserving consumers.

The minister said the Competition Commission has also been directed to prevent market manipulation and the formation of cartels, while OGRA will further improve transparency in its licensing and regulatory procedures.

The relevant authorities will also monitor the quality and safety of LPG cylinders and transportation vehicles through a track-and-trace mechanism.

Ali Pervaiz Malik estimated that the international market price of imported LPG, after including premiums and other costs, can range between 450 and 500 rupees per kilogram.

He said the government will provide targeted relief to deserving consumers through the differential fund mechanism, with subsidized rates to be determined by the Prime Minister.

Speaking on the occasion, Attaullah Tarar said Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has placed the protection of public interests at the forefront during the ongoing crisis. He said the government did not allow any additional burden to fall on the people.

The minister said the government has also decided to promote competition in the liquefied petroleum gas sector to facilitate consumers.

He said the government transferred profits earned by refineries to the public, adding that such an initiative has never been undertaken in the country’s history. Attaullah Tarar said all measures taken by the Prime Minister are aimed at providing relief to the people.

headline: 2 policemen guarding polio workers shot dead in KP’s Mohmand
description: PESHAWAR - Gunmen riding a motorcycle shot and killed two police officers assigned to protect polio workers during a door-to-door vaccination campaign Tuesday
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
PESHAWAR - Gunmen riding a motorcycle shot and killed two police officers assigned to protect polio workers during a door-to-door vaccination campaign Tuesday in Mohmand district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, officials said.

The drive-by shooting in Mohmand district that borders Afghanistan also wounded a third police official.

The policemen were traveling to a nearby village to guard vaccination teams when they came under fire, police officer Ayaz Khan told reporters.

The attackers fled the scene. No group immediately claimed responsibility for the attack.

The Pakistani Taliban regularly target anti-polio drives and police protecting health workers, falsely claiming that polio vaccination campaigns are part of a Western conspiracy to sterilize children.

headline: Three-day 10th Pakistan Industrial Expo to begin on 14th
description: LAHORE - The 10th Pakistan Industrial Expo (PIE 2026) will be held from November 14 to 16 at Expo Centre Lahore, bringing together Pakistani and Chinese
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: LAHORE - The 10th Pakistan Industrial Expo (PIE 2026) will be held from November 14 to 16 at Expo Centre Lahore, bringing together Pakistani and Chinese manufacturers, investors and technology providers to promote industrial cooperation, technology transfer and investment opportunities. The details of the three-day exhibition were shared at a press conference, where organisers and industry representatives highlighted its focus on emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI), robotics, industrial automation, CNC machinery and smart manufacturing. Fa Wenyan, CEO of Everest International Expo (China), said the Pakistan Industrial Expo had served as a bridge between Pakistani industries and Chinese manufacturing expertise since 2017. He said the 10th edition would further strengthen cooperation in technology transfer, local manufacturing, investment and employment generation.

headline: Pakistan successfully tests first indigenously developed air-to-air missile Fa’az
description: ISLAMABAD - Pakistan on Tuesday conducted successful flight test of first indigenously developed Fa’az air-to-air missile. According to a press release
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Pakistan on Tuesday conducted successful flight test of first indigenously developed Fa’az air-to-air missile. According to a press release issued by the Inter-Services Public Relation (ISPR), it marks another significant milestone in the advancement of national aerospace and defense capabilities.

The missile is equipped with state of the art terminal guidance system, it can engage enemy aerial targets at longer ranges. Fa’az will significantly enhance operational flexibility of Pakistan Air Force, further strengthening the country’s overall defense posture.

The successful flight test underscores the technical maturity, innovation and self-reliance achieved by Pakistan’s defense industry.

The launch was witnessed by senior officers of the Pakistan Armed Forces, along with distinguished scientists and engineers who played a pivotal role in the development of this advanced weapon system.

The President, the Prime Minister of Pakistan, Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defense Forces and Services Chiefs congratulated the scientists and engineers on this remarkable achievement.

headline: UK, Pakistani bank launch fully funded Chevening scholarships for Pak students
description: ISLAMABAD - The United Kingdom and Allied Bank Limited (ABL) yesterday launched a landmark scholarship partnership to enable talented Pakistanis to pursue
author: SHAFQAT ALI
article_text: ISLAMABAD - The United Kingdom and Allied Bank Limited (ABL) yesterday launched a landmark scholarship partnership to enable talented Pakistanis to pursue fully funded master’s degrees at leading British universities, opening new opportunities for higher education and professional development. Under the Chevening-ABL Scholarship programme, two Pakistani scholars will receive financial support annually over three academic years, beginning in 2027-28, to study disciplines critical to Pakistan’s future development, including artificial intelligence, technology, cybersecurity, digital transformation, economics and financial inclusion. Allied Bank has become the first organisation in Pakistan to establish a locally funded Chevening Scholarship partnership, bringing together the UK Government’s flagship international scholarship programme and Pakistan’s private sector to invest in emerging national leadership. British High Commissioner Jane Marriott said Pakistan’s greatest strength was its people and expressed confidence that the partnership would enable promising future leaders to study at world-leading British universities and bring innovative ideas and expertise back home. “It is especially fitting that a former Chevening Scholar is now opening the same door for the next generation,” she said. The first two Chevening-ABL scholars will be selected from the existing applicant pool for the 2027-28 academic year. Applications for the 2028-29 Chevening-ABL Scholarships are expected to open in August 2027 alongside the regular Chevening application cycle, with successful candidates commencing their studies in the United Kingdom in 2028.

headline: CM Maryam sends Rs 5b defamation notice to federal minister Salik over corruption allegations
description: LAHORE - Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif has served a legal notice on Federal Minister for Overseas Pakistanis and Human Resource Development
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
LAHORE - Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif has served a legal notice on Federal Minister for Overseas Pakistanis and Human Resource Development Chaudhry Salik Hussain, demanding withdrawal of his allegations of widespread corruption in Punjab and payment of Rs5 billion in damages for what she described as defamatory remarks.

The legal notice, issued through Additional Advocate General Punjab Ch Muhammad Nawaz, has also been served on ARY News anchor Naeem Ashraf Butt, who interviewed the federal minister, and ARY Chairman Muhammad Iqbal for facilitating and broadcasting the allegedly defamatory statements.

The notice relates to an interview with Chaudhry Salik Hussain broadcast on ARY News on November 2, 2026, in which the federal minister made remarks about alleged corruption in Punjab. During the interview, he reportedly said: “I do not have evidence, but I hear stories about corruption in Punjab every day,” adding that “cupboards, not files, are filled with corruption cases in Punjab.”

According to the legal notice, the minister made sweeping allegations about corruption in the provincial administration despite admitting that he possessed no evidence to substantiate them.

It maintains that the remarks created an impression among viewers that corruption was widespread across the provincial administration, without identifying any particular department, public office, official, project, transaction or inquiry to support the claims.

The notice argues that a federal minister is expected to exercise responsibility while making allegations against another constitutional government and cannot convert hearsay into apparent facts or make sweeping accusations without credible evidence. It also holds the ARY News anchor responsible for introducing and pursuing the subject without seeking clarification or demanding documentary evidence from the interviewee. The notice says responsible journalism required the host to establish the factual basis of such serious allegations before broadcasting them.

The ARY chairman has also been made a recipient of the notice for facilitating and broadcasting the interview. Describing the remarks as false, baseless and defamatory, the chief minister maintains that they have undermined public confidence in the integrity of the Punjab government and her leadership.

The notice acknowledges the importance of freedom of expression, responsible journalism and the right of public representatives to question government performance. However, it argues that these rights do not provide an unrestricted licence to circulate unverified allegations or damage the reputation of others through unsupported assertions.

Maryam Nawaz has given the three recipients seven days to withdraw and unequivocally retract the allegations, publish an unconditional apology and clarification on the same media platforms with prominence equivalent to the original broadcast, and remove or correct the allegedly defamatory portions of the interview and related clips.

She has also demanded Rs5 billion in damages for the alleged harm to her reputation. The notice further directs the recipients to preserve the complete original interview, unedited footage, audio recordings, editorial notes, publication records, relevant communications and available broadcast analytics for possible use in legal proceedings.

It warns that failure to comply with the demands within seven days will compel the chief minister to initiate legal proceedings, including under the Punjab Defamation Act, 2024, before the competent forum. The notice stated that it has been issued without prejudice to any other legal remedies available to the chief minister under the Constitution and laws of Pakistan.

Earlier, addressing a laptop and Honhaar Scholarship distribution ceremony at COMSATS University, Attock, Maryam Nawaz Sharif on Tuesday announced that she was sending a defamation notice to Federal Minister Chaudhry Salik Hussain over his allegations of corruption against the Punjab government, challenging him to produce evidence to substantiate his claims.

The chief minister stated the federal minister from Gujrat had alleged that cupboards in Punjab were filled with money earned through corruption. She termed the allegations baseless and said she would serve a legal action on him.

“Trillions of rupees are being invested in development projects in Punjab, with individual projects worth Rs300 billion each. I can take an oath before these children that I have not committed corruption of even a single rupee,” she said.

Maryam Nawaz said she was answerable to the people and Allah Almighty if any wrongdoing was established, challenging those making allegations to provide evidence instead of spreading accusations.

“If you have evidence, bring it forth — otherwise I will drag you to court,” she warned, questioning why the federal minister continued to serve in a government that he himself considered corrupt.

The chief minister alleged that Salik’s criticism had little to do with corruption or development, claiming that he was unhappy over her decision to replace the deputy commissioner of Gujrat a few days ago. She said the federal minister wanted an officer of his choice appointed to the post.

“I do not appoint deputy commissioners on recommendations because that would amount to a breach of trust. Those appointed through recommendations undermine the country,” she said.

Maryam also took exception to Salik’s remarks describing former Punjab chief minister Chaudhry Pervez Elahi as the best-ever chief minister of the province. Defending her government’s performance in Gujrat, she criticised the state of drainage and infrastructure in the city during Elahi’s tenure. Recalling a visit to Gujrat around two years ago, she said the city had been badly affected by rainwater accumulation, with even her Land Cruiser becoming submerged.

“The Gujrat that Pervez Elahi handed me — I went there about two years ago and it was raining. Believe me, the water was up to here,” she said, gesturing towards her neck. “My Land Cruiser was completely submerged,” she added.

She said Gujrat had previously looked more like a village than a developed city, but the situation had now improved considerably. “Now, when it rains, rainwater does not accumulate. That work was not done by the Chaudhrys,” she said.

The chief minister said the Punjab government was distributing laptops and scholarships purely on merit, without discrimination on the basis of political affiliation, recommendations or money.

Turning to the students receiving laptops and Honhaar Scholarships, Maryam Nawaz congratulated them and said she had personally travelled to Attock as a mother to celebrate their achievements. She described the scholarship recipients as the cream of Punjab, saying their success was the result of hard work and perseverance.

“Parents feel immense pride when their children succeed. These students are receiving the reward of their hard work and are entitled to it. There is no need for them to express gratitude; they should claim their rightful due with dignity,” she said.

She said she had come to present her government’s performance report rather than point out the shortcomings of others.

Recalling the struggles of scholarship recipients, she cited the example of a girl whose financial difficulties following her mother’s death had been resolved through the Honhaar Scholarship. She also met a student whose father was a labourer and who was delighted to receive the financial assistance.

She said many talented students in the past had been forced to discontinue their education because of financial constraints, but no student would now be deprived of education for lack of funds.

The chief minister announced that an electric bike scheme for students would also be launched in the coming days, with pink bikes for girls and black bikes for boys, to facilitate their daily commute.

She said the law and order situation had been improved to ensure the safety of girls travelling independently on motorcycles. “Every son and daughter in Punjab enjoys a sense of security. Everyone knows that they are safe in Punjab. Punjab is the only province providing laptops, scholarships and electric bikes to students,” she said, adding that the province also honoured its students with a Guard of Honour.

Maryam Nawaz said development appeared to come to a halt as soon as one crossed Punjab’s borders, where colleges, roads and public transport facilities were lacking.

“I am not a mother who merely points out problems; I work day and night to resolve them,” she remarked.

She also expressed satisfaction over educational initiatives in Attock, saying she was delighted to see a Grammar School alongside a Nawaz Sharif School of Eminence upon entering the district.

She said 300 Nawaz Sharif Schools of Eminence were being established across Punjab, equipped with air-conditioned classrooms, artificial intelligence labs and science laboratories. Describing the initiative as an educational revolution, she claimed that the standard of these institutions was even better than that of grammar schools.

The chief minister said she loved every child of Punjab as much as her own children and shared a special emotional bond with them. She recalled how a student in Mandi Bahauddin had told her that she was crying with happiness because she wanted to meet her.

“This is a relationship of love and affection, a bond of hearts. Those who indulge in unnecessary criticism cannot understand this relationship between me and the children,” she said, adding that she would respond to their affection with even greater love.

She urged students not to lose heart in the face of criticism, saying success required hard work, perseverance and the ability to overcome challenges.

Maryam Nawaz said 850 kilometres of roads had been constructed in Attock alone. She also referred to the introduction of Green Buses, establishment of bus terminals, free medicines in hospitals and free treatment facilities as part of the government’s initiatives.

She said loans had been disbursed for the construction of 250,000 houses across Punjab. Citing the example of a retired subedar who owned a plot but lacked resources to build a house, she said he had been able to construct his home after receiving a loan of Rs1.5 million.

The chief minister said Attock had received little attention in the past and had looked more like a village than a city. However, a new market had now been developed, while billions of rupees had been spent on sewerage and drainage projects to address the city’s longstanding flooding problem.

She also ordered the provision of transport for the University of Engineering and Technology (UET), Taxila. The chief minister urged students to respect their parents and never speak rudely to them, even when angry. She asked them to express gratitude to their parents for their sacrifices and said respecting parents brought blessings and honour.

She also sought a commitment from students to keep their streets, neighbourhoods, buses and cities clean. She said 200,000 workers were engaged in the Suthra Punjab programme, but even two million workers would not be able to maintain cleanliness if people continued throwing garbage in public places.

Calling for public cooperation, she urged citizens to take responsibility for keeping their surroundings clean. The chief minister also asked young people to pledge that they would never take up arms against their country and nation, regardless of what others said.

“I have heard people saying, ‘What is there in Pakistan?’ I say that everything is in Pakistan,” she said, urging students never to allow the national flag to be lowered. She prayed that Allah Almighty would bless Pakistan with progress and prosperity and enable the young generation to fulfil their parents’ dreams.

LAHORE - Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif has served a legal notice on Federal Minister for Overseas Pakistanis and Human Resource Development Chaudhry Salik Hussain, demanding withdrawal of his allegations of widespread corruption in Punjab and payment of Rs5 billion in damages for what she described as defamatory remarks.

The legal notice, issued through Additional Advocate General Punjab Ch Muhammad Nawaz, has also been served on ARY News anchor Naeem Ashraf Butt, who interviewed the federal minister, and ARY Chairman Muhammad Iqbal for facilitating and broadcasting the allegedly defamatory statements.

225,000 loans disbursed under Apni Chhat, Apna Ghar scheme

The notice relates to an interview with Chaudhry Salik Hussain broadcast on ARY News on November 2, 2026, in which the federal minister made remarks about alleged corruption in Punjab. During the interview, he reportedly said: “I do not have evidence, but I hear stories about corruption in Punjab every day,” adding that “cupboards, not files, are filled with corruption cases in Punjab.”

According to the legal notice, the minister made sweeping allegations about corruption in the provincial administration despite admitting that he possessed no evidence to substantiate them.

Punjab CM Maryam inaugurates development projects in Attock

It maintains that the remarks created an impression among viewers that corruption was widespread across the provincial administration, without identifying any particular department, public office, official, project, transaction or inquiry to support the claims.

The notice argues that a federal minister is expected to exercise responsibility while making allegations against another constitutional government and cannot convert hearsay into apparent facts or make sweeping accusations without credible evidence. It also holds the ARY News anchor responsible for introducing and pursuing the subject without seeking clarification or demanding documentary evidence from the interviewee. The notice says responsible journalism required the host to establish the factual basis of such serious allegations before broadcasting them.

Faryal Talpur to visit Lahore ahead of LG elections

The ARY chairman has also been made a recipient of the notice for facilitating and broadcasting the interview. Describing the remarks as false, baseless and defamatory, the chief minister maintains that they have undermined public confidence in the integrity of the Punjab government and her leadership.

The notice acknowledges the importance of freedom of expression, responsible journalism and the right of public representatives to question government performance. However, it argues that these rights do not provide an unrestricted licence to circulate unverified allegations or damage the reputation of others through unsupported assertions.

Over 456,000 children administered polio drops on first day

Maryam Nawaz has given the three recipients seven days to withdraw and unequivocally retract the allegations, publish an unconditional apology and clarification on the same media platforms with prominence equivalent to the original broadcast, and remove or correct the allegedly defamatory portions of the interview and related clips.

She has also demanded Rs5 billion in damages for the alleged harm to her reputation. The notice further directs the recipients to preserve the complete original interview, unedited footage, audio recordings, editorial notes, publication records, relevant communications and available broadcast analytics for possible use in legal proceedings.

Punjab launches ‘Chamkta Lahore’ campaign to combat smog

It warns that failure to comply with the demands within seven days will compel the chief minister to initiate legal proceedings, including under the Punjab Defamation Act, 2024, before the competent forum. The notice stated that it has been issued without prejudice to any other legal remedies available to the chief minister under the Constitution and laws of Pakistan.

Earlier, addressing a laptop and Honhaar Scholarship distribution ceremony at COMSATS University, Attock, Maryam Nawaz Sharif on Tuesday announced that she was sending a defamation notice to Federal Minister Chaudhry Salik Hussain over his allegations of corruption against the Punjab government, challenging him to produce evidence to substantiate his claims.

The chief minister stated the federal minister from Gujrat had alleged that cupboards in Punjab were filled with money earned through corruption. She termed the allegations baseless and said she would serve a legal action on him.

“Trillions of rupees are being invested in development projects in Punjab, with individual projects worth Rs300 billion each. I can take an oath before these children that I have not committed corruption of even a single rupee,” she said.

Maryam Nawaz said she was answerable to the people and Allah Almighty if any wrongdoing was established, challenging those making allegations to provide evidence instead of spreading accusations.

“If you have evidence, bring it forth — otherwise I will drag you to court,” she warned, questioning why the federal minister continued to serve in a government that he himself considered corrupt.

The chief minister alleged that Salik’s criticism had little to do with corruption or development, claiming that he was unhappy over her decision to replace the deputy commissioner of Gujrat a few days ago. She said the federal minister wanted an officer of his choice appointed to the post.

“I do not appoint deputy commissioners on recommendations because that would amount to a breach of trust. Those appointed through recommendations undermine the country,” she said.

Maryam also took exception to Salik’s remarks describing former Punjab chief minister Chaudhry Pervez Elahi as the best-ever chief minister of the province. Defending her government’s performance in Gujrat, she criticised the state of drainage and infrastructure in the city during Elahi’s tenure. Recalling a visit to Gujrat around two years ago, she said the city had been badly affected by rainwater accumulation, with even her Land Cruiser becoming submerged.

“The Gujrat that Pervez Elahi handed me — I went there about two years ago and it was raining. Believe me, the water was up to here,” she said, gesturing towards her neck. “My Land Cruiser was completely submerged,” she added.

She said Gujrat had previously looked more like a village than a developed city, but the situation had now improved considerably. “Now, when it rains, rainwater does not accumulate. That work was not done by the Chaudhrys,” she said.

The chief minister said the Punjab government was distributing laptops and scholarships purely on merit, without discrimination on the basis of political affiliation, recommendations or money.

Turning to the students receiving laptops and Honhaar Scholarships, Maryam Nawaz congratulated them and said she had personally travelled to Attock as a mother to celebrate their achievements. She described the scholarship recipients as the cream of Punjab, saying their success was the result of hard work and perseverance.

“Parents feel immense pride when their children succeed. These students are receiving the reward of their hard work and are entitled to it. There is no need for them to express gratitude; they should claim their rightful due with dignity,” she said.

She said she had come to present her government’s performance report rather than point out the shortcomings of others.

Recalling the struggles of scholarship recipients, she cited the example of a girl whose financial difficulties following her mother’s death had been resolved through the Honhaar Scholarship. She also met a student whose father was a labourer and who was delighted to receive the financial assistance.

She said many talented students in the past had been forced to discontinue their education because of financial constraints, but no student would now be deprived of education for lack of funds.

The chief minister announced that an electric bike scheme for students would also be launched in the coming days, with pink bikes for girls and black bikes for boys, to facilitate their daily commute.

She said the law and order situation had been improved to ensure the safety of girls travelling independently on motorcycles. “Every son and daughter in Punjab enjoys a sense of security. Everyone knows that they are safe in Punjab. Punjab is the only province providing laptops, scholarships and electric bikes to students,” she said, adding that the province also honoured its students with a Guard of Honour.

Maryam Nawaz said development appeared to come to a halt as soon as one crossed Punjab’s borders, where colleges, roads and public transport facilities were lacking.

“I am not a mother who merely points out problems; I work day and night to resolve them,” she remarked.

She also expressed satisfaction over educational initiatives in Attock, saying she was delighted to see a Grammar School alongside a Nawaz Sharif School of Eminence upon entering the district.

She said 300 Nawaz Sharif Schools of Eminence were being established across Punjab, equipped with air-conditioned classrooms, artificial intelligence labs and science laboratories. Describing the initiative as an educational revolution, she claimed that the standard of these institutions was even better than that of grammar schools.

The chief minister said she loved every child of Punjab as much as her own children and shared a special emotional bond with them. She recalled how a student in Mandi Bahauddin had told her that she was crying with happiness because she wanted to meet her.

“This is a relationship of love and affection, a bond of hearts. Those who indulge in unnecessary criticism cannot understand this relationship between me and the children,” she said, adding that she would respond to their affection with even greater love.

She urged students not to lose heart in the face of criticism, saying success required hard work, perseverance and the ability to overcome challenges.

Maryam Nawaz said 850 kilometres of roads had been constructed in Attock alone. She also referred to the introduction of Green Buses, establishment of bus terminals, free medicines in hospitals and free treatment facilities as part of the government’s initiatives.

She said loans had been disbursed for the construction of 250,000 houses across Punjab. Citing the example of a retired subedar who owned a plot but lacked resources to build a house, she said he had been able to construct his home after receiving a loan of Rs1.5 million.

The chief minister said Attock had received little attention in the past and had looked more like a village than a city. However, a new market had now been developed, while billions of rupees had been spent on sewerage and drainage projects to address the city’s longstanding flooding problem.

She also ordered the provision of transport for the University of Engineering and Technology (UET), Taxila. The chief minister urged students to respect their parents and never speak rudely to them, even when angry. She asked them to express gratitude to their parents for their sacrifices and said respecting parents brought blessings and honour.

She also sought a commitment from students to keep their streets, neighbourhoods, buses and cities clean. She said 200,000 workers were engaged in the Suthra Punjab programme, but even two million workers would not be able to maintain cleanliness if people continued throwing garbage in public places.

Calling for public cooperation, she urged citizens to take responsibility for keeping their surroundings clean. The chief minister also asked young people to pledge that they would never take up arms against their country and nation, regardless of what others said.

“I have heard people saying, ‘What is there in Pakistan?’ I say that everything is in Pakistan,” she said, urging students never to allow the national flag to be lowered. She prayed that Allah Almighty would bless Pakistan with progress and prosperity and enable the young generation to fulfil their parents’ dreams.

article_text:
ISLAMABAD - A parliamentary panel has appointed a four-member sub-committee to investigate the non-completion of K-IV project despite huge expenditure.

The 14th meeting of the Standing Committee on Water Resources, which was held here under the chairmanship of Ahmad Atteeq Anwer, MNA, was informed that the WAPDA Act, 1958 presently contains no statutory provisions regarding the creation, jurisdiction, powers, or functions of the security setup. After discussion, the committee decided to defer consideration of the Bill until its next meeting.

The committee appointed a four member sub-committee under the convenorship of Muhammad Idrees “to investigate the non-completion of K-IV project despite huge expenditure incurred”. The committee directed the authorities concerned to clarify whether the issue of water theft from the Kachhi Canal had been reported to the relevant departments and whether any action had been taken to address the matter. The committee further directed that a detailed report on the status of the matter and the action taken be submitted to the committee within one week.

The following MNAs namely Muhammad Idrees, Mian Khan Bugti, Mir Munawar Ali Talpur, Waseem Qadir, Saba Talpur, Zulfiqar Ali Behan, (On Zoom), Syed Javed Ali Shah Jillani, (On Zoom), Amin Ul Haque (Mover), Mian Muhammad Mueen Watto (Federal Minister for Water Resources) and Rana Ansar (Preliminary Secretary) besides the officials of the Ministry of Water Resources attended the meeting.

headline: PTI infighting deepens after loss of KP stronghold
description: ISLAMABAD - After losing power in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on October 11, the opposition Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) is struggling to maintain its organisational
author: Imran Mukhtar
article_text: ISLAMABAD - After losing power in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on October 11, the opposition Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) is struggling to maintain its organisational cohesion both in the province and at the centre, as internal divisions within the party increasingly spill out into the open. The latest accusations came from PTI leader and former KP information adviser Barrister Muhammad Ali Saif when he, in a television interview, targeted several senior figures in the party. The interim party chairman Gohar Ali Khan rejected all these allegations, calling them baseless. Saif alleged that the current leadership including Gohar, Asad Qaiser and opposition leader in the Senate Raja Nasir Abbas was responsible for the circumstances PTI was facing. He also accused opposition alliance chief Mehmood Khan Achakzai for his failure to pursue negotiations with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif for PTI founder Imran Khan’s release, despite being given the role of leader of the opposition in the National Assembly for that purpose. Last month, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja and his party colleague and former chief minister Ali Amin Gandapur had traded barbs amid speculations of a forward bloc within their parliamentary party of KP. Raja hinted that a group was making plans to revolt against the central leadership, adding that unity of the party was at stake. Referring to reports, he said 68 PTI members of the KP Assembly were going to announce the new provincial party president and the candidate for the next chief minister without the approval of jailed party founder Imran Khan and the Political Committee—one of the highest-level decision-making bodies of the party. His remarks had come days after the federal government had imposed an emergency and governor’s rule in KP, making the PTI-led provincial government dysfunctional. In his response, Gandapur termed the statement by Raja “regrettable, irresponsible and damaging” to the internal unity of the PTI. Making vague allegations against his party’s own elected representatives was unbecoming of any responsible leader at a time when the PTI was facing extraordinary political challenges, he said. Infighting within the PTI is not new, as the party has grappled with internal rivalries even when its chief Khan was at the helm. These rifts have become increasingly visible since his incarceration. The situation has been further compounded by the loss of the party’s last remaining stronghold following the collapse of its provincial government. Although the Political Committee has recently dismissed claims of internal divisions within the PTI, the growing differences within its ranks are no longer difficult to discern. These divisions have also hampered the party’s ability to formulate an effective political response to the evolving situation, even three weeks after its provincial government was rendered dysfunctional. As the party struggles to restore order within its ranks, the uncertainty is taking a toll on its activists and workers, many of whom are already exhausted and looking to the central leadership for direction. Several hardcore members of the PTI have been critical of the central leaders, calling on them to step down and make way for individuals with greater political wisdom and acumen.

headline: Rescue 1122 releases monthly performance report of last month
description: Rahim Yar Khan - Rescue 1122 Rahim Yar Khan has released its monthly performance report for October 2026. According to the report, a total of 32,341 phone
author: IHSAN UL HAQ
article_text:
Rahim Yar Khan - Rescue 1122 Rahim Yar Khan has released its monthly performance report for October 2026. According to the report, a total of 32,341 phone calls were received at the Rescue 1122 Control Room during the month, out of which only 7,327 were emergency calls. Among the total calls, 23,735 were fake, irrelevant or unnecessary calls and 459 were distorted, blank or dropped calls, making a total of 24,194 such calls. Besides, 803 calls were for seeking information and 18 were wrong calls. The emergency incidents included 891 road traffic accidents, 5,479 other emergencies including mostly medical emergencies, 50 fire incidents, 94 incidents of crime, violence and gunshot injuries, 5 drowning incidents and 610 miscellaneous emergencies. On average, 236 emergency calls were responded to daily. The general average response time remained 9 minutes, while the average response time for fire emergencies was 8 minutes. Overall, Rescue 1122 provided service to 7,246 victims. 2,215 victims were provided first aid at the spot, 4,791 patients were shifted to hospitals after medical aid, while 240 persons were found dead on the spot. According to the report, a total of 1,089 road traffic accidents occurred in all four tehsils of the district, in which 1,225 persons were affected. Among the victims, 933 were men and 292 were women. 18 persons died, 466 victims were in stable condition and 741 were in unstable condition. The vehicles involved in the accidents included 1,296 motorcycles, 95 motorcycle rickshaws, 76 cars, 74 other vehicles, 43 rickshaws, 31 trucks, 28 tractor-trolleys, 22 vans and 8 buses. Among the victims, 752 were drivers, 367 passengers and 106 pedestrians, while 76 underage drivers were also recorded in the statistics. Age-wise, 330 victims were of 21 to 30 years, 276 of 11 to 20 years, 218 of 31 to 40 years, 166 of 41 to 50 years, 130 of 51 to 60 years, 52 above 60 years and 53 of 1 to 10 years.

Regarding injuries, 1,070 received minor injuries, 84 deep injuries, 38 single fractures, 22 head injuries and 11 multiple fractures.

Major causes of accidents included 669 due to negligence and carelessness, 144 due to over-speeding, 39 due to wrong turn, 6 due to U-turn, 8 due to tyre burst and 223 due to other reasons.

According to the report, Tehsil Rahim Yar Khan witnessed the highest number of traffic accidents, while motorcyclists and youth were prominently affected in overall statistics.

Rescue 1122 appealed to the citizens to follow traffic rules, wear helmets while riding motorcycles, avoid over-speeding and careless driving and ensure safety of their own and others’ lives during driving.

As per report

Rescue 1122 transferred 1,192 persons from small hospitals to big hospitals across the district. Among patients referred by doctors, 50 were from Rahim Yar Khan, 508 from Sadiqabad, 393 from Khanpur, 241 from Liaqatpur and 148 patients were shifted to hospitals of other districts outside the district.

To maintain fitness of rescuers, monthly physical tests, races, competitions and written tests were conducted. Knowledge was enhanced through online examinations of professional skills. A monthly Darbar was held in which problems faced by rescuers during emergencies were heard and steps were taken for their immediate solution.

Rahim Yar Khan - Rescue 1122 Rahim Yar Khan has released its monthly performance report for October 2026. According to the report, a total of 32,341 phone calls were received at the Rescue 1122 Control Room during the month, out of which only 7,327 were emergency calls.  Among the total calls, 23,735 were fake, irrelevant or unnecessary calls and 459 were distorted, blank or dropped calls, making a total of 24,194 such calls. Besides, 803 calls were for seeking information and 18 were wrong calls. The emergency incidents included 891 road traffic accidents, 5,479 other emergencies including mostly medical emergencies, 50 fire incidents, 94 incidents of crime, violence and gunshot injuries, 5 drowning incidents and 610 miscellaneous emergencies. On average, 236 emergency calls were responded to daily. The general average response time remained 9 minutes, while the average response time for fire emergencies was 8 minutes. Overall, Rescue 1122 provided service to 7,246 victims. 2,215 victims were provided first aid at the spot, 4,791 patients were shifted to hospitals after medical aid, while 240 persons were found dead on the spot. According to the report, a total of 1,089 road traffic accidents occurred in all four tehsils of the district, in which 1,225 persons were affected. Among the victims, 933 were men and 292 were women. 18 persons died, 466 victims were in stable condition and 741 were in unstable condition. The vehicles involved in the accidents included 1,296 motorcycles, 95 motorcycle rickshaws, 76 cars, 74 other vehicles, 43 rickshaws, 31 trucks, 28 tractor-trolleys, 22 vans and 8 buses. Among the victims, 752 were drivers, 367 passengers and 106 pedestrians, while 76 underage drivers were also recorded in the statistics. Age-wise, 330 victims were of 21 to 30 years, 276 of 11 to 20 years, 218 of 31 to 40 years, 166 of 41 to 50 years, 130 of 51 to 60 years, 52 above 60 years and 53 of 1 to 10 years.

Regarding injuries, 1,070 received minor injuries, 84 deep injuries, 38 single fractures, 22 head injuries and 11 multiple fractures.

Major causes of accidents included 669 due to negligence and carelessness, 144 due to over-speeding, 39 due to wrong turn, 6 due to U-turn, 8 due to tyre burst and 223 due to other reasons.

According to the report, Tehsil Rahim Yar Khan witnessed the highest number of traffic accidents, while motorcyclists and youth were prominently affected in overall statistics.

Rescue 1122 appealed to the citizens to follow traffic rules, wear helmets while riding motorcycles, avoid over-speeding and careless driving and ensure safety of their own and others’ lives during driving.

headline: Pakistan, Kazakhstan seek stronger trade, investment, connectivity ties
description: ISLAMABAD - Pakistan and Kazakhstan reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening bilateral economic relations, increasing trade and exploring new investment
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text: ISLAMABAD - Pakistan and Kazakhstan reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening bilateral economic relations, increasing trade and exploring new investment opportunities during a meeting between Federal Minister for Investment Qaiser Ahmad Sheikh and Kazakhstan’s Deputy Prime Minister Sirjan Zhomangarin. During the meeting, Sheikh emphasized the need to promote business-to-business (B2B) cooperation, enhance private-sector engagement and improve banking channels to facilitate trade and investment. He highlighted opportunities in e-commerce, warehousing, textiles and mining, noting that Kazakhstan’s affordable energy could attract Pakistani investment in the textile sector, said a release issued here on Tuesday. Referring to the MoUs signed during President Asif Ali Zardari’s visit to Kazakhstan in February, Sheikh stressed the need for their early implementation to translate commitments into tangible economic benefits. Kazakhstan’s Deputy Prime Minister expressed his desire for Pakistan’s Prime Minister to visit Kazakhstan and reaffirmed his country’s commitment to strengthening bilateral relations. He emphasized the need to increase bilateral trade and said a five-year roadmap had been developed to advance cooperation. He noted that Pakistan’s market of approximately 250 million people offered significant opportunities for Kazakhstan, while Pakistan could use Kazakhstan as a gateway to the wider Eurasian market. The Deputy Prime Minister also highlighted the need for direct air connectivity between Pakistan and Kazakhstan to facilitate business, trade and people-to-people exchanges. He informed that Kazakhstan’s Foreign Minister would visit Pakistan to attend the preparatory meeting for the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO). Both sides emphasized the importance of stronger connectivity, effective implementation of existing agreements and greater private-sector engagement to transform the potential of bilateral relations into concrete economic partnerships.

headline: Mikaeel makes history again for Pakistan, wins ITF J100 singles title
description: LAHORE (Staff Reporter): Pakistan’s rising tennis star Mikaeel Ali Baig has made history once again, capturing the prestigious ITF J100 Kuala Lumpur
author: The Nation
article_text:
LAHORE (Staff Reporter): Pakistan’s rising tennis star Mikaeel Ali Baig has made history once again, capturing the prestigious ITF J100 Kuala Lumpur singles championship with a command-ing display of skill, determination and dominance. Entering the tournament as the fifth seed, the 17-year-old delivered an exceptional perfor-mance throughout the week, culminating in a stunning 6-0, 6-1 victory over Japan’s second seed Sota Kagawa in the championship final.

The triumph marked Mikaeel’s eighth ITF junior singles title, bringing his remarkable career tally to 16 international titles, eight singles and eight doubles championships. Mikaeel’s road to the championship was marked by impressive victories over some of the tournament’s strongest contenders.

In the semifinals, he defeated Japan’s top seed Yuta Amano 7-5, 6-2, displaying exceptional composure, tactical maturity and aggressive baseline tennis. In the quarterfinals, he produced a flawless performance against Russia’s third seed Ivan Makarov, winning 6-0, 6-0. Earlier, he overcame Japan’s Mao Tazuru 7-6(5), 6-1 and India’s Arya Venkataragavan 6-0, 6-0.

His dominance continued in the final, where he conceded just one game against the second seed to secure the J100 crown. Mikaeel’s triumph represents a significant milestone for Pakistani jun-ior tennis and is believed to rank among the country’s most notable international junior singles achievements since the junior career of Pakistan tennis legend Aisam-ul-Haq Qureshi.

The achievement is particularly significant given the strength of the international field and his commanding victories over the tournament’s top two seeds. The Kuala Lumpur title follows an-other major accomplishment during his ongoing Asian tour, where he recently captured the ITF J200 doubles championship in Miki, Japan.

He also reached the singles and doubles semifinals at the J100 tournament in Kawaguchi, Japan, and advanced to the third round of the prestigious J300 tournament in Wanju, South Korea.

Currently Pakistan’s No. 1 internationally ranked junior, Mikaeel has steadily climbed the ITF world junior rankings through consistent performances against leading international competi-tors. His impressive record includes three consecutive ITF junior singles titles in Pakistan in 2025, a doubles championship at the USTA Winter National Championships in the United States, and a gold medal for Pakistan at the 2025 Junior Davis Cup Asia/Oceania pre-qualifying event in Ku-ching, Malaysia.

With 16 ITF titles at just 17 years of age, Mikaeel continues to establish himself as one of Paki-stan’s most promising young tennis talents, demonstrating the ability to compete and succeed against elite junior players on the international stage.

His latest triumph in Kuala Lumpur is not only a personal milestone but also a proud moment for Pakistan, reinforcing the country’s potential to produce champions capable of making their mark on the world tennis stage.

headline: Floodlights installed at Larkana Basketball Court
description: LAHORE - The Sindh Basketball Association (SBBA) has appreciated the Sindh Sports Department for installing floodlights at the basketball court of Khuhro
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - The Sindh Basketball Association (SBBA) has appreciated the Sindh Sports Department for installing floodlights at the basketball court of Khuhro Sports Complex in Larkana, providing players with improved facilities for evening and night-time activities. SBBA Patron Ghulam Muhammad Khan, President Ghulam Abbas Jamal Ch and Secretary Aamir Sha-rif, along with other basketball officials, thanked Sindh Sports Minister Sardar Muhammad Bux Khan Mahar, Secretary Sports Manwar Ali Mahesar and other officials for their efforts to pro-mote sports and provide better facilities to young athletes. Ghulam Muhammad also acknowl-edged the contributions of Larkana DSO Mahfooz Makhani to the development of basketball in the region.

headline: Soldier martyred, 17 terrorists killed in Balochistan operations
description: ISLAMABAD - At least 17 Indian-sponsored terrorists were killed by security forces in two intelligence-based operations in Kachhi and Kharan districts of
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text: ISLAMABAD - At least 17 Indian-sponsored terrorists were killed by security forces in two intelligence-based operations in Kachhi and Kharan districts of Balochistan. An intelligence-based operation was conducted in the Sanni area of Kachhi district. During the operation, an attempt by terrorists to establish a roadblock was thwarted by the proactive action of security forces, resulting in the killing of ten Indian-sponsored terrorists. Weapons and ammunition were also recovered. In another intelligence-based operation in Kharan district, security forces busted a terrorist hideout and, after an intense exchange of fire, seven Indian-sponsored Khawarij were sent to hell. Weapons and ammunition were also recovered. Meanwhile, during the intense exchange of fire, Sepoy Hikmat Ullah, having fought gallantly, paid the ultimate sacrifice and embraced Shahadat. Sanitization operations are being conducted to eliminate any other Indian-sponsored terrorists found in the area. A relentless counter-terrorism campaign under the vision of “Azm-e-Istehkam”, as approved by the Federal Apex Committee on the National Action Plan, will continue at full pace by the security forces and law enforcement agencies of Pakistan to wipe out the menace of foreign-sponsored and foreign-supported terrorism from the country. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday paid tribute to the security forces for successful operations against India-backed Fitna al-Hindustan terrorists in Balochistan’s Kachhi and Kharan districts, in which 17 militants were killed. The prime minister commended the security forces for the operations, a Prime Minister’s Office news release said. The prime minister also paid tribute to Sepoy Hikmatullah of the Pakistan Army, who was martyred during an operation against terrorists in Kharan. He prayed for the elevation of the martyr’s ranks and offered condolences to his family. The prime minister said the security forces were achieving significant successes against terrorism under the vision of Azm-e-Istehkam. He reiterated the government’s resolve to eliminate terrorism from the country in all its forms.

headline: Ayesha Zafar’s fifty powers Incredibles to first Super-3 T20 win
description: LAHORE - A blistering half-century by Ayesha Zafar guided Incredibles to their first victory in the PCB Women’s Super-3 T20 Tournament, defeating
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - A blistering half-century by Ayesha Zafar guided Incredibles to their first victory in the PCB Women’s Super-3 T20 Tournament, defeating Warriors by 39 runs in the sixth match at Iqbal Stadium, Faisalabad on Tuesday. Batting first, Incredibles posted 167-6 in 20 overs, with Ayesha smashing 50 off just 25 balls, including five fours and three sixes. Captain Gull Feroza contributed 46 off 50 deliveries, while Humna Bilal claimed two wickets for Warri-ors. In reply, Warriors managed 128-8, with Sadaf Shamas scoring 38 and Eyman Fatima adding 36. Umm-e-Hani and Waheeda Akhtar took two wickets apiece. Warriors will face Champions in their next fixture on Nov 5.

headline: Dar, JI delegation discuss fuel prices, measures to provide relief to public
description: ISLAMABAD - Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Tuesday held a meeting with a delegation of Jamaat-e-Islami (JI), led by Liaquat Baloch, to
author: SHAFQAT ALI
article_text: ISLAMABAD - Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Tuesday held a meeting with a delegation of Jamaat-e-Islami (JI), led by Liaquat Baloch, to discuss petroleum prices and measures to ease the economic burden on the public, particularly low-income households. The meeting focused on exploring practical steps to provide relief to ordinary citizens amid mounting economic pressures and global economic challenges, the Foreign Office said. Both sides held candid discussions on energy pricing and public relief measures and agreed to continue consultations over the coming days to develop a mutually agreed way forward. Ishaq Dar reaffirmed the government’s commitment to prioritising public welfare and facilitating the common man in the face of prevailing economic challenges. He emphasised that sustained dialogue and cooperation across political parties were essential to addressing pressing national economic issues and developing effective relief measures. The meeting was attended by Minister for Planning, Development and Special Initiatives, the Adviser to the Prime Minister on Inter-Provincial Coordination, Special Assistant to the Prime Minister Tariq Bajwa, Secretary Finance and Special Secretary Petroleum. The consultations reflected efforts to build political consensus on petroleum pricing and explore avenues for providing greater economic relief to vulnerable segments of society.

headline: Din/FG, DP/Imperial win JPF Times Polo Cup openers
description: LAHORE - Din/FG and Diamond Paints/Imperial made winning starts to the JPF Times Polo Cup 2026 (2-6 goals), securing convincing victories on the opening day of
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - Din/FG and Diamond Paints/Imperial made winning starts to the JPF Times Polo Cup 2026 (2-6 goals), securing convincing victories on the opening day of the tournament at Jinnah Polo Fields on Tuesday. In the first match of the opening day, Din/FG outclassed AOS 8-3, with Raja Temur Nadeem producing an outstanding five-goal performance. Syed Ayan Salman, Sheikh Muhammad Farhad and Ahmad Bilal Riaz contributed one goal apiece. For AOS, Agha Musa Ali Khan scored twice, while Abdullah Ijaz added one goal. The second encounter of the day saw Diamond Paints/Imperial overpower Lotto Carpets Singapore 8-3.5, with Raja Jalal Arslan leading the charge with five fabulous goals. Ibrahim Sheikh scored twice and Bilal Haye added one to complete the winning team’s tally. Lotto Carpets Singapore received a half-goal handicap advantage, while Aarib Ali Malik, Imran Abid Mir and Taimur Ali Malik scored one goal each. The opening day’s matches attracted a sizeable gathering of polo enthusiasts, players and their families. Jinnah Polo Fields Secretary Major (R) Adil Sultan Rao was also present on the occasion.

headline: ECP warns MQM-P of losing election symbol over delayed intra-party polls
description: ISLAMABAD - The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) has issued a show-cause notice to Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) for failing to hold
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: ISLAMABAD - The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) has issued a show-cause notice to Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) for failing to hold intra-party elections within the extended deadline, giving the party 14 days to explain its failure or face legal action, including possible loss of its election symbol. According to the notice issued by the ECP, MQM-P failed to fulfill the legal requirement of holding intra-party elections by October 15, 2026, despite being granted an extension. The commission stated that regular elections of office-bearers were a mandatory legal requirement for all political parties under the Elections Act, 2017. It further said political parties were required to submit an election certificate to the ECP within seven days of completing their intra-party elections. The commission warned that failure to hold intra-party elections could render MQM-P ineligible for an election symbol, adding that its symbol could also be withheld for the next general elections. The party has been given 14 days to submit its response to the show-cause notice, failing which the ECP may initiate further proceedings in accordance with the law. The ECP had issued the show-cause notice to MQM-P on October 26.

headline: NA panel concerned over low retailers participation in Tajir Dost Scheme
description: ISLAMABAD - The National Assembly Standing Committee on Finance and Revenue has expressed concern over the lower than anticipated response from retailers under
author: Imran Ali Kundi
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - The National Assembly Standing Committee on Finance and Revenue has expressed concern over the lower than anticipated response from retailers under ‘The Tajir Dost Scheme’ despite extensive consultations with trade organisations and business representatives. The committee reviewed the implementation of the Tajir Dost Scheme on Tuesday. Minister of State for Finance and Revenue Bilal Azhar Kayani informed the committee that the deadline for filing tax returns under the scheme had expired on 31st October and the government was now preparing to initiate the enforcement phase. It was explained that non-compliant retailers would be liable to penalties, in addition to fulfilling their statutory obligation to file tax returns.

The minister of state also apprised that the government remained committed to broadening the tax base and implementing the scheme. It was further informed that consultations had been held with the Attorney General for Pakistan and the FBR to ensure the legal and procedural soundness of the proposed enforcement measures. The detailed enforcement plan would be finalised and subsequently submitted to the Prime Minister. While deliberating on key issues relating to the country’s economic and fiscal policies, the NA panel reviewed the performance and proposed reforms of the Export Facilitation Scheme (EFS), progress on the implementation of the Tajir Dost Scheme, and the economic implications of border closures.

During the discussion on the Export Facilitation Scheme, members sought a comprehensive assessment of its financial utilization, operational mechanism, eligibility criteria and contribution towards enhancing Pakistan’s exports. Concerns were expressed over the alleged misuse of the facility and the absence of a corresponding increase in overall export figures. Members emphasized that the effectiveness of the scheme must be assessed through verifiable data demonstrating its actual contribution to export growth.

The minister of state for finance and revenue informed the committee that the EFS was designed to facilitate exporters by reducing the cost of imported raw materials utilised in the production of goods meant for export. He assured the committee that a comprehensive presentation, covering the scheme’s performance, financial utilization, impact on exports, eligibility criteria and proposed reforms, would be submitted at the next meeting.

The Committee decided to defer “The Companies (Amendment) Bill, 2026” till its next meeting. The meeting was attended by MNAs: Rana Iradat Sharif Khan, Syed Sami ul Hassan Gillani, Dr Mirza Ikhtiar Baig, Dr Nafisa Shah, Muhammad Jawed Hanif Khan, Shahida Begum and Dr Sharmila Sahiba Faruqui (virtually). Bilal Azhar Kayani, Minister of State for Finance and Revenue/Special Invitee also attended the meeting. The senior officers from the Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Law and Justice, Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) and SECP also attended the meeting.

headline: JUI-F condemns drone surveillance of Fazl’s residence
description: ISLAMABAD - Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam (Fazal) on Tuesday strongly condemned the alleged drone surveillance of its chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman’s residence,
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: ISLAMABAD - Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam (Fazal) on Tuesday strongly condemned the alleged drone surveillance of its chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman’s residence, describing it as a violation of the sanctity of his home, fundamental human rights and Islamic and traditional values. In a statement, JUI-F spokesperson Aslam Ghauri said the intrusion into the privacy of Maulana Fazlur Rehman’s residence reflected the intellectual and moral degradation of powerful quarters, warning that such actions could fuel hatred, resentment and public unrest. He said the drone footage of he JUI-F chief’s residence was contrary to human rights, Eastern cultural values and Islamic traditions, adding that respect for the privacy and dignity of individuals and their families was a fundamental principle that must not be disregarded. Expressing regret over the incident, Aslam Ghauri said Maulana Fazlur Rehman had taken a principled stand for the protection of women’s dignity and honour, yet his own residence was being subjected to such an intrusion under the present government. He alleged that arguments based on reason and wisdom were being countered through false propaganda, accusations and degrading tactics rather than meaningful political engagement.

headline: Ushna, Meheq, Bismal advance as Sheheryar Malik Memorial Tennis Championship inaugurated
description: LAHORE - Ushna Suhail, Meheq Khokhar, Bismal Zia and Fajar advanced as the 10th Sheheryar Malik Memorial Pakistan Open Tennis Championship 2026 was inaugurated
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - Ushna Suhail, Meheq Khokhar, Bismal Zia and Fajar advanced as the 10th Sheheryar Malik Memorial Pakistan Open Tennis Championship 2026 was inaugurated at the Nishtar Park Sports Complex on Tuesday. The championship was formally inaugurated by chief guest Fazal-ur-Rehman, Member Planning and Development Board, Punjab. Prominent tennis personalities, including SEVP of PLTA Rashid Malik (Sitara-e-Imtiaz and Tamgha-e-Imtiaz), Rao Iftikhar Ahmad, Imran Siddiqui, Waqar Nisar, Sohail Malik, Said Hassan, Mehboob Waheed and tournament coordinator Faheem Siddiqui, players, their parents and tennis enthusiasts were also present on the occasion. Chief guest Fazal-ur-Rehman paid glowing tribute to Rashid Malik’s late son and also lauded Malik’s outstanding dedication and tireless efforts towards the growth and promotion of tennis in Punjab. “We need more dedicated and visionary sports organisers like Mr. Malik, who can help develop sporting nurseries, nurture young talent and promote sports across the country,” he said. Speaking on the occasion, Rashid Malik welcomed the participating players and wished them success, urging them to demonstrate determination, discipline and sportsmanship throughout the competition. He also thanked all the sponsors of the mega event, whose support helped the organizers organize such a grand tennis event. Meanwhile, in the ladies’ singles pre-quarterfinals, top contender Ushna Sohail defeated Shahnoor Umer 6-0, 6-1 while Meheq Khokhar thumped Anabya Baig 6-0, 6-0, Bismal Zia blanked Saima Tahseen 6-0, 6-0 and Fajar Fayyaz overcame Zainah Abdullah 7-5, 6-4. In the men’s singles, M Shoaib defeated Jabir Ali 6-2, 6-2, Abubakar Talha overcame Ali Talha 6-3, 6-2, and Yousaf Khalil registered a convincing 6-0, 6-0 victory over M Junaid. M Huzaifa Khan beat Imran Bhatti 6-2, 6-1, Heera Ashiq defeated Usman Rafiq 6-1, 6-0, while Mudassar Murtaza overcame Uzair Khan 6-1, 6-1. Asad Zaman edged past M Talha Khan 7-6, 6-3, and Barkat Ullah defeated Asad Ullah 6-2, 6-2. In the men’s doubles, M Abid and Abdullah Adnan defeated Shehryar Anees and Jabir Ali 6-4, 6-0, while Talha Khan and Huzaifa Khan beat Kashif Rehmat and Hamza Naeem 6-1, 6-0. Omer Babar and Ahtesham Arif overcame Sami Zeb and Saif Ullah 7-6, 4-6, 10-8 in a closely contested match. Ahmad Babar and Heera Ashiq defeated Hamza Khan and Kamran Khalil 6-1, 6-2, while Imran Bhatti and Asad Zaman beat Asad Ullah and Uzair Khan 6-1, 6-2.

headline: Iran could use chemical weapons, Israel tells US, Gulf countries
description: DUBAI - Israel has shared with the US and Gulf countries intelligence that Iran is considering using chemical weapons against them, The New York Times
author: News Desk
article_text: DUBAI - Israel has shared with the US and Gulf countries intelligence that Iran is considering using chemical weapons against them, The New York Times reports. Israeli officials are arguing that the chemical weapons threat is more urgent than Iran’s nuclear threat, says the NYT. They told US officials that Iran is developing technology to deliver chemical weapons via missiles or to sneak them into enemy countries. Some US officials see the intelligence as being used by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to urge US President Donald Trump to go back to active combat against the Islamic Republic, according to the report. Gulf countries found the intelligence briefings “unserious.” Still, reports the NYT, some officials are taking the Israeli warnings seriously, in light of Iran’s threats against the US and its allies. Israeli emergency response drills this week have not focused on the chemical weapons threat, per the report. The Prime Minister’s Office does not comment on the specific claims in the article, telling The Times of Israel that “Israel is following closely every threat from the Iranian terror regime, and is ready to confront them.”

headline: Federal govt agrees to curtail loadshedding in KP
description: ISLAMABAD - The federal government has agreed to curtail electricity loadshedding in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and extend the duration of electricity supply to
author: Fawad Yousafzai
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - The federal government has agreed to curtail electricity loadshedding in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and extend the duration of electricity supply to high-loss areas of the province that were earlier facing prolonged outages. The announcement was made by Federal Minister for Power Awais Leghari during a consultative meeting between representatives of the federal and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa governments. On the special directives of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, a meeting was held here to formulate sustainable solutions for the power and energy challenges in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Federal Minister for Power Sardar Awais Leghari and the federal minister for petroleum held comprehensive discussions on energy sector issues in KP.

In line with the Prime Minister’s vision, the meeting aimed to improve the energy situation and provide relief to the public in close collaboration with the provincial administration. The high-level meeting was attended by Governor Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Faisal Karim Kundi, Secretary Power Division, Secretary Petroleum, Special Assistant to the Prime Minister (SAPM) on Energy, and Chief Secretary Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. During the meeting, Governor Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Faisal Karim Kundi highlighted the overall energy landscape in the province and urged for a meaningful reduction in the duration of loadshedding, particularly in high-loss and hard-hit areas.

The federal leadership expressed confidence that the public would reciprocate this goodwill gesture by clearing their outstanding electricity dues and supporting efforts against power theft, ensuring that this sustained power supply can be maintained uninterrupted. Outlining a sustainable solution, Sardar Awais Ahmad Khan Leghari stated that the Transformer-Based Load Management System (APMS) is being actively implemented across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Under this modern and automated mechanism, the conventional practice of shutting down entire feeders will be phased out, transitioning load management directly to individual transformers. Concluding the meeting, the federal government and the provincial leadership agreed to maintain close coordination to ensure the timely execution of the agreed roadmap, delivering prompt and lasting relief to the citizens of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
