headline: PCB names Shaheens’ squad for Asia Cup title defence
description: LAHORE - The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) has unveiled a 15-member Pakistan Shaheens squad for the ACC Men’s Asia Cup Rising Stars Championship
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) has unveiled a 15-member Pakistan Shaheens squad for the ACC Men’s Asia Cup Rising Stars Championship 2026, with Abdul Samad appointed captain as the defending champions prepare to defend their title in Doha, Qatar, from November 19 to 29. The emerging middle-order batter will lead a promising combination of young talent and international experience in the eight-team competition, where Pakistan have been drawn in Group B alongside arch-rivals India, Nepal and the United Arab Emirates (UAE). The Shaheens will rely on a formidable batting line-up featuring Hasan Nawaz, Maaz Sadaqat, Haider Ali, Shahzaib Khan, Farhan Yousuf and Shamyl Hussain, while wicketkeeper-batter Rohail Nazir will provide additional experience and stability behind the stumps. Pakistan’s pace attack will be spearheaded by Mohammad Hasnain, whose express pace and international experience will be key to the team’s title ambitions. He will receive support from Ahmed Daniyal, Akif Javed and Muhammad Imran Randhawa. The bowling combination also includes left-arm all-rounder Danish Aziz, leg-spinner Saad Masood and left-arm wrist-spinner Sufyan Muqeem, giving the defending champions a balanced attack with a variety of options. Pakistan Shaheens will launch their campaign against the UAE on November 20 before facing arch-rivals India in a high-profile encounter on November 22. They will conclude their group-stage commitments against Nepal on November 24. With India also in their group, the clash between the traditional rivals is expected to be one of the major attractions of the opening round, while Pakistan will be keen to build momentum and secure a place in the knockout stage. Under the tournament format, the top two teams from each of the two groups will qualify for the semi-finals, scheduled for November 26 and 27. The championship final will take place on November 29. PAKISTAN SHAHEENS SQUAD: Abdul Samad (captain), Ahmed Daniyal, Akif Javed, Danish Aziz, Farhan Yousuf, Haider Ali, Hasan Nawaz, Maaz Sadaqat, M Hasnain, M Imran Randhawa, Rohail Nazir (wk), Saad Masood, Shahzaib Khan, Shamyl Hussain and Sufyan Muqeem.

headline: Two schoolchildren, van driver injured in acid attack in Vehari
description: Vehari - Two schoolchildren and a van driver sustained minor burn injuries in an alleged acid attack at Achar Bazaar, Macheewal, after school hours, triggering
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: Vehari - Two schoolchildren and a van driver sustained minor burn injuries in an alleged acid attack at Achar Bazaar, Macheewal, after school hours, triggering concern among local residents. According to details, an unidentified person allegedly threw acid on children Waheed and Waqas, residents of 531 EB, and van driver Tasawwar Iqbal while they were waiting to return home. The injured were shifted for medical examination, and their condition was reported to be out of danger. Initial reports identified a man named Shakeel as the suspected attacker, reportedly over an old dispute with the van driver. The suspect allegedly fled the scene and has not yet been arrested. Residents also raised concerns over the alleged delay in police response. However, senior police officials later reached the hospital to inquire about the condition of the injured and obtain details of the incident. Citizens have demanded a transparent investigation, immediate arrest of the suspect and action to ensure justice for the victims.

headline: US to end $4b in annual military aid to Israel by end of 2026: Trump
description: WASHINGTON - US President Donald Trump on Tuesday claimed that the United States will cease providing some $4 billion in annual military aid to Israel after
author: News Desk
article_text:
WASHINGTON - US President Donald Trump on Tuesday claimed that the United States will cease providing some $4 billion in annual military aid to Israel after the end of this year, in comments that reportedly caught Israeli security and financial officials off guard.

Trump tried to qualify the announcement by stressing that Israel has been a good ally and even backs the policy, but his decision to issue it on the morning of the Congressional midterm elections highlights how toxic the issue of aid to Israel has become among both parties in the US. “As far as paying Israel, Bibi Netanyahu and I have made a deal — we give Israel $4 billion a year — we made a deal months ago that we’re stopping,” Trump told Fox News in a phone interview. “They’re fine with it because they’ve become a very successful country. They don’t need it. headline: Power consumers face Rs1.914-1.962 trillion capacity payments burden in CY2027
description: ISLAMABAD - Pakistan’s power consumers are projected to pay Rs1.914 to Rs1.962 trillion in capacity payments — accounting for 52 to 57 percent
author: Fawad Yousafzai
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Pakistan’s power consumers are projected to pay Rs1.914 to Rs1.962 trillion in capacity payments — accounting for 52 to 57 percent of the total power purchase price under various scenarios — during CY2027, as questions have been raised over the impact of revised deals with independent power producers (IPPs) on capacity charges.

In a public hearing on the CPPA-G’s petition for determination of the power purchase price (PPP) for CY2027, it was informed that the PPP could increase in the range of Re0.56 to Rs3.94 per unit under six different scenarios. However, the projections remain surrounded by uncertainty over liquefied natural gas (LNG) supplies and global fuel prices, which could complicate the country’s power purchase price outlook for 2027.

During the hearing, CPPA-G officials also warned that consumers could face a fuel price adjustment (FPA) burden in December and January, mainly due to low hydropower generation, reduced availability of indigenous gas for power generation and high fuel costs. However, Managing Director CPPA-G Rehan Akhtar said it was too early to quantify the impact. The National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (NEPRA) held a public hearing Tuesday on the CPPA’s request to determine the power purchase price for January through December 2027. NEPRA Chairman Waseem Mukhtar said the availability of LNG would be a key factor in determining the final power purchase cost, adding that supplies for next year were still unclear.

Managing Director CPPA-G said uncertainty in international crude oil prices was another major risk because LNG and other fuels used for power generation are linked, directly or indirectly, to global oil prices. The CPPA-G said its 2027 estimates were based on assumptions about oil and LNG prices, water availability, fuel mix, electricity demand and exchange rates. The CPPA-G has submitted its PPP forecast for CY2027 with six scenarios, projecting PPP in the range of Rs25.883 per unit to Rs29.255 per unit or Rs3.37 trillion to Rs3.81 trillion.

The current national average power purchase price is Rs25.32 per unit. Capacity payments to IPPs alone are projected at between Rs1.914 trillion and Rs1.962 trillion next year. The projections are based on total energy sold to DISCOs of 130,081 million units in base case scenario and 127,937 million units sensitivity scenario under low demand growth and normal hydrology, said projection of PPP for calendar year 2027. The capacity payment is primarily sensitive to US$/PKR exchange rate, KIBOR/SOFR rate and local and international inflation. Under base case scenario of 2.6% growth & Rs279/US$ the capacity charges have been projected at Rs1.914 trillion, while at worst case scenario assuming 0.7% & Rs290/US$ capacity charges have been assumed at Rs1.962 trillion.

Representative of Karachi Chamber of Commerce and Industry Tanvir Bari questioned whether promised reductions in capacity charges after negotiations with independent power producers had materialized. He said that capacity charges do not appear to be coming down. For the outgoing calendar year 2026, the power purchase cost is estimated at Rs3.185 trillion, with an average purchase price of Rs25.32 per unit. Capacity payments are projected at Rs1.923 trillion, or Rs14.86 per unit. NEPRA will finalize its 2027 power purchase price after the hearing and forward the proposed basic electricity tariff to the federal government.

In a public hearing on the CPPA-G’s petition for determination of the power purchase price (PPP) for CY2027, it was informed that the PPP could increase in the range of Re0.56 to Rs3.94 per unit under six different scenarios. However, the projections remain surrounded by uncertainty over liquefied natural gas (LNG) supplies and global fuel prices, which could complicate the country’s power purchase price outlook for 2027.

During the hearing, CPPA-G officials also warned that consumers could face a fuel price adjustment (FPA) burden in December and January, mainly due to low hydropower generation, reduced availability of indigenous gas for power generation and high fuel costs. However, Managing Director CPPA-G Rehan Akhtar said it was too early to quantify the impact. The National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (NEPRA) held a public hearing Tuesday on the CPPA’s request to determine the power purchase price for January through December 2027. NEPRA Chairman Waseem Mukhtar said the availability of LNG would be a key factor in determining the final power purchase cost, adding that supplies for next year were still unclear.

Managing Director CPPA-G said uncertainty in international crude oil prices was another major risk because LNG and other fuels used for power generation are linked, directly or indirectly, to global oil prices. The CPPA-G said its 2027 estimates were based on assumptions about oil and LNG prices, water availability, fuel mix, electricity demand and exchange rates. The CPPA-G has submitted its PPP forecast for CY2027 with six scenarios, projecting PPP in the range of Rs25.883 per unit to Rs29.255 per unit or Rs3.37 trillion to Rs3.81 trillion.

The current national average power purchase price is Rs25.32 per unit. Capacity payments to IPPs alone are projected at between Rs1.914 trillion and Rs1.962 trillion next year. The projections are based on total energy sold to DISCOs of 130,081 million units in base case scenario and 127,937 million units sensitivity scenario under low demand growth and normal hydrology, said projection of PPP for calendar year 2027. The capacity payment is primarily sensitive to US$/PKR exchange rate, KIBOR/SOFR rate and local and international inflation. Under base case scenario of 2.6% growth & Rs279/US$ the capacity charges have been projected at Rs1.914 trillion, while at worst case scenario assuming 0.7% & Rs290/US$ capacity charges have been assumed at Rs1.962 trillion.

Representative of Karachi Chamber of Commerce and Industry Tanvir Bari questioned whether promised reductions in capacity charges after negotiations with independent power producers had materialized. He said that capacity charges do not appear to be coming down. For the outgoing calendar year 2026, the power purchase cost is estimated at Rs3.185 trillion, with an average purchase price of Rs25.32 per unit. Capacity payments are projected at Rs1.923 trillion, or Rs14.86 per unit. NEPRA will finalize its 2027 power purchase price after the hearing and forward the proposed basic electricity tariff to the federal government.

headline: Hamza Roman enters last eight, three more Pakistanis eye progress at J-60 C’ships
description: LAHORE - Pakistan’s Hamza Roman breezed into the boys’ singles quarterfinals of the J-60 Bard Foundation Junior World Tennis Championships
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
LAHORE - Pakistan’s Hamza Roman breezed into the boys’ singles quarterfinals of the J-60 Bard Foundation Junior World Tennis Championships Islamabad-2026, giving the home contingent a major boost at the PTF Tennis Complex. Hamza outclassed Sweden’s Nils Preger 6-3, 6-3 in the second round, producing a confident display to secure his place among the last eight. His victory highlighted Pakistan’s growing presence in the international junior competition and strengthened the home players’ hopes of making a deep run. Three more Pakistani players, Ahtesham Humayun, Amir Mazari and Muhammad Hassan Usmani, are scheduled to compete in their respective second-round singles matches today (Wednesday), with all three aiming to join Hamza in the next stage. Pakistan’s young players also remained active in the boys’ doubles event, where several local combinations featured in the opening round. Abdul Basit, partnering Serbia’s Vukasin Pavlovic, registered a convincing 6-0, 6-0 victory over Kazakhstan’s Sanzhar Bolat and Pakistan’s Abdurrehman Sohail. Rayan Khan and Muhammad Shayan also advanced after defeating China’s Yupei Liang and Bo Han Yang 6-3, 6-4. Amir Mazari, playing alongside Sri Lanka’s Aahil Kaleel, overcame Pakistan’s Abdar Ali and Kazakhstan’s Alshinhan Mukhamedkali 6-4, 6-2. The all-Pakistani pairing of Muhammad Hassan Usmani and Muhammad Haziq Asim produced another encouraging result, beating M Ahmad Afzal and Thailand’s Tachatam Srisen 7-6(5), 6-2. In other boys’ doubles encounters, Thailand’s Napat Pattanalertphan and Phasin Sinchalong defeated Australia’s Adnan Afzal and Pakistan’s Arham Tariq 6-0, 6-2, while China’s Aolun Ma and Haoxuan Xu overcame Russia’s Daniel Elias and Nikita Dogadin 7-6(4), 6-4. Sweden’s Nils Preger and Belarus’ Aliaksandr Viarsotski edged Pakistan’s Zohaib Afzal Malik and Muhammad Yahya 6-3, 6-7(6), 10-8. In the remaining boys’ singles matches, Russia’s Nikita Dogadin defeated Thailand’s Napat Pattanalertphan 6-3, 6-1, while Sri Lanka’s Aahil Kaleel beat Pakistan’s Muhammad Shayan 6-1, 6-4. China’s Haoxuan Xu also advanced with a 6-3, 6-4 win over Pakistan’s Muhammad Yahya. The girls’ singles second round featured several competitive encounters. Thailand’s Ploypetch Daungkhiaw defeated Russia’s Evelina Dzepa 6-4, 6-4, while compatriot Pimpisia Wongwanitkajon overcame Kazakhstan’s Polina Sushkova 6-2, 1-6, 6-4. Russia’s Victoria Gruntova beat China’s Daixi Hu 3-6, 6-1, 6-4, and Thailand’s Anyawee Paisarnpanuwong edged China’s Yijia Wang 6-2, 5-7, 6-3.

The championship features 58 players, 36 boys and 22 girls, representing 14 countries: Pakistan, Russia, Hong Kong, China, Thailand, Kazakhstan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Serbia, Australia, Spain, Canada, Belarus and Sweden.

headline: DPO Tasswar Iqbal reviews crimes situation in Burewala
description: MAILSI - A meeting was held at DPO Office Vehari under the chairmanship of DPO Vehari Tasswar Iqbal to review crime situation. SDPO Circle Burewala Rana
author: Peer Abdul Razaq Qureshi
article_text:
MAILSI - A meeting was held at DPO Office Vehari under the chairmanship of DPO Vehari Tasswar Iqbal to review crime situation. SDPO Circle Burewala Rana Muhammad Imran Tipu and all SHOs of Circle Burewala attended the meeting. During the meeting, a detailed review of the performance of all police stations of Circle Burewala was taken. DPO Vehari Tasswar Iqbal issued necessary instructions to the officers regarding the arrest of declared criminals, timely settlement of cases under investigation, arrest of remaining accused, safe recovery of kidnapped persons and completion of pending challans on priority basis.

DPO Vehari directed that all available resources should be utilised to eradicate crime, protect the lives and property of citizens and provide timely justice to the public. He clarified that police officers should discharge their responsibilities with professionalism, hard work and honesty. The trend of significant reduction in crime rate in Vehari district was also discussed in the meeting. On this occasion, DPO Taswar Iqbal said that to maintain this trend of reduction in crime rate, establish law and order and suppress criminal elements, every officer and official of the police force should work with professionalism and professional teamwork. Reader to DPO Rana Muhammad Ashraf and PA to DPO Vehari Mian Ghulam Farid were also present on this occasion.

headline: World Conference on Int’l Arbitration goes over investment protection, procedural justice
description: DOHA - The 6th World Conference on International Arbitration in Doha has delved into a combination of key issues pertinent to advancing the arbitration system
author: News Source
article_text: DOHA - The 6th World Conference on International Arbitration in Doha has delved into a combination of key issues pertinent to advancing the arbitration system and its efficiency. Across four sessions, participants have debated back and forth the integration of the judiciary and arbitration, the future of arbitral proceedings, investment protection through international arbitration, and the limits of arbitral tribunals’ discretion. The first session drilled down on the nature of the nexus between the judiciary and arbitration, the role of judicial oversight in supporting arbitral proceedings and ensuring their procedural integrity, as well as ways to achieve complementarity between the two systems, in pursuit of bolstering confidence in arbitration and ensuring its effectiveness as an alternative means of dispute resolution. headline: Maliha topples two-time European champion at IMMAF World C’ships
description: LAHORE - Pakistan’s Maliha Ali produced a landmark performance at the IMMAF World Championships in Georgia, defeating Russia’s highly regarded
author: Azhar Khan
article_text: LAHORE - Pakistan’s Maliha Ali produced a landmark performance at the IMMAF World Championships in Georgia, defeating Russia’s highly regarded Veronika Drozdova in a thrilling contest to claim one of the most notable victories of the championship. The Hunza-born fighter showcased impressive striking, intelligent movement and disciplined cage control against an opponent with an established international record. Drozdova, a two-time European champion and one of Russia’s promising mixed martial arts talents, entered the competition with a formidable reputation. Maliha, however, met the challenge with confidence and composure, refusing to be intimidated by her opponent’s credentials. With this victory, Maliha has also qualified for the quarterfinals of the mega MMA event. The victory carries added significance given Russia’s standing in international mixed martial arts. The country has a deep talent pool, an established development structure and a strong presence across the sport’s major competitions. Against that backdrop, Maliha’s success represents an important moment for Pakistan’s growing MMA programme. Maliha comes from Hunza, Gilgit-Baltistan, and trains at BRAVE Gym Lahore alongside her twin sister, Manisha Ali. The sisters work under the guidance of Omar Ahmed, president of the Pakistan Mixed Martial Arts Federation, who was personally present in Maliha’s corner for the bout. The twins are emerging as promising figures in Pakistan’s combat-sports scene. Their journey from the mountains of northern Pakistan to an international championship reflects both their commitment and the potential of young athletes who receive sustained coaching, preparation and opportunities to compete. Maliha’s performance also highlights the importance of a clear pathway for developing fighters. Regular domestic competition, quality coaching and exposure to Asian and world-level events can help athletes build the experience required to challenge established opponents. Linking those stages with opportunities to progress towards professional competition will be important for the continued growth of the sport in Pakistan. For the national team, the result offers encouragement that Pakistani fighters can compete with leading opponents from countries with longer-established MMA systems. It is also a moment of recognition for the coaches and support staff working to raise standards and broaden opportunities for emerging talent. Maliha’s victory is, therefore, more than a personal milestone. By overcoming a two-time European champion on the world stage, she has brought attention to Pakistan’s developing MMA talent and provided an inspiring example for young athletes aspiring to follow in her footsteps. Her achievement, alongside the progress of her twin sister, gives Pakistan further reason to invest in the next generation of fighters and strengthen its presence in international combat sports.

headline: M4.6 quake hits Tajikistan
description: ASTANA - An earthquake measuring 4.6 hit Tajikistan on November 3. According to operational data from the Kazakhstan National Data Centre, tremors occurred at
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: ASTANA - An earthquake measuring 4.6 hit Tajikistan on November 3. According to operational data from the Kazakhstan National Data Centre, tremors occurred at 10:35am Astana time (GMT 05:35am). The coordinates of the epicenter are 37.80° north latitude, 72.93° east longitude. The magnitude of the quake was 4.6, and the energy class was 10.8. No information on casualties or damage was provided in the operational report. Earlier, it was reported that a magnitude 4.5 earthquake struck China on Tuesday.

Earlier, it was reported that a magnitude 4.5 earthquake struck China on Tuesday.

headline: TDAP, NAVTTC and BRSP to strengthen collaboration for export promotion, skills development
description: QUETTA - The Trade Development Authority of Pakistan (TDAP) hosted a high-level consultative meeting in Quetta on Tuesday at the conclusion of first edition of
author: PR
article_text:
QUETTA - The Trade Development Authority of Pakistan (TDAP) hosted a high-level consultative meeting in Quetta on Tuesday at the conclusion of first edition of WEXNET Quetta. The meeting was attended by Engr Qamar-ul-Islam Raja, Chairman National Vocational and Technical Training Commission (NAVTTC), Dr Nadia Karim Shaw, Executive Director NAVTTC, Anwar Saleem Kasi, Chairman Balochistan Rural Support Programme (BRSP), Dr Tahir Rasheed, Chief Executive Officer BRSP; Zafar Buledi, Secretary Population Welfare Department, Government of Balochistan, and Sheryar Taj, Secretary TDAP.

The discussions focused on strengthening institutional collaboration to promote export-oriented economic activities, technical and vocational skills development, trainings, internships, entrepreneurship, and market linkages, with particular emphasis on creating sustainable economic opportunities for women, youth, and local communities in Balochistan.

Following detailed deliberations, TDAP, NAVTTC and BRSP mutually agreed to establish a collaborative framework for undertaking coordinated interventions aimed at enhancing export potential, developing market-relevant technical skills, supporting local enterprises, and facilitating their integration into national and international value chains. As a significant outcome of the meeting, it was agreed that to strengthen the capacity of the SME sector for promotion of exports memoranda of understanding (MoUs) would be formalized between TDAP and NAVTTC, and TDAP and BRSP, respectively. Accordingly joint seminars and workshops would be conducted and internships programs would be planned.

The initiative represents an important step towards fostering institutional synergies, strengthening the linkages between skills development and export promotion, and unlocking the economic potential of Balochistan through inclusive, sustainable and export-led growth.

headline: Punjab governor urges political forces to prioritise national interest
description: Vehari - Punjab Governor Sardar Saleem Haider Khan has said that under the leadership of Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari, the
author: Sh Fazal Ur Rehman
article_text: Vehari - Punjab Governor Sardar Saleem Haider Khan has said that under the leadership of Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari, the party is playing its role in promoting national reconciliation, parliamentary supremacy, democratic stability and political consensus on matters of national security. He stressed that in the prevailing circumstances all political forces must rise above their differences, prioritise national interests and adopt a joint strategy to address challenges facing the country, including terrorism and economic difficulties. He expressed these views during a meeting with a delegation from Vehari district, led by prominent political and social personality Mirza Muhammad Khalid, at Governor House, Lahore. The meeting discussed the country’s political situation, national security, the role of Parliament, the performance of the Punjab government and development issues in South Punjab.The Governor said that despite being part of the coalition government, the PPP would maintain its distinct political identity and ideological position. He emphasised the need for effective measures to address inflation, unemployment, farmers’ problems and the provision of basic facilities, adding that making Parliament an effective centre of national decision-making was a pressing necessity.The delegation included President Pakistan Mughal Supreme Council Ahsan Ali Mughal, Aziz Shehzad Lar and Mirza Talha Harvez. Speaking on the occasion, Mirza Muhammad Khalid said that mutual respect, consultation and constructive criticism in coalition politics strengthened democracy. He urged the government to pay special attention to inflation, unemployment, fair prices for farmers’ produce, education, healthcare and basic civic facilities. He further stressed that the problems and development needs of South Punjab, along with employment opportunities, should be included among the government’s priorities. He said the PPP could further strengthen its political roots in Punjab through strong engagement with farmers, labourers, traders and youth, supported by an active organisational structure. He added that people now expected practical measures and solutions to their problems rather than political promises.

headline: Kazakhstan plans to build uranium reserve of 150,000 tonnes by 2050
description: ASTANA - Kazakhstan is considering the creation of a state strategic uranium reserve to secure fuel supplies for its future nuclear power plants, a wire
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: ASTANA - Kazakhstan is considering the creation of a state strategic uranium reserve to secure fuel supplies for its future nuclear power plants, a wire service quotes Chairman of the Atomic Energy Agency Almassadam Satkaliyev as saying. According to Satkaliyev, the agency is reassessing its approach to uranium resource management, viewing uranium not only as a raw material but also as a strategic resource for Kazakhstan’s long-term economic development. Speaking at a meeting of the Qurultay Committee on Economic Policy, Industry, and Energy, Satkaliyev said the agency was considering the creation of a state strategic uranium reserve to secure fuel supplies for future nuclear power plants. He explained that Kazakhstan’s nuclear industry development strategy through 2050 calls for reserving at least 150,000 tons of uranium by that year, along with developing and approving a conceptual framework for establishing the strategic reserve. The agency is currently working to determine the approaches and mechanisms needed to establish the strategic reserve, taking into account Kazakhstan’s long-term nuclear energy requirements. “The strategic reserve is expected to be developed as a comprehensive, multi-level system covering the entire nuclear fuel supply chain, from reserving uranium deposits underground to building physical stockpiles of natural uranium, reserves of ready-to-use nuclear fuel, and other mechanisms,” Satkaliyev added.

headline: IHC decides to frame charges against CDA Member Estate
description: ISLAMABAD - The Islamabad High Court (IHC) Tuesday decided to frame charges in contempt of court proceedings against Capital Development Authority (CDA)
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: ISLAMABAD - The Islamabad High Court (IHC) Tuesday decided to frame charges in contempt of court proceedings against Capital Development Authority (CDA) Member Estate Zaman Wattoo for failing to appear before the court citing illness. A single bench of IHC comprising Chief Justice of IHC Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar conducted hearing of the contempt of court proceedings and rejected Wattoo’s request for an unconditional apology. Wattoo appeared before the court alongside his counsel, CDA lawyer Nazir Jawad. The IHC Chief Justice observed that the contempt proceedings would be dealt with first, while the main petition would be heard later. He also directed the prosecutor to appear fully prepared at the next hearing. At the outset of the hearing, Wattoo sought unconditional apology and requested that the case be closed immediately. However, the IHC Chief Justice rejected the plea and stated that the accused would be indicted on the next hearing.

headline: Coca-Cola Pak recognised at SDPI’s 29th Sustainable Development Conference for plastic road project
description: ISLAMABAD - Coca-Cola Pakistan has been honored with the prestigious Sustainability Award in the Sustainable Cities and Built Environment category at the 29th
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Coca-Cola Pakistan has been honored with the prestigious Sustainability Award in the Sustainable Cities and Built Environment category at the 29th Sustainable Development Conference (SDC) and 4th Sustainability Investment Expo (SIE), organized by the Sustainable Development Policy Institute (SDPI).

The award was presented by Her Excellency Maja Derrous Mortensen, Ambassador of Denmark to Pakistan, and Romina Khurshid Alam, Coordinator to the Prime Minister for Climate Change and Environmental Coordination. Dr Faisal Hashmi, Senior Director, Public Affairs, Communications & Sustainability, Coca-Cola Pakistan & Afghanistan Region, received the award on behalf of the company.

Held under the theme “Rethinking Development in an Age of Disruption,” the awards recognize transformative initiatives that drive scalable, eco-friendly, and climate-resilient solutions. The recognition honors a groundbreaking public-private partnership through which Coca-Cola Pakistan collaborated with the Capital Development Authority (CDA) and TeamUp/National Incubation Center (NIC) to construct Pakistan’s first plastic road along Ataturk Avenue in Islamabad.

headline: Korean ambassador calls for strengthening bilateral cooperation with Pakistan
description: FAISALABAD - Ambassador of the Republic of Korea to Pakistan Han Sungho reaffirmed the commitment of Pakistan and South Korea to strengthening bilateral
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
FAISALABAD - Ambassador of the Republic of Korea to Pakistan Han Sungho reaffirmed the commitment of Pakistan and South Korea to strengthening bilateral cooperation in food security, nutrition and agriculture. He was addressing the inaugural session of two-day international conference organised by the Pak Korea Nutrition Center (PKNC), University of Agriculture Faisalabad (UAF) under the theme “Advancing Nutrition through Partnerships & Policy.”

The ambassador appreciated the achievements of the Pakistan Korea Nutrition Center project, attributing its success to the strong partnership between the two countries and the dedication of all stakeholders. He said Korean agencies were contributing to Pakistan’s development in trade, economic cooperation, health, food and nutrition security and cultural heritage. KOICA Islamabad Country Director Donggil Oh emphasised that sustainable development required coordinated efforts among governments, academic institutions and development partners, highlighting the importance of institutional capacity building, knowledge exchange and translating research into practical initiatives. UAF Vice Chancellor Prof. Dr. Zulfiqar Ali described nutrition as a fundamental pillar of human development, economic productivity and national prosperity. He said PKNC had trained more than 12,000 frontline nutrition workers, supported the development of nutritious and fortified food products, established modern research and training facilities, strengthened provincial outreach centres, and awarded research, policy research and start up grants to promote innovation and entrepreneurship in the food and nutrition sector. GCWUF Vice Chancellor Prof. Dr. Kanwal Amin, Dr. Arif Rehman, Chief of the Food and Agriculture Section at the Planning Commission of Pakistan Ms. Sodam Baek, Deputy Country Director of KOICA Dr. Jaehan Kim, Project Manager Consultant and other participants also attended the conference. Central Project Director of PKNC, Prof. Dr. Moazzam Rafiq Khan said the centre was playing a significant role in nutrition research, capacity building and international collaboration. He expressed hope that the conference would facilitate scientific knowledge sharing, identification of research gaps and development of policy recommendations to address nutritional challenges.

headline: Pakistan tops world in YouTube views: PTA
description: ISLAMABAD - Pakistan has emerged as one of the world’s biggest social media markets, with 100 million TikTok users and 96 million YouTube users.
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: ISLAMABAD - Pakistan has emerged as one of the world’s biggest social media markets, with 100 million TikTok users and 96 million YouTube users. According to figures shared by the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) before a National Assembly committee on Tuesday, around 100 million Pakistanis use TikTok, while as many as 150 million watch and upload videos on the platform. YouTube currently has 96 million users in the country and generates approximately 560 million views every day. PTA Chairman Hafeez-ur-Rehman presented the figures during a National Assembly Standing Committee on Information Technology meeting. The briefing also highlighted massive daily activity on WhatsApp, even as lawmakers criticised the quality of mobile and internet services across the country. The PTA chairman told the committee that Pakistan ranks among the world’s leading countries in terms of YouTube video viewership. He said WhatsApp has around 100 million users in the country, Pakistanis make approximately one billion calls and send 12 billion messages through the messaging platform every day.

headline: UBL named Best Bank of Year 2025 in large banks category by CFA Society Pakistan
description: KARACHI - United Bank Limited (UBL), Pakistan’s leading bank, has been recognised as Best Bank of the Year 2025 in the Large Banks Category by CFA
author: PR
article_text:
KARACHI - United Bank Limited (UBL), Pakistan’s leading bank, has been recognised as Best Bank of the Year 2025 in the Large Banks Category by CFA Society Pakistan at the 23rd Annual Excellence Awards. The recognition acknowledges the bank’s financial strength, sustained growth and continued commitment to excellence across the banking sector.

With a deposit base of Rs 6.5 trillion, a nationwide network of over 2,200 branches, a capital base of Rs 529 billion and a workforce of more than 35,000 employees, UBL has established a strong presence across Pakistan’s financial landscape. The bank also places special emphasis on inclusive employment, by maintaining a significant female workforce, while at the same time creating career opportunities for the youth of the country. Through these initiatives, UBL continues to contribute to employment generation, diversity and broader economic participation.

In addition to being named Best Bank of the Year, UBL received recognition in three other categories at the awards ceremony. These included the Best ESG Reporting Award 2025 (Winner), Corporate Finance House of the Year (January 2025 to June 2026) – Fixed Income (Runner-Up), and Best Digital Banking Services of the Year 2025 – Commercial Banks (Runner-Up). The multiple accolades reflect UBL’s performance across key areas of banking, including financial services, corporate finance, environmental, social and governance (ESG) practices, and digital banking. They also underscore the bank’s continued focus on strengthening its institutional capabilities, advancing digital transformation and delivering innovative financial solutions to its customers.

headline: IHC suspends Justice of Peace’s order related to PIMS fire FIR
description: ISLAMABAD - The Islamabad High Court (IHC) Tuesday suspended a Justice of the Peace’s order related to dismissal of an application seeking the
author: Shahid Rao
article_text: ISLAMABAD - The Islamabad High Court (IHC) Tuesday suspended a Justice of the Peace’s order related to dismissal of an application seeking the registration of an FIR into the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) fire tragedy. A single bench of IHC comprising Justice Khadim Hussain Soomro issued the orders while hearing a petition seeking registration of a criminal case over the incident and compensation for the affected families. In this regard, the IHC bench also directed the authorities to submit the complete record, along with the inquiry report, and issued notices to the respondents, including the federal government and the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO). During the hearing, the IHC bench warned that it could order criminal proceedings against those responsible for the deaths of 14 newborns in the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences fire tragedy if negligence was established. The judge remarked, “I will summon all the reports and evidence,” adding that “If any negligence comes to light, I will order an FIR against those responsible.” He directed authorities to produce the complete record, including the inquiry report. Besides this, the court issued notices to the federal government, Prime Minister’s Office, Ministry of Health and Establishment Division, seeking their responses. The IHC bench also directed to issue notices to the Islamabad Healthcare Regulatory Authority, Auditor General, chief commissioner, deputy commissioner, Capital Development Authority, Capital Emergency Services, Pims executive director, Islamabad inspector general of police and Federal Investigation Agency director general. The petition was filed by lawyer Riaz Hanif Rahi, who told the court that 14 children had died after being burnt in the incident, while another child succumbed to injuries later. He said no FIR had been registered despite an inquiry into the tragedy. Rahi maintained that the inquiry report had established negligence and urged the court to direct police to register a case before the end of the day’s proceedings. He also said he was the only person to have approached the police with an application seeking registration of an FIR. When the judge asked whether an inquiry had been conducted, the lawyer replied that its findings had confirmed lapses. He questioned the purpose of collecting evidence when no criminal case had been registered in which it could be presented. The judge, however, asked the counsel to focus on the legal arguments rather than repeatedly pressing for an immediate order to register the FIR. The court suspended the Justice of Peace’s order dismissing the application for registration of a case. According to Rahi, the application had been rejected on the grounds that related petitions were already pending before the high court. During the hearing, the lawyer described the deaths as an appalling tragedy, saying: “Even the young of animals in a jungle are not treated like this.” Justice Soomro asked him to address the legal merits of the petition. The court adjourned further proceedings until November 12. The petition sought the registration of an FIR in connection with the deaths of 14 newborns in a fire at the Gynaecology Ward/ Special Care Centre of the Mother and Child Hospital (MCH) at Pims. The petitioner alleged that the incident was caused by gross negligence, including the absence of staff from a ward that had reportedly been locked to prevent theft. The incident occurred on August 26, when a fire broke out in the neonatal nursery on the third floor of the Mother and Child Healthcare Centre at the Pims in Islamabad, killing 14 newborn babies.

headline: Pakistani surgeons showcase research at World Olympiad Congress in Mexico
description: MEXICO - The International Society of Aesthetic Plastic Surgeons held its World Olympiad Congress in the beautiful city of Cancun, Mexico, from October 26 to
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: MEXICO - The International Society of Aesthetic Plastic Surgeons held its World Olympiad Congress in the beautiful city of Cancun, Mexico, from October 26 to 31, 2026. Delegates from 102 countries participated in the prestigious event. Three surgeons from Pakistan attended the congress. Dr Afzaal Bashir, an eminent plastic surgeon from King Edward Medical University, Lahore, presented his research on stem cell-based craft work in facial aesthetics. Meanwhile, Dr Ch Salman and Dr Sunaina from Punjab Rangers Teaching Hospital, Lahore, presented their work on the effects of digitalisation on postgraduate residents. Dr Afzaal represented as National Secretary from Pakistan and attended the membership executive committee meeting.

headline: Pregnant woman allegedly shot dead by brother over inheritance dispute
description: MUZAFFARGARH - An eight-month pregnant woman was allegedly shot dead by her brother over a dispute involving inherited land in Jatoi tehsil of
author: Khurram Malaizai
article_text:
MUZAFFARGARH - An eight-month pregnant woman was allegedly shot dead by her brother over a dispute involving inherited land in Jatoi tehsil of Muzaffargarh district, police said. The victim was identified as Mumtaz Mai. A case has been registered at Jatoi police station on the complaint of her mother-in-law.

According to the first information report (FIR), the suspect, identified as Shahid, allegedly wanted his sister to transfer four kanals and 17 marlas of inherited land in his name. When she refused, he allegedly opened fire on her, killing her on the spot. The FIR stated that the victim had returned home after purchasing a cold drink from a shop for her brother when the suspect allegedly approached her from behind and shot her. The eight-month pregnant woman died at the scene. Her husband is reportedly residing in Saudi Arabia. Police have registered a case and launched an investigation into the incident. Further legal action is under way.

headline: China, Indonesia conclude joint army counter-terrorism training
description: BEIJING - China and Indonesia completed their “Sharp Knife 2026” joint army counter-terrorism training with a ceremony in Guangzhou, south
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
BEIJING - China and Indonesia completed their “Sharp Knife 2026” joint army counter-terrorism training with a ceremony in Guangzhou, south China’s Guangdong province, on Monday. This joint training session, which began on Oct 27, was a planned military exchange between the two militaries for 2026, aimed at improving their combat-oriented training capabilities. During the training, troos from the two countries were organised into mixed groups and jointly completed specialised sub-training, tactical coordination and comprehensive drills. As part of the comprehensive drills, the troops worked closely together in key exercises including land- and water-based rescue and coordinated clearance operations. The training also featured thematic seminars, weapon and equipment displays, sports competitions and cultural exchanges. At the ceremony, joint training guidance groups from both sides delivered speeches and presented certificates to outstanding participants.

As the third edition of the Sharp Knife joint training series between the two countries’ armies, the latest exercise is expected to further strengthen traditional friendship and military exchanges and cooperation between China and Indonesia, as well as contribute to regional peace and stability.

headline: Local cement despatches up by 1.17pc in October
description: ISLAMABAD - Local cement despatches by the industry during the month of October were 4.041 million tons compared to 3.994 million tons in October 2025, showing
author: Imran Ali Kundi
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Local cement despatches by the industry during the month of October were 4.041 million tons compared to 3.994 million tons in October 2025, showing an increase of 1.17 percent. According to the data released by All Pakistan Cement Manufacturers Association, export despatches declined by 3.67% to 768,754 tons compared to 798,019 tons in October 2025. Total cement despatches during October 2026 were 4.810 million tons against 4.792 million tons despatched during the same month of last fiscal year, showing an increase of 0.37%. In Oct-26, total despatches by north based cement mills were 3.397 million tons cement, showing a decline of 3.13% against 3.507 million tons despatches in Oct-25. South based mills despatched 1.41 million tons cement during Oct-26 that was 9.90% more compared to the despatches of 1.29 million tons during Oct-25. Against the domestic despatches of 3.393 million tons in Oct-25, north based cement mills despatched 3.397 million tons cement in domestic markets in Oct-26, showing an increase of 0.13%. South based mills despatched 643,816 tons cement in local markets during Oct-26 that was 7.05% more compared to the despatches of 601,401 tons during Oct-25. Compared to the exports of 114,082 tons in Oct-25, there were no exports from north based mills in Oct-26. Exports from south increased by 12.40% to 768,754 tons in Oct-26 from 683,937 tons during the same month last year. During the first four months of current fiscal year, total cement despatches (domestic and exports) were 17.953 million tons that are 2.93% higher than 17.442 million tons despatched during the corresponding period of last fiscal year.

Domestic despatches during this period were 14.889 million tons against 14.055 million tons during same period last year, showing an increase of 5.93%. Export despatches were 9.51% less as the volumes reduced to 3.064 million tons during the first four months of current fiscal year compared to 3.387 million tons exports done during same period of last fiscal year. North based mills despatched 12.344 million tons cement domestically during the first four months of current fiscal year, showing an increase of 4.87% than cement despatches of 11.770 million tons during Jul-25 to Oct-25. There were no exports from north during Jul-26 to Oct-26 compared with 775,948 tons exported during the same period last year. Total despatches by north based mills reduced by 1.61% to 12.344 million tons during first four months of current financial year from 12.546 million tons during same period of last financial year. Domestic despatches by south based mills during Jul-26 to Oct-26 were 2.545 million tons, showing an increase of 11.36% over 2.285 million tons cement despatched during the same period of last fiscal year. Exports from south also increased by 17.38% to 3.064 million tons during Jul-26 to Oct-26 compared with 2.611 million tons exported during the same period last year. Total despatches by south based mills increased by 14.57% to 5.610 million tons during first four months of current financial year from 4.896 million tons during same period of last financial year.

headline: NA panel expresses concerns over persistent poor quality of internet services
description: ISLAMABAD - The National Assembly Standing Committee on Information Technology and Telecommunication Tuesday expressed serious concerns over the persistent
author: Tahir Niaz
article_text: ISLAMABAD - The National Assembly Standing Committee on Information Technology and Telecommunication Tuesday expressed serious concerns over the persistent poor quality of internet services across the country. It observed that despite the Committee’s continuous efforts over the past two years to address the issue, the quality of services have not improved to the required standard. The Committee noted that internet services remained unsatisfactory in several districts. Even major cities including Karachi and Islamabad were facing issues regarding internet connectivity and service quality, it observed. The Committee particularly highlighted frequent signal drops during WhatsApp calls and observed that internet services in smaller cities and remote districts were, in certain areas, almost negligible. The meeting of the Standing Committee on Information Technology and Telecommunication was held under the Chairmanship of Syed Amin ul Haq, MNA at the Parliament House, Islamabad. In response to the committee concerns, the Chairman, Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA), informed the Committee that the Authority had identified the issues through surveys conducted across different areas and had also taken telecom operators on board to address deficiencies in service quality. He explained that wherever shortcomings were identified, the concerned telecom operators were directed to improve their Quality of Service within a period of three months. In cases where no improvement was observed during subsequent surveys, show-cause notices were issued to the respective operators. The Chairman PTA further informed the Committee that five show-cause notices had been issued to telecom operators during the preceding three months. However, recovery of the imposed amounts remained pending, as the concerned operators had approached the courts and obtained stay orders, resulting in delays in the recovery process. The Chairman PTA also highlighted prolonged power outages as one of the major factors affecting the quality of telecommunication services in the country. He stated that load-shedding in rural areas, particularly where electricity remained unavailable for 12 to 16 hours a day, adversely affected the functioning of telecom towers, consequently disrupting internet connectivity for the general public. Regarding the improvement of telecommunication infrastructure, the Chairman PTA informed the Committee that following the 5G spectrum auction, progress had been made towards upgrading the existing network infrastructure. He stated that approximately 70 percent of the 5G services in Karachi had been rolled out, while around 2,300 telecom towers had been upgraded to support 5G technology. He further explained that infrastructure development and resolution of spectrum-related issues were being undertaken progressively, and expressed confidence that these measures would contribute to significant improvements in the overall Quality of Service in the country in the long run. The Committee took up the Electronic Transactions Amendment Bill, 2026, for consideration. The representative of the Ministry of Law and Justice informed the Committee that consultations and collaboration with the Pakistan Peoples’ Party (PPP) regarding the proposed legislation were underway and that the Bill had reached an advanced stage, with consensus on the proposed amendments expected to be finalized shortly. The representative requested the Committee to defer consideration of the Bill until the ongoing consultation process was completed, assuring that the proposed amendments, finalized through consensus, would subsequently be presented before the Committee for consideration and further directions regarding its passage. In view of the request made by the Ministry of Law and Justice, the Committee agreed to defer the Bill for consideration in its next meeting.

headline: Shabbar Zaidi calls for independent commission on KE amid Discos privatisation push
description: LAHORE - Former Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) chairman and noted economist Shabbar Zaidi has called for the formation of an independent commission to
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
LAHORE - Former Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) chairman and noted economist Shabbar Zaidi has called for the formation of an independent commission to examine the challenges facing K-Electric, warning that the experience of Pakistan’s only privatised power utility carries important lessons for the government’s plan to privatise electricity distribution companies (DISCOs).

In a post on X, Zaidi said KE was the country’s only privatised energy company and had seen around $720 million in foreign investment but argued that the investment had generated no return for investors so far. Referring to the recent tariff-related developments, he questioned whether Karachi could remain economically sustainable under such circumstances. He termed the matter a “national issue” and proposed an independent commission to review it.

Zaidi’s comments come as the government moves ahead with plans to privatise Islamabad Electric Supply Company (IESCO), Gujranwala Electric Power Company (GEPCO) and Faisalabad Electric Supply Company (FESCO), for which expressions of interest have been received from local and international investors. KE’s MYT has also invited criticism from various quarters who argue that regulatory uncertainty surrounding the utility could influence investor perceptions of Pakistan’s wider power-sector privatisation programme.

The debate has intensified following the September 23 decision of the NEPRA Appellate Tribunal, which dismissed KE’s appeals against NEPRA’s October 2025 review decisions while allowing appeals filed by the federal government and CPPA-G. NEPRA subsequently notified the revised decisions. Although the Sindh High Court has suspended the decision and the related tariff notifications issued under it, the prolonged regulatory uncertainty appears to be taking an increasing toll on Karachi.

Under the revised Multi-Year Tariff framework, KE’s return on equity was reduced to around 14-15% from 24-30%, while dollar-linked returns were replaced with rupee-based returns and distribution-loss targets were tightened. KE has maintained that the revised framework is financially unsustainable and could affect its ability to finance future investments and maintain service reliability.

The company’s background material estimates that the tariff changes could result in lost investment, delay planned expenditure and affect a proposed addition of roughly 2,200MW of generation capacity, including 1,100MW of renewable energy. It also points to the withdrawal of Shanghai Electric Power’s $1.77 billion proposed acquisition of a controlling stake in KE in September 2025 as an example of the risks prolonged regulatory uncertainty can pose to foreign investment. Against the backdrop of the government’s wider DISCOs privatisation programme, Zaidi’s intervention has therefore added to the debate over whether Pakistan can attract long-term private capital into electricity distribution without a predictable and commercially sustainable regulatory framework.

headline: Chinese scientist Fu Bojie wins 2026 Volvo Environment Prize for pioneering ecological restoration research
description: HELSINKI - Chinese scientist Fu Bojie was awarded the 2026 Volvo Environment Prize in Stockholm, Sweden, on Monday for his outstanding contributions to
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: HELSINKI - Chinese scientist Fu Bojie was awarded the 2026 Volvo Environment Prize in Stockholm, Sweden, on Monday for his outstanding contributions to ecological restoration and sustainability research, particularly his work in improving the ecological environment of China’s Loess Plateau. Fu, an academician of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) and a researcher at its Research Centre for Eco-Environmental Sciences, was recognised for his pioneering contributions to social-ecological systems and sustainability science. The prize jury said Fu’s decades of work on the Loess Plateau and other dryland regions in China has offered valuable lessons for areas worldwide facing land degradation, water scarcity and food insecurity. Speaking to Xinhua after receiving the award, Fu said he felt deeply honored, describing the prize as recognition of Chinese scientists’ achievements in ecological restoration and sustainability research, as well as China’s progress in environmental protection and restoration. He attributed the achievement to nearly three decades of environmental conservation efforts in China and long-term research support from the CAS, the National Natural Science Foundation of China and the Ministry of Science and Technology. “The work on the Loess Plateau was not mine alone. It was the result of sustained efforts by my team members and generations of students who have worked there over the years,” Fu said. According to a press release issued by the Volvo Environment Prize Foundation, decades of large-scale ecological restoration have significantly improved vegetation cover across the Loess Plateau.

headline: All 69 victims of Spain’s deadly train crash identified
description: ASTANA - All 69 victims of last week’s deadly high-speed train collision in Urda, central Spain, have been identified, while 29 injured people remain
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: ASTANA - All 69 victims of last week’s deadly high-speed train collision in Urda, central Spain, have been identified, while 29 injured people remain hospitalised, authorities said Monday. Spain’s Integrated Data Centre (CID) confirmed that the provisional death toll remains at 69, including 54 Spanish nationals and 15 foreigners. The victims, all adults, included 40 men and 29 women. The foreign victims included four Americans, two Australians, two Japanese and one each from Argentina, Canada, the Czech Republic, France, Mexico, Portugal and Tunisia. The Institute of Legal Medicine and Forensic Sciences of Toledo and Ciudad Real completed the identification process. Of the 69 victims, 56 were identified through fingerprint analysis conducted by the Civil Guard’s Criminalistics Service, while the remaining 13 were identified through DNA testing by the National Institute of Toxicology. The families of all 69 victims have been notified of the identification results, while the relevant consular offices have also been informed in cases involving foreign nationals. Meanwhile, the regional government of Castilla-La Mancha reported that 29 people injured in the collision remain hospitalised in four hospitals, including nine in intensive care units and 20 in general wards. Of the 110 patients initially admitted to six hospitals, 81 have been discharged, according to the regional health authorities. Nine patients have been transferred to hospitals in Madrid, including one on Monday, while another has been transferred to Andalusia. According to local media, recovery operations at the accident site have made progress. All carriages of the two trains involved in the collision, operated by Iryo and Spain’s national railway operator Renfe, have now been removed from the tracks. The Civil Guard continues to search the accident site for human remains, with around 50 officers deployed in the area. Earlier, it was reported that Spain declared three days of national mourning after the deadly train collision.

headline: Chairman IPO-Pakistan visits ICCBS at Karachi University
description: KARACHI - Chairman of the Intellectual Property Organization (IPO-Pakistan), Dr. Hafiz Aziz ur Rehman visited the International Center for Chemical and
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: KARACHI - Chairman of the Intellectual Property Organization (IPO-Pakistan), Dr. Hafiz Aziz ur Rehman visited the International Center for Chemical and Biological Sciences (ICCBS), University of Karachi, on Tuesday. Chairman, accompanied by Dr. Muhammad Fayyaz, Controller of Patents, and Saima Kanwal, Assistant Controller of Patents, was received by Prof. Dr. Muhammad Raza Shah, Director of ICCBS. IPO-Pakistan, which operates under the Ministry of Commerce, is the national body responsible for the administration, protection, and promotion of intellectual property rights in Pakistan. During the meeting, Dr. Hafiz Aziz ur Rehman and Prof. Dr. Muhammad Raza Shah discussed matters of mutual interest, particularly the registration and protection of patents for scientific inventions and intellectual property rights related to research discoveries. They also discussed ways to promote scientific research and strengthen research infrastructure in higher education institutions. Dr. Aziz ur Rehman appreciated the state-of-the-art research facilities available to students at ICCBS and commended its international standing as a leading center of scientific research. He emphasized the importance of strengthening research infrastructure in universities and other higher education institutions to foster innovation and promote academic excellence in the country. Earlier, Prof. Raza Shah briefed the visiting delegation on the establishment and development of ICCBS and its major scientific contributions. He also highlighted the Centre’s research activities in molecular medicine, drug discovery, forensic science, and natural product chemistry.

headline: Tech giants weaponising digital space to crush right of self-determination, warns Pakistan
description: UNITED NATIONS - In a sharp critique of the global digital landscape, Pakistani has warned that world’s tech giants are systematically weaponising
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: UNITED NATIONS - In a sharp critique of the global digital landscape, Pakistani has warned that world’s tech giants are systematically weaponising emerging technologies, censorship, and digital surveillance to suppress legitimate self-determination struggles and manipulate public opinion. “Internet shutdowns, censorship, digital surveillance and restrictive media laws are employed to suppress legitimate voices, distort realities and delegitimize struggles for fundamental rights and self-determination,” Pakistani delegate Amanat Ali told the UN General Assembly’s Fourth Committee (Special Political and Decolonization) as it began its review of questions relating to information. Against this backdrop, Amanat Ali, press counsellor at the Pakistan Mission to the UN, called for stronger efforts to counter Islamophobia, racism and xenophobia, warning of the broader dangers posed by hate speech and intolerance in an increasingly polarised information environment. In this regard, the Pakistani delegate called for urgent international cooperation to curtail the concentration of power among multinational technology corporations and block the use of restrictive media laws that mask human rights abuses in occupied territories and conflict zones. He emphasised that misinformation, disinformation, and hate speech are no longer just communication failures, but actively weaponised instruments used to polarize societies and destroy public trust, posing a severe threat in conflict zones. Spotlighting the immense, unchecked power of multinational tech corporations, the Pakistani delegate criticised their opaque algorithms and corporate content policies, which systematically control and alter global public discourse without accountability. He explicitly targeted the strategic information blockades enforced by occupying powers. He noted that internet shutdowns, digital surveillance, censorship, and restrictive media laws are systematically deployed to silence dissent, distort ground realities, and delegitimise struggles for fundamental rights and self-determination. While acknowledging AI’s potential to expand knowledge and accelerate development, he warned that its misuse facilitates widespread deception and alters information integrity, making transparent international governance vital. Ali concluded by urging the UN Department of Global Communications (DGC) to prioritise multilingualism by allocating more resources to close the gap between official languages, and to leverage local UN Information Centres to broadcast credible, balanced coverage.

headline: Kayani advises SMEs to take full advantage of EFS
description: ISLAMABAD - Minister of State for Finance and Railways Bilal Azhar Kayani affirmed the government’s commitment to boosting the export sector and
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Minister of State for Finance and Railways Bilal Azhar Kayani affirmed the government’s commitment to boosting the export sector and improving the ease of doing business, urging small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) engaged in exports to take full advantage of the Export Facilitation Scheme (EFS). He made these remarks while chairing a consultative meeting of the Prime Minister’s Committee to Review the Export Facilitation Scheme at the Finance Division.

The meeting was attended by Secretary Commerce, Special Secretaries from Finance and Commerce, senior officials from the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR), alongside representatives of the All Pakistan Textile Mills Association (APTMA), Pakistan Textile Exporters Association (PTEA), and the Sialkot Chamber of Commerce and Industry and prominent exporters via video link. During the session, various proposals were reviewed in detail to streamline the scheme, enhance its efficiency, and align it with evolving trade dynamics. Bilal Azhar Kayani underscored that the prescribed qualification criteria for inclusion in any EFS category would be applied across the board, reiterating that no exemptions would be granted regarding standard operating procedures.

The minister of state directed the relevant authorities to clarify and simplify regulations governing the import of capital goods and manufacturing machinery for exporters. The meeting also conducted an in-depth review of the amendments at cutting export overheads, encouraging local value addition, and stimulating domestic manufacturing. The minister of state for finance reiterated the government’s resolve to review current exporter schemes, ensuring they are tailored to exporters’ needs to deliver optimal outcomes. The meeting concluded with a consensus to sustain active consultations with all stakeholders and trade bodies to drive export growth and accelerate national economic activity.

headline: Clifton police arrest motorcycle lifter, recover stolen bike

author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: KARACHI - Clifton Police Station arrested a suspected motorcycle lifter and recovered a motorcycle from his possession, according to a District South Police spokesperson on Tuesday. The arrested suspect was identified as Shafqat, son of Muhammad Mohsin. A case has been registered against him at Defence Police Station, the spokesperson said. The suspect has been handed over to the investigation wing of the Anti-Vehicle Lifting Cell (AVLC), Clifton, for further legal proceedings and investigation.

headline: SAI calls for lower energy prices, policy stability to protect industry
description: KARACHI - Industrialists of the SITE Industrial Area have called on the government to urgently address high energy costs, policy stability issues as these
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: KARACHI - Industrialists of the SITE Industrial Area have called on the government to urgently address high energy costs, policy stability issues as these factors could threaten industrial operations, investment and Pakistan’s export competitiveness. SAI president Abdul Hadi said immediate and practical measures were needed to lower production costs and restore confidence among local industrialists as well as international business partners. Without meaningful action, businesses would struggle to keep operations going while the outlook for industrial expansion and economic recovery would weaken further, he added . Hadi stressed that affordable and uninterrupted supplies of electricity, gas and water were essential to keep industrial units running and maintain competitiveness in global markets. The SITE Association president called for fundamental reforms in the energy sector to make electricity, gas and water both affordable and reliable for industrial consumers. Hadi also pressed for consistent, long-term industrial and economic policies that remain predictable even after change of the governments. He also urged the establishment of a transparent and predictable tax system that reduces the financial burden on industry, and called for interest rates to be aligned with those of competing regional economies so that businesses can access cheaper financing. Hadi urged policymakers to move beyond announcements and introduce practical steps that address the sector’s underlying challenges. The SITE Association of Industry has asked the government to prioritize these issues in its economic strategy, emphasizing that a stronger industrial base is essential for sustainable economic recovery and improved export performance.

headline: Karachi intensifies anti-polio drive after poliovirus detection
description: KARACHI - Following confirmation of the presence of the poliovirus in Jamali Colony, the Karachi administration and the Emergency Operations Centre (EOC) have
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: KARACHI - Following confirmation of the presence of the poliovirus in Jamali Colony, the Karachi administration and the Emergency Operations Centre (EOC) have decided to further strengthen the anti-polio campaign to prevent the spread of the virus and ensure its complete eradication from the city. Commissioner Karachi Syed Hassan Naqvi has directed the relevant departments to adopt a comprehensive strategy, with particular focus on low-coverage areas, informal settlements, shanty towns and underserved communities. The Commissioner on Tuesday visited Union Council 18, Jamali Colony, along with Deputy Commissioner East Nasrullah Abbasi, Karachi Polio Task Force Coordinator Saud Yaqub, town administration officials, Union Council Chairman and elected representatives of the area. He also chaired a review meeting to assess the anti-polio campaign’s planning, vaccination coverage and measures being taken to prevent the spread of the virus. The Commissioner said that all relevant departments needed to intensify their efforts and work with greater commitment to make the anti-polio campaign successful. He was given a detailed briefing on the arrangements for the campaign. It was informed that the current anti-polio drive, which commenced on November 2, would continue until November 8. During the campaign, 2.16 million children under the age of five will be administered polio vaccine drops. Special security arrangements have been made to ensure the smooth and successful implementation of the campaign, with more than 23,000 polio workers performing their duties across the city. The Commissioner emphasized the need for coordinated efforts, driven by a strong national commitment, to ensure effective implementation of the campaign and prevent further transmission of the virus. During the meeting, Deputy Commissioner East Nasrullah Abbasi briefed the Commissioner on the challenges being faced during the anti-polio campaign, sensitive locations and obstacles affecting vaccination coverage in the area. Particular attention was drawn to the difficulties of reaching children in informal settlements, shanty towns and underprivileged communities, as well as the measures being taken to address these challenges. Deputy Commissioner East Nasrullah Abbasi informed the Commissioner that a comprehensive plan had been prepared to ensure that all children under five years of age in Jamali Colony received polio drops. The administration was seeking the support of respected community members and influential local opinion leaders. Parents of all children had been contacted, and they were extending their cooperation. The Commissioner Karachi was given a detailed briefing on the anti-polio campaign and its implementation plan in Union Council 18, Jamali Colony. The briefing included an assessment of vaccination arrangements, campaign targets and progress in reaching children across the area. It was informed that Jamali Colony has a total population of 62,647, with a household vaccination target of 5,284, a school target of 1,616 children and a transit target of 232 children. Special planning and arrangements have been made to prevent the spread of the poliovirus in Jamali Colony and ensure its eventual eradication. The Commissioner was also briefed on the performance of the campaign launched on November 2. On the first day, the vaccination target was 1,022 children. However, polio teams managed to reach or contact 1,061 children, of whom 846 were administered polio drops through coordinated field efforts. This represented approximately 83 per cent achievement against the day’s target, reflecting encouraging progress. The Commissioner was informed that three vaccinators were deployed in the area. For vaccination coverage, the Union Council has two Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI) fixed sites and two outreach (OR) sites. Jamali Colony also has three identified slum or informal settlement areas. The meeting reviewed, in detail, the measures being undertaken at the Union Council level to eradicate polio, vaccination coverage among children and the performance of field teams, with the objective of ensuring 100 per cent coverage. Meanwhile, Karachi Polio Task Force Coordinator Saud Yaqub briefed Commissioner Karachi on the first day’s vaccination targets and coverage under the ongoing campaign. The Commissioner was informed that, out of approximately 2.1 million children under the age of five in Karachi Division, 20 per cent coverage had been achieved on the first day of the campaign. Against a target of 425,682 households, vaccination teams successfully reached 84 per cent of households. Commissioner Naqvi stressed that priority measures to prevent the spread of the poliovirus must be undertaken in close collaboration with local communities. He directed the relevant authorities to ensure vaccination of children whose parents had previously refused to cooperate and to maintain close monitoring of population movements and migration within Karachi. He emphasised that special efforts must be made to ensure that children of both refusing families and families on the move were not missed during vaccination campaigns. The Commissioner also directed officials to include informal settlements located within or adjacent to affluent residential neighbourhoods in campaign planning. Such settlements are often overlooked during administrative surveys and vaccination activities. He personally identified some of these locations and instructed the relevant officers to ensure that no settlement or child was left out of the vaccination drive. On the occasion, Saud Yaqub informed the meeting that although the overall vaccination coverage in Karachi had improved. He stressed the need to identify these areas and ensure vaccination through targeted strategies and focused interventions.

headline: Sindh launches ‘Herd Transformation Initiative’ to revolutionise livestock genetics
description: KARACHI - In a landmark move to bolster the province’s dairy and meat production, the Sindh Livestock and Fisheries Department, in collaboration with
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: KARACHI - In a landmark move to bolster the province’s dairy and meat production, the Sindh Livestock and Fisheries Department, in collaboration with FonGrow (an organisation of Fauji Fertilisers), has successfully launched the ‘Herd Transformation Initiative.’ The initiative reached a critical milestone on November 2, 2026, with the first successful batch of embryo transfers carried out at the Sindh Institute of Animal Science in Karachi. The project represents a paradigm shift in livestock management, utilising advanced genetic technology to rapidly improve local breeds. Rapid genetic improvement Briefing Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah, Minister for Livestock and Fisheries Mohammad Ali Malkani highlighted that the initiative will drastically accelerate the genetic improvement of local cattle. Traditionally, herd transformation takes approximately 30 years; however, this new technology is expected to achieve the same results in just five years. The strong demand for the programme was evident, with the Livestock Department ordering 132 embryos of Red Sindhi and Guzerata breeds, while private farmers have already placed orders for an additional 90 embryos. Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah congratulated the Livestock Department, its secretary Kazim Jatoi, Sindh Institute of Animal Science team, FonGrow team and the entire project team on this achievement. He emphasised that the success of the embryo transfer process is a significant step toward meeting the growing milk and meat demands of Pakistan’s population and will provide a substantial boost to the livelihoods of local farmers. The Chief Minister urged the department to scale up the initiative across the province to ensure that the benefits of high-yield genetics reach the grassroots level, ultimately enhancing food security in the region.
