headline: UCP seeks stronger academic links with Turkish universities
description: LAHORE - The University of Central Punjab (UCP) celebrated the 103rd Republic Day of Turkiye with a special ceremony held here on Tuesday. The ceremony
author: STAFF REPORT
article_text:
LAHORE - The University of Central Punjab (UCP) celebrated the 103rd Republic Day of Turkiye with a special ceremony held here on Tuesday. The ceremony highlighted the historic friendship between Pakistan and Turkiye and exploring new avenues of academic cooperation between the two countries.Turkish Consul General in Lahore Mehmet Emin Shamshek, accompanied by his wife, attended the ceremony as chief guest. Dean Professor Dr Khalid Manzoor Butt, Pro-Rector Professor Dr Hammad Naveed, Group Head of Punjab Group of Colleges Khadija Amir and other distinguished guests were also present. The university campus was decorated with the national flags of Pakistan and Turkiye, while students warmly welcomed the guests with bouquets. In his welcome address, Professor Dr Khalid Manzoor Butt highlighted the historic, cultural and brotherly ties between Pakistan and Turkiye, saying that the friendship between the two countries was founded on mutual trust and shared values.

He also underscored the importance of defence cooperation among Türkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan. Students presented regional dances and traditional songs reflecting Pakistani culture, which were appreciated by the chief guest. The Turkish Consul General thanked the UCP administration for celebrating Turkiye’s national day with enthusiasm and warmth. In his remarks, Pro-Rector Professor Dr Hammad Naveed thanked the Consul General and his wife for attending the ceremony and presented them with commemorative shields and traditional handicrafts. Later, delegations from UCP and the Turkish Consulate discussed opportunities for joint degree programmes, student and faculty exchanges, research collaboration and enhanced academic ties. The Turkish Consul General assured his cooperation in strengthening institutional linkages between UCP and Turkish universities.

headline: Ombudsman secures Rs216m relief for 269 citizens in three months
description: OUR STAFF RE - The Office of the Ombudsman Punjab on Tuesday secured the release of outstanding dues worth Rs.216.10 million to 269 citizens across the
author: STAFF REPORT
article_text: OUR STAFF RE - The Office of the Ombudsman Punjab on Tuesday secured the release of outstanding dues worth Rs.216.10 million to 269 citizens across the province in three months through timely intervention,providing them financial relief. The citizens had approached the Ombudsman Punjab after facing delays or refusal by government departments to pay their legitimate dues. Acting on their complaints,the Ombudsman Punjab directed the relevant departments to release the outstanding amounts. According to a spokesperson,80 citizens received Rs.89.459 million as financial assistance while Rs.26.739 million was paid to 30 citizens against contractual dues. Similarly,16 citizens received Rs.37 million in pension benefits while eight were paid Rs.2.915 million as family pension. Moreover,40 citizens received Rs10.955 million as marriage grants while 10 were paid Rs.5.798 million as death grants. An amount of Rs.5.219 million was released to 23 citizens under the General Provident Fund (GP Fund) while 55 citizens received Rs.36.758 million in outstanding salaries. The payments also included Rs.239,400 in property tax refunds to three citizens and Rs.113,400 in farewell grants to two citizens. Additionally, one citizen received Rs.923,000 in group insurance, while another was paid Rs.750,000 as gratuity. The complainants appreciated the Ombudsman Punjab’s intervention, saying it helped them secure their legitimate dues and resolve their grievances.

headline: Punjab launches ‘Chamkta Lahore’ campaign to combat smog
description: LAHORE - On the direction of Chief Minister(CM), Maryam Nawaz Sharif, the provincial government on Tuesday launched a cleanliness and anti-smog drive
author: Staff Reporter
article_text: LAHORE - On the direction of Chief Minister(CM), Maryam Nawaz Sharif, the provincial government on Tuesday launched a cleanliness and anti-smog drive “Chamkta Lahore’’ aimed at improving sanitation, reducing airborne dust and ensuring cleaner roads and public spaces across the provincial capital. Minister for Local Government, Zeeshan Rafique inaugurated the campaign at a ceremony held at Liberty Chowk. Special Assistant to the CM Shoaib Mirza, Deputy Commissioner (DC), Ali Ijaz and the Chief Executive Officer(CEO) of the Lahore Waste Management Company (LWMC) were also present. Zeeshan Rafique and Shoaib Mirza operated anti-smog mist guns and reviewed their functioning. Speaking to the media, Zeeshan Rafique said the initiative had been launched under the chief minister’s vision of a clean Punjab. He said anti-smog measures introduced by the provincial government over the past two years had produced encouraging results, adding that smog levels in November were noticeably lower than those recorded two years ago. He said the provision of 10 anti-smog mist guns was a key feature of the “Chamkta Lahore” campaign. Mounted on rickshaws, these cost-effective machines would spray water into the air to suppress dust particles and complement the city’s road-washing operations. The minister said the campaign would focus on ensuring comprehensive cleanliness along major roads, busy thoroughfares and commercial areas. Initially,100 major roads, locations and commercial markets have been identified for targeted cleaning operations, he added. Under the campaign, approximately 648 kilometers of roads will be washed every week, with a daily target of 100 kilometers. Sixteen mechanical washing machines will be deployed for road cleaning while 46 rickshaw-mounted washers will be used to clean footpaths. Zeeshan Rafique expressed confidence that the initiative would make Lahore cleaner and contribute to efforts to combat smog and improve air quality. Highlighting the provincial government’s development initiatives,he said Punjab was making progress under the leadership of Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz. He pointed to ongoing projects in road infrastructure, healthcare, education and urban beautification, saying development activities were being carried out from major cities to union councils across the province. He added that the government’s public welfare initiatives and development projects were aimed at improving people’s quality of life. Special Assistant to CM Shoaib Mirza praised the efforts of sanitation workers, describing them as heroes whose hard work was instrumental in maintaining cleanliness. He said the chief minister’s initiative would be extended to all districts to ensure its benefits reached people across the province. content_blocks.text: LAHORE - On the direction of Chief Minister(CM), Maryam Nawaz Sharif, the provincial government on Tuesday launched a cleanliness and anti-smog drive “Chamkta Lahore’’ aimed at improving sanitation, reducing airborne dust and ensuring cleaner roads and public spaces across the provincial capital. Minister for Local Government, Zeeshan Rafique inaugurated the campaign at a ceremony held at Liberty Chowk. Special Assistant to the CM Shoaib Mirza, Deputy Commissioner (DC), Ali Ijaz and the Chief Executive Officer(CEO) of the Lahore Waste Management Company (LWMC) were also present. Zeeshan Rafique and Shoaib Mirza operated anti-smog mist guns and reviewed their functioning. Speaking to the media, Zeeshan Rafique said the initiative had been launched under the chief minister’s vision of a clean Punjab. He said anti-smog measures introduced by the provincial government over the past two years had produced encouraging results, adding that smog levels in November were noticeably lower than those recorded two years ago. He said the provision of 10 anti-smog mist guns was a key feature of the “Chamkta Lahore” campaign. Mounted on rickshaws, these cost-effective machines would spray water into the air to suppress dust particles and complement the city’s road-washing operations. The minister said the campaign would focus on ensuring comprehensive cleanliness along major roads, busy thoroughfares and commercial areas. Initially,100 major roads, locations and commercial markets have been identified for targeted cleaning operations, he added. Under the campaign, approximately 648 kilometers of roads will be washed every week, with a daily target of 100 kilometers. Sixteen mechanical washing machines will be deployed for road cleaning while 46 rickshaw-mounted washers will be used to clean footpaths. Zeeshan Rafique expressed confidence that the initiative would make Lahore cleaner and contribute to efforts to combat smog and improve air quality. Highlighting the provincial government’s development initiatives,he said Punjab was making progress under the leadership of Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz. He pointed to ongoing projects in road infrastructure, healthcare, education and urban beautification, saying development activities were being carried out from major cities to union councils across the province. headline: Over 456,000 children administered polio drops on first day
description: LAHORE - More than 456,000 children were administered polio vaccine on the first day of the ongoing anti-polio campaign in Lahore, while vaccination teams
author: STAFF REPORT
article_text:
LAHORE - More than 456,000 children were administered polio vaccine on the first day of the ongoing anti-polio campaign in Lahore, while vaccination teams reached 295,151 households across the city. The progress of the campaign was reviewed at a meeting chaired by Deputy Commissioner Lahore Muhammad Ali Ijaz, who directed the relevant departments to ensure 100 per cent coverage and effectively address all missed and refusal cases. Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Health Dr Asif Arbab Khan briefed the meeting on the campaign’s first-day performance. Additional Deputy Commissioner (Municipal Services), assistant commissioners and Union Council Medical Officers (UCMOs) also attended the meeting. He also instructed the teams to address parents’ concerns through effective communication and complete vaccination of all eligible children. Emphasising the importance of maintaining the cold chain, he directed the health authorities to ensure proper storage and handling of polio vaccines throughout the campaign.

DC Muhammad Ali Ijaz said polio eradication was a national responsibility and, in line with the vision of Chief Minister Punjab Maryam Nawaz Sharif, all-out efforts would be made to ensure a polio-free Punjab. He said there was no room for negligence in the anti-polio campaign and directed the officials to adopt an effective strategy to cover refusal cases. He also urged parents to cooperate with vaccination teams and ensure that their children received polio drops.

headline: Faryal Talpur to visit Lahore ahead of LG elections
description: LAHORE - Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Women’s Wing Central President Faryal Talpur is expected to visit Lahore on November 10 or 11 for approximately a
author: STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Women’s Wing Central President Faryal Talpur is expected to visit Lahore on November 10 or 11 for approximately a week as the party intensifies preparations for the upcoming local government elections in Punjab. The PPP Lahore has planned a grand reception for Ms Talpur, with party leaders, office-bearers and workers expected to participate in welcoming her, according to a press release issued on Tuesday. PPP Lahore President Faisal Mir and nominated Secretary Information Majid Ghori said the visit would mark a new phase in the party’s organisational and political activities in Punjab. They said Ms Talpur would be briefed on preparations for the local government elections, candidate selection, organisational matters and the party’s electoral strategy. The briefing would also cover the performance of local party organisations, electoral preparations in Lahore and other districts, and the status of prospective candidates. Meetings with party ticket holders, prospective candidates and workers intending to contest the local government elections would also be part of her visit. The PPP leaders said the visit aimed to strengthen the party at the grassroots level and mobilise its workers for an effective electoral campaign across Punjab. They added that the party leadership and workers would jointly formulate a comprehensive strategy to enhance the PPP’s political presence in Lahore and other districts, with a focus on public outreach and organisational mobilisation. The PPP has vowed to actively participate in the upcoming local government elections and strengthen its organisation across the province, the press release said.

headline: Punjab CM Maryam inaugurates development projects in Attock
description: LAHORE - Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif inaugurated 127 development projects in Attock, including 59 road construction and rehabilitation schemes
author: STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif inaugurated 127 development projects in Attock, including 59 road construction and rehabilitation schemes worth Rs 23 billion, during her visit to the district on Tuesday. The inaugurated projects also included an Agri Mall, Land Record Centre, Model Children’s Home and Fateh Jang Special Education Centre, said a handout issued here. The 59 road schemes included Fateh Jang–Pindi Gheb Road, Dhok Lahm Jhamat Road and Mithial Chowk–Dhok Pathan Road, besides several other roads. The chief minister received a warm welcome upon her arrival as a large number of people, party workers and children gathered along roads and streets to greet her. Flowers were showered along various routes and intersections, while her vehicle was covered with rose petals along Hattian Road, Kamra Road and University Road. Separately, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif distributed laptops and Honhaar scholarships among students at a ceremony held at COMSATS University, Attock, on Tuesday, with students from Swabi, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, also benefiting from the education support initiatives. Students from KP appreciated the Punjab government for extending the scholarship programme beyond provincial boundaries, saying the financial assistance had enabled them to pay semester fees amounting to nearly Rs200,000, said a handout issued here. At the ceremony, the chief minister distributed laptops and scholarship cheques among students. She was also presented with portraits and sketches prepared by students. A total of 6,161 laptops were distributed among students across the Rawalpindi division. These included 628 laptops for public university students, 257 for private university students, 461 for medical colleges, 375 for nursing colleges, 17 for special education institutions and 423 for colleges under the Higher Education Department. Under the Honhaar Scholarship Programme, 2,590 scholarships worth Rs196.97 million were awarded to students in the Rawalpindi division. Of these, 2,085 scholarships worth Rs170.21 million were allocated to students of public universities, while 314 scholarships worth Rs19.8 million went to students of medical universities and colleges. Another 191 scholarships worth Rs6.96 million were awarded to students of HED colleges. The programme covers students enrolled in public and private universities, federally chartered universities, BS colleges, special education institutions, and medical and dental colleges. The chief minister has increased the number of laptops allocated for deserving students from 40,000 to 112,000. So far, 48,292 laptops have been distributed among students in different districts of Punjab. Under the first three phases of the Honhaar Scholarship Programme, 108,000 students have received scholarships. The ceremony was attended by elected representatives, party ticket-holders and other political leaders, whom the chief minister also met on the occasion.

The chief minister received a warm welcome upon her arrival as a large number of people, party workers and children gathered along roads and streets to greet her. Flowers were showered along various routes and intersections, while her vehicle was covered with rose petals along Hattian Road, Kamra Road and University Road. Separately, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif distributed laptops and Honhaar scholarships among students at a ceremony held at COMSATS University, Attock, on Tuesday, with students from Swabi, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, also benefiting from the education support initiatives. Students from KP appreciated the Punjab government for extending the scholarship programme beyond provincial boundaries, saying the financial assistance had enabled them to pay semester fees amounting to nearly Rs200,000, said a handout issued here. Under the Honhaar Scholarship Programme, 2,590 scholarships worth Rs196.97 million were awarded to students in the Rawalpindi division. Of these, 2,085 scholarships worth Rs170.21 million were allocated to students of public universities, while 314 scholarships worth Rs19.8 million went to students of medical universities and colleges. The programme covers students enrolled in public and private universities, federally chartered universities, BS colleges, special education institutions, and medical and dental colleges. The chief minister has increased the number of laptops allocated for deserving students from 40,000 to 112,000. So far, 48,292 laptops have been distributed among students in different districts of Punjab. Under the first three phases of the Honhaar Scholarship Programme, 108,000 students have received scholarships. The ceremony was attended by elected representatives, party ticket-holders and other political leaders, whom the chief minister also met on the occasion.

headline: 225,000 loans disbursed under Apni Chhat, Apna Ghar scheme
description: LAHORE - More than 128,000 houses have been completed under Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif’s Apni Chhat, Apna Ghar programme with the
author: STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - More than 128,000 houses have been completed under Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif’s Apni Chhat, Apna Ghar programme with the government recovering 97.6 percent of loan instalments amounting to Rs22.29 billion, according to a handout. A special meeting chaired by the chief minister reviewed progress on the housing initiative, which has attracted more than 1.7 million registrations since its launch. The meeting was informed that over 225,000 loans had been disbursed under the scheme, while 128,718 houses had been completed. Another 62,600 houses were nearing completion, and 171,597 beneficiaries had received the second instalment of their loans. The briefing highlighted a loan recovery rate of 97.6 per cent, with Rs22.29 billion recovered in instalments from beneficiaries. Maryam Nawaz approved inviting fresh applications for the Apni Chhat, Apna Ghar scheme and directed the authorities to ensure timely achievement of its completion targets. The meeting was also briefed on the Apni Chhat, Mehfooz Chhat initiative, for which the application process has been completed. Under the programme, 3,055 applicants have received loans worth Rs1.216 billion, while construction and expansion work on 532 houses has been completed. The chief minister directed the relevant authorities to ensure that all targets under the housing initiatives were achieved within the stipulated timelines.
